reviews.summary:
H002 whole-contract review: `nerva chat -z` preserves final-answer-only stdout, bounded piped/file/argument input, nonzero refusal/failure/usage/auth/unreachable/interrupt exits, confirmed versus requested session attribution, and an atomic nerva.chat.usage.v1 receipt on ordinary success and failure paths. It never approves a queued action; pending IDs remain queued and force an incomplete result. Interactive output/exit compatibility remains while its optional receipt can report incomplete.

The hub supplies request-owned bounded generation usage on JSON chat replies and SSE end events. Accepted owned generation dispatch attempts are observed after quota, physical data-handling and host/protocol checks. Retries, specialists, synchronous response-driving auxiliary generation, streaming and synthesis are included; control probes, embeddings/audio and explicitly detached title/review/cache jobs are excluded. Task-owned pending attempts prevent cross-task usage attribution; nested scopes preserve provenance, inactive inherited scopes cannot authenticate a model, unknown POSTs during generation make totals unknown, and closed/bounded collectors reject late or overflowing observations. Tokens require complete valid provider counters for every attempt; failed/partial retries cannot hide behind later success. Local zero needs positive provider/route/host proof and complete counters. Exact requested models confirmed against the wire can use dated repository estimates; unsupported cache-write premiums, Gemini Pro long-context tiers, unknown models and uncertain provenance stay unpriced. Mixed identities receive a bounded breakdown. The provider field denotes the backend adapter, not an attestation of remote weights or an invoice.

Source-assigned runtime stops survive synthesis independently of prose: settled tool-loop exits, exact thinking exhaustion, terminal agent failures/timeouts, policy/continuation refusal and terminal synthesis errors make one-shot execution incomplete. Stop metadata is finite and bounded; malformed present metadata fails closed. Legacy hubs retain text-fallback limits. Successful deterministic synthesis fallback may still return complete specialist answers; a failed observed attempt keeps its usage unknown. Authorization and early owner/session preflight errors retain their HTTP failure codes and can yield unavailable telemetry while still producing a failure receipt. CLI validators reject malformed, missing, negative, boolean, nonfinite, oversized or inconsistent telemetry without crashing or changing the answer verdict; error objects carry only bounded projected telemetry.

Verification includes real owned HTTP MockTransport calls through actual backend adapters, actual ASGI JSON/SSE, concurrent/nested/late task behavior, runtime-stop to synthesis to HTTP to CLI, malformed receipts, pending approvals, transport failures, real isolated FastAPI lifespan/CLI smoke and the frozen backend milestone with its explicitly recorded outcome. No live-provider, native Windows/device or invoice claim is made. Unrelated Hermes flags, invocation IDs and writing through a symlink are outside the frozen acceptance; the atomic replace behavior is retained. Interrupt review and regressions verify exit 130 before POST and after decoded response/output, preserving observed session, usage, stops and pending IDs; already emitted terminal text cannot be retracted. The full frozen run was not green (32 failed cases); all 32 original nodes pass after fixture/status repairs, and the isolated interrupt fix passes integrated CLI coverage.

reviews.summary:
`nerva config` now has nine actions: list, get, set, unset, check, edit, path, env-path and migrate (agents/cli/nerva.py:268-280 declares the four new ones, the dispatch is agents/cli/nerva.py:1329-1336, and tests/test_nerva_cli.py:105 pins the tree). The first five behave as before: list/get/set/unset take dotted or escaped names that reach into a JSON value, and `check` validates every stored value against its declared schema (agents/cli/nerva.py:1337-1349). Every verb is offline, on the same data root and settings store the hub uses.

`config edit` opens every editable setting in $VISUAL, then $EDITOR, then vi (notepad on Windows) as one `category.key = JSON` file in the `config list` format (agents/cli/nerva.py:1426-1441, agents/cli/nerva.py:1451-1472). The file is created owner-only and deleted afterwards. A secret, a route-only row and an undeclared row are named in a comment and their value is never written to it. After the editor exits 0, only lines whose value differs from the stored one are written. Each goes through the same schema validation and the same guarded write as `config set`: the retention approval, the model-selection guards and the busy-store message (agents/cli/nerva.py:1361-1400, agents/cli/nerva.py:1503-1569). A bad line (not JSON, duplicated, unknown, secret, route-only, schema-refused) is named and the rest is still written, with exit 1. A missing editor, a non-executable editor or a nonzero editor exit writes nothing. Tests: tests/test_nerva_cli.py:569-592 (only changed lines written, temp file removed), tests/test_nerva_cli.py:595-612 (no change, failed editor, $VISUAL over $EDITOR), tests/test_nerva_cli.py:615-630 (partial acceptance with every rejection named), tests/test_nerva_cli.py:633-651 (secrets never shown or written), tests/test_nerva_cli.py:654-659 (route-only), tests/test_nerva_cli.py:662-667 (non-executable editor), tests/test_nerva_cli.py:670-676 (Windows argv).

`config path` prints the profile, its data root and the settings database, with a row count read read-only without creating or seeding anything, and `--json` (agents/cli/nerva.py:1572-1609; tests/test_nerva_cli.py:713-729, including a `-p` profile). `config env-path` lists the repo, data-home and profile `.env` files in the order the hub reads them, whether each is present and read, the `.env.example` and the secret store, and whether dotenv is disabled. It prints names and presence only, never a value (agents/cli/nerva.py:1612-1665; tests/test_nerva_cli.py:732-762).

`config migrate [--dry-run] [--json]` is the "missing or outdated keys" report plus the write. agents/core/settings_migrate.py reads the raw store read-only and plans three kinds of change: a `seed` for each declared setting the store lacks, a `default` for a shipped default a later build changed (applied only while the stored value is still the old default and the change has not already been applied), and a `retired` rewrite of a model id that a vendor retired, on every model setting rather than only the row that shipped it. Skill-switch rows are listed as `kept`, never reseeded (agents/core/settings_migrate.py:134-170). `apply` writes exactly that plan in one transaction, each statement guarded so a value the owner changed since the plan is left alone, records the default markers, and notifies a running hub (agents/core/settings_migrate.py:173-213). The `migrate` verb prints one line per change, writes nothing under `--dry-run`, and with no store says it would create one with all declared settings or creates it (agents/core/settings_migrate.py:216-222; agents/cli/nerva.py:1680-1735). A locked store gives a named retry message, and a file that is not a settings store gives a named failure. Tests: tests/test_settings_db_migrate.py:95-123 (plan names a seed, a changed default and retired ids and writes nothing), tests/test_settings_db_migrate.py:126-133 (owner values left alone), tests/test_settings_db_migrate.py:136-146 (kept switch rows), tests/test_settings_db_migrate.py:152-196 (apply writes exactly the plan, records the marker, works on a store with no migrations table), and tests/test_nerva_cli.py:679-693, tests/test_nerva_cli.py:696-710, tests/test_nerva_cli.py:765-806 and tests/test_nerva_cli.py:809-820 (busy store, rewrite, dry-run then apply then idempotent, create-only-when-applied).

The retired-model table is data and is Anthropic-only. It has four rows, each naming the repo file that records the retirement, and a test checks that file holds the retired id and date (agents/core/settings_migrate.py:58-67; tests/test_settings_db_migrate.py:51-73, tests/test_settings_db_migrate.py:218-220). The model settings it scans are claude_model, default_model, gemini_model, compatible_model and the sub-agent model (agents/core/settings_migrate.py:71-77). Nothing in the repo records a retired xAI, OpenAI, Google or OpenRouter id, so none is listed and none is taken from memory. The mechanism is the same one `hermes migrate xai` is: tests/test_settings_db_migrate.py:199-215 shows that a row supplied for an xAI id rewrites llm.compatible_model and leaves an unlisted id alone. Hermes's own vendor-specific retired-model list is data that Nerva does not carry. `config check` validates stored values against their schema, and the report of missing keys, changed defaults and retired ids is `config migrate --dry-run`. A boot still applies seeds and changed defaults silently, but the retired-model rewrite across every model setting runs only when the owner runs `nerva config migrate`. Nothing here was run against a live provider.

reviews.summary: `nerva doctor` rulează `scripts/doctor.py` fără să schimbe nimic, cu un motiv numit pentru fiecare verificare, `--json` și `--smoke`. Are cinci verificări obligatorii (python, venv, locks_in_sync, bind_is_loopback, data_root_writable) și zece consultative (runtimes, readyz, runtime_resolves, voice din H613, config_sources, model_roles din H277, smoke și, din H501, host_not_root, sshd_no_passwords, container_storage; scripts/doctor.py:129-131). Iese cu 1 doar când pică una obligatorie; o consultativă care pică e `warn`. Din HEQ lot 1 (H242), `runtime_resolves` verifică dacă ruta pe care o ia un turn Jarvis chiar se rezolvă la un model utilizabil, nu doar dacă răspunde un runtime. Citește verdictul strict al hub-ului, blocul `model` din `GET /api/onboarding/command-center` (același select_backend, fără generare), cu un singur credențial local: `JARVIS_USER_TOKEN`, altfel `JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN`, pe care îl trimite doar unui hub de pe această mașină, decis după adresă, nu după ortografie (scripts/doctor.py:542, scripts/doctor.py:589-596). E `ok` doar pe `ready: true` care numește ruta, providerul și modelul. Altfel dă motivul numit (`configured_not_resident`, `route_unselected`, `needs_token`, `malformed_reply` …), iar fără un hub gata e `skip`. `readyz` și această citire folosesc aceeași adresă de hub ca `nerva status` (`NERVA_HUB_URL`, altfel `JARVIS_HOST`/`JARVIS_PORT`; o adresă wildcard e apelată prin loopback). Din H273, `config_sources` arată, informativ, din ce strat vine fiecare cheie de configurare (mediul procesului > `.env`-ul repo-ului > `.env`-ul din data home) și ce valori din `.env` sunt acoperite de un strat de mai sus — doar nume, niciodată o valoare. `nerva status` arată același verdict pe o linie `runnable:`, separat de vechiul `model_state`, afișat acum „resident”. Alte diagnostice sunt verbe separate: `nerva desktop status` (ce îi lipsește host-ului pentru operatorul desktop), `nerva security audit` (vulnerabilități cunoscute, prin OSV) și `nerva extensions doctor`. Hermes' `debug dump`/`debug share --local` report: version and commit, active model/provider, which API keys and platform tokens are set, non-default config, and redacted log tails. build_bundle (agents/core/support_bundle.py:293) now carries all of it, still allow-listed. `meta` adds the checked-out commit, read from .git without running git (agents/core/support_bundle.py:92). `model` (agents/core/support_bundle.py:196) names the selected backend, the default/Gemini/Claude/compatible model ids, compatible provider, cloud fallback and reasoning effort (agents/core/support_bundle.py:44). It leaves out base URLs. The product posture is read from the hub's runtime settings, or the stored rows offline (agents/core/support_bundle.py:120). Every shown value passes _shown_value (agents/core/support_bundle.py:69), which does not trust a row's declared kind, because a write does not check it. A select value must be one of its declared options. A number or toggle must be one. A model id (the free-text rows at agents/core/support_bundle.py:48) must have a model id's shape (no `@`, so neither `user:pw@host` nor an e-mail passes), no scheme, no JWT prefix and nothing the settings credential scanner flags. Anything else reads `(withheld)`. `credentials` (agents/core/support_bundle.py:210) reports, by variable name only, which provider keys are set: each profile's auth_env, plus the *_API_KEYS pool only for providers that actually pool (provider_probe.POOLED). They go through the HUD log reader and its secret redactor, and e-mail addresses are masked as Hermes masks them. Logs are opt-in (`--logs N`, route `?log_lines=N` at agents/core/routers/support.py:23) rather than default-on. The earlier assessment listed three gaps against Hermes `backup` / `backup --quick` / `import`. All three are closed on this branch:

1. Quick state-only snapshot. create_backup(quick=True) keeps only the state databases (agents/core/backup.py:573-574). The `nerva backup create --quick` verb is defined at agents/cli/nerva.py:329-331, and the module CLI has the same flag (agents/core/backup.py:1737).

2. Restore is no longer limited to the module CLI.
   - The `nerva backup` tree has create, list, verify, restore and cancel (agents/cli/nerva.py:327-349; dispatch in cmd_backup at agents/cli/nerva.py:2222).
   - The admin route POST /api/admin/backup/restore queues a backup.restore card at the irreversible tier and answers 202. It never restores on the request alone (agents/core/routers/backup.py:98-137). DELETE withdraws a staged restore (agents/core/routers/backup.py:160-175).
   - With a hub running, `nerva backup restore` posts to that route (agents/cli/nerva.py:2316). With no hub running, the owner must type RESTORE; the restore is then staged and applied in place (agents/cli/nerva.py:2343-2360).
   - An accepted card is routed to backup.apply_approved (agents/core/autonomy/irreversible.py:45). Only a process that can restart the hub may take it (agents/core/autonomy/irreversible.py:51, agents/core/backup.py:1608-1627).

3. The server no longer has to be stopped by hand.
   - apply_approved stages the restore and asks the hub to restart (agents/core/backup.py:1657-1697).
   - serve.py applies the staged restore at boot, before agents.web opens any store (serve.py:105-123).
   - run_server installs a stopper and then re-execs (POSIX), exits 75 for NSSM, or spawns a successor (interactive Windows) (serve.py:408-418, serve.py:474-501).
   - When the hub has no restart path, it says "manual" everywhere instead of promising a restart (agents/core/routers/backup.py:140-144, agents/core/backup.py:1686-1696).
   - Each restore first takes a rollback snapshot of the matching kind (agents/core/backup.py:1546-1550).

What review round 7 added:
- GET /api/admin/backup now also reports restart, stage_within_seconds and refused_restore (agents/core/routers/backup.py:47-52). The tick comes from a single helper that the coordinator loop also sleeps on (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:153-157, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:572).
- `nerva approvals accept` says at once whether the restore is "NOT applied yet" or will be applied by a self-restart (agents/cli/nerva.py:2027-2042). It then follows for 8 s and reports a stage, an outcome or a refusal (agents/cli/nerva.py:2045-2089).

At HEAD d2ec765, all three gaps in the 2026-10-14 assessment are closed in code.

(1) Dry run. --dry-run is a real CLI path. With it, _main prints plan_uninstall as JSON and removes nothing (agents/core/uninstall.py:730-739). The plan lists every target and whether it exists. It also shows the data root and purge feasibility when --purge-data is given, and the desktop paths when --gui or --gui-only is given (agents/core/uninstall.py:377-409). The dry run is reachable from all three entry points: uninstall.sh --dry-run (uninstall.sh:70-71, 87-91), UNINSTALL.bat /DRYRUN (UNINSTALL.bat:110-115) and `nerva uninstall --dry-run` (agents/cli/nerva.py:699-700, 3762-3774). Without --confirm, the CLI still refuses with exit 2 (agents/core/uninstall.py:741-744).

(2) Typed confirmation. --purge-data is no longer a bare flag. _confirm_purge (agents/core/uninstall.py:588-624) works in two ways. Interactively, the user must type back the data root's folder name; a mismatch cancels and removes nothing. Without a terminal, --yes-purge must give the data root's exact absolute path. A relative path or the bare folder name is refused, because it would match on every machine (agents/core/uninstall.py:575-586). --yes-purge without --purge-data is refused (agents/core/uninstall.py:726-728). Purge feasibility is checked before the prompt (agents/core/uninstall.py:751-774). The purge runs before any software is removed, so a failed purge leaves the install intact.

(3) Desktop app removal. --gui also removes the Tauri desktop shell, and --gui-only removes only the shell. desktop_app_targets covers macOS, Windows and Linux, plus the cargo output of a source build (agents/core/uninstall.py:126-209). _remove_desktop (agents/core/uninstall.py:436-482) handles each kind of install:
- NSIS installs run their own uninstall.exe in place.
- Copies owned by a package manager are reported with the command that removes them, not deleted.
- A path is reported removed only once it is gone.

--gui-summary is a read-only JSON probe (agents/core/uninstall.py:234-256). The flags are wired in uninstall.sh:29-31, 75-76, in UNINSTALL.bat:45-47, 58 and in agents/cli/nerva.py:707-711.

Latest change (the regression both skeptics found): with no system Python on Windows, UNINSTALL.bat runs from .venv. That fallback, and only that one, now passes --allow-locked-venv (UNINSTALL.bat:89-98, 111, 117). The module then removes every other target and leaves .venv in place. It lists .venv under not_removed with venv_left_behind and exits 1 (agents/core/uninstall.py:536-546, 662-665, 745-749). Before, it refused and pointed the user back at the same script. `nerva uninstall` does not expose the flag (agents/cli/nerva.py:4810-4813). The implementer reports that the new tests failed before the fix (6 failed) and passed after. Both skeptic reviews passed.

Limits that still apply:
- On Windows, `nerva uninstall` (which runs inside .venv) still refuses to remove the software and points to UNINSTALL.bat (agents/core/uninstall.py:310-314, 746-748). Only the dry run and --gui-only work there.
- In the bat's no-system-Python fallback, .venv must be deleted by hand.
- --purge-data erases only the data root. The user-home entries it leaves are listed by kept_after_purge.
- Hermes' --yes maps to --confirm here, and its --full maps to --purge-data.

reviews.summary: `nerva security audit` inventariază distribuțiile interpretorului curent și pinurile Python exacte ale descriptorilor de extensie numiți, întreabă OSV.dev prin `PluginHTTPClient` (rezoluție DNS pinată, ancorele TLS ale owner-ului, breaker; querybatch în loturi de 1000 cu paginare urmărită + un detaliu per advisory; pleacă doar perechi nume+versiune, anunțate pe stderr), unește oglinzile GHSA/PYSEC ale aceluiași CVE într-o singură constatare cu cea mai mare severitate declarată, numește fix-ul din intervalul care conține versiunea instalată și iese 0/1/5. Un advisory fără severitate declarată pică orice prag; o bază de date de neatins, un lot rămas paginat după 20 de pagini sau un audit care nu se încheie înseamnă exit 5 și nicio afirmație. O distribuție cu metadate nedecodabile e sărită și numită; textul advisory-urilor e curățat de caractere de control înainte de terminal. MCP (comenzi stdio configurate de owner) e listat ca neauditat, cu motivul. Probat live: 48 distribuții curate; un pin `requests 2.19.0` dă 5 constatări după unirea a 5 oglinzi PYSEC. Recenzie adversarială independentă: nouă defecte, toate remediate în același PR. reviews.summary: Inbound webhook subscriptions are real and owner-managed. The admin-only routes list, create, patch and delete hooks, and a delivery posts to POST /api/webhooks/{id} with a token or an HMAC-signed body, a deliver-only mode that skips the agent, an event allow-list, a prompt template and a receiver switch that refuses everything when off (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:674-748, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:111-133). The three items the row still listed are now built. (1) A signed test action. The store builds a sample delivery for a hook (its first subscribed event or the one given, a small payload that says it is a test or the owner's own object) and signs it the way a sender must, as the HMAC of the raw body or the token header (agents/core/webhooks.py:936-965). POST /api/webhooks/{hook_id}/test is admin-only; it verifies that sample with the receiver's own signature or token check, reads the receiver switch and the hook's switch, runs the same event, filter and prompt-template classification as a real delivery, and answers a report with the outcome (run, deliver_only, skipped, filtered or refused), the HTTP status a sender would see, the reason, the text the target would get and the sample with its credential masked (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:308-359, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:640-671, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:167-184). It is dry: no turn runs, nothing is pushed, no call, skip or filter is counted, and only a last_test note and an audit row are written. (2) A declarative payload filter instead of the refused --script hook. A hook carries up to 16 rules {path, op, value}, all of which must hold; the ops are eq, ne, contains, startswith, endswith, glob (at most one *), in, exists and missing, each linear in what it reads, with no regex and no owner code run over the attacker-controlled payload (agents/core/webhooks.py:264, agents/core/webhooks.py:277-326, agents/core/webhooks.py:364-420). It is set on create and by PATCH, checked after the event list and before the template, and a delivery a rule turns away is answered 202, never run, and counted as filtered with the rule and the echoed value kept on the hook for the admin (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:102-108, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:124, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:146, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:627-633, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:792-796, agents/core/webhooks.py:916-924). A stored filter that is not valid, including a rule from the first build with the removed regex op matches, reads as unreadable and filters every delivery (fail closed) until it is rewritten (agents/core/webhooks.py:821-828). (3) The CLI verbs. nerva webhook subscribe|list|remove|test ride the same admin routes: subscribe takes the target, type, name, --signed, --events, --prompt, --deliver, --deliver-only, --description and a JSON --filter and prints the hook URL and the token or signing secret once; list shows credential kind, switch, destination, events, filter rule count (or unreadable) and calls; remove deletes; test sends the signed dry sample with --event and --payload and prints the outcome (agents/cli/nerva.py:448-480, agents/cli/nerva.py:2958-2979, agents/cli/nerva.py:2982-3080). The HUD Webhooks panel has a test button that shows the report, a filter editor in each hook's detail pane, a filter box in the create form, a rule-count tag, the filtered count with the last rule that turned a delivery away, and an unreadable-filter warning that never clears the stored filter unless the owner edits it (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:96-112, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:127-145, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:194-205, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:331-339, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:424-445, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:542-547, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:579-583, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:590-595). Pinned by tests: every filter op and the verdict text, rule validation, the removed regex op and fail-closed stored rules, an adversarial-subject timing check, filtered deliveries not retried under an Idempotency-Key, the sample being verified by the receiver, the dry admin-only test route with filtered, skipped and refused outcomes, the CLI verbs round-tripped through the real route handlers, the command tree, and the HUD test button, filter editor and unreadable-filter behaviour (tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:443-485, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:499-528, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:554-569, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:581-588, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:607-621, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:654-664, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:686-701, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:704-724, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:727-738, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:741-755, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:758-765, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:843-845, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:848-941, tests/test_nerva_cli.py:88-94, frontend/src/test/webhooks-panel.test.tsx:808-924, frontend/src/test/webhooks-panel.test.tsx:928-1019). reviews.summary:
The port-conflict diagnostic, plus one stale line of evidence corrected. `serve.py` gains `probe_bind(host, port)`, called from `main()` after the posture guards and before uvicorn binds: a taken port prints the exact address, the command that identifies the holder (`nerva status`) and the way out (`JARVIS_PORT`), then exits **12**; `EACCES` exits **13**, and since #1177 that arm branches on the port number instead of asserting a cause it cannot know — below 1024 it names the privileged-port rule (root or `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE`; move `JARVIS_PORT` above 1024), at or above 1024 it says outright that this is *not* the privileged-port rule and root/Administrator will not help, then points at the reservations that actually produce it (Windows `netsh interface ipv4 show excludedportrange tcp`, whose Hyper-V/WSL blocks routinely cover the shipped default 8080; an SELinux `name_bind` denial on Linux) plus `JARVIS_PORT`. Both codes are deliberately distinct from uvicorn's `STARTUP_FAILURE` (3), which it uses for *every* startup failure — that collision was the actual defect, because a supervisor could not tell "the port is taken" from "the lifespan crashed". The probe is a **diagnostic, not a lock**: it binds and closes, reserves nothing, and any `OSError` outside the two named arms is swallowed, so an unexpected probe failure can never turn a boot that would have worked into a refusal. The socket **constructor sits inside the guarded region** too — a first cut that built it above the `try` turned `JARVIS_HOST=::1` on a box with no IPv6 stack into an 8-frame traceback + exit 1 in place of uvicorn's one-line error + exit 3, the diagnostic making the boot worse than no diagnostic. It also mirrors asyncio's own flags rather than stricter ones: `SO_REUSEADDR` on POSIX, because `uvicorn.Server.startup` binds through `loop.create_server` where asyncio sets it, so a probe without it would refuse a port merely holding a TIME_WAIT connection from the instance the owner just stopped — a boot uvicorn would have completed; and `IPV6_V6ONLY` on an AF_INET6 probe, so an IPv4 listener on the same port cannot turn a working v6 boot into exit 12. **The frozen 2026-09-07 evidence was stale on one point**: it recorded "no --status", but `nerva status` has existed since the unified CLI (the `status` verb in `agents/cli/nerva.py`, `status = verbs.add_parser("status", ...)` at agents/cli/nerva.py:177). 13 `test_probe_bind_*` functions, 16 collected cases (the IPv6-conflict case skips on a box with no IPv6 stack). Both exit codes are asserted **by execution** rather than by reading the branch — the sub-1024 `EACCES` arm runs in a child dropped to an unprivileged uid with `setpriv`, because pytest runs as root here and a sub-1024 bind simply succeeds; the high-port `EACCES` arm is driven through a stubbed `bind()` that answers `EACCES`, parametrised over 1024/8080/49152/65535, because its real reproduction is a Windows excluded port range that cannot be staged on Linux, and a sibling test pins that port 80 still gets the privileged-port sentence. reviews.summary:
`nerva prompt-size` exists and reports the fixed per-call cost by component, largest first, offline: no hub, no backend, no request. That is what makes it usable for the question it answers (what is paid before the conversation starts) on a box where the hub is not even running. It reads the personas from disk and asks the tool registry for the specs it declares.
`agents/core/prompt_size.py` breaks the cost into: one row per agent persona found on disk (`soul_components`, agents/core/prompt_size.py:116); the shared behaviour contract `identity` (`identity_component`, agents/core/prompt_size.py:136); `host-detected`, the one-line block of what Nerva detected about the host (container, WSL, Termux, supervisor; `host_detected_component`, agents/core/prompt_size.py:149); `environment-hint`, the operator's `JARVIS_ENVIRONMENT_HINT` block (`environment_hint_component`, agents/core/prompt_size.py:158); one row per tool, costed as the JSON that crosses the wire rather than by name, because a verbose `input_schema` can outweigh a whole persona (`tool_schema_components`, agents/core/prompt_size.py:197-210); the skills index rendered the way `Agent.build_prompt` renders it, the H326 category-grouped index when given as text and the flat `Available skills:` rows otherwise (`skills_index_component`, agents/core/prompt_size.py:166-183, matching agents/core/agent.py:860-867); a `skills-loaded` row for the skills a session carries from earlier turns, empty and therefore not part of a fresh session's floor (`skills_loaded_component`, agents/core/prompt_size.py:186-194); and the turn scaffold every request pays (`scaffold_component`, agents/core/prompt_size.py:213).
The headline figure is the per-call floor, not the sum: `Breakdown.per_call` (agents/core/prompt_size.py:86) adds the shared components to ONE soul. That is the named agent's soul, or the heaviest soul when no agent is named, so the number is the worst realistic case rather than a flattering one. An unknown agent returns no soul and is not billed to someone else. The first version summed all 18 personas and announced 71.8% of a 32k window where a real request pays about 6.5%; a wrong number is worse than no number, so the per-call floor is what is read first, and tests/test_prompt_size.py pins the correction (`test_the_floor_is_one_soul_not_all_of_them`, tests/test_prompt_size.py:86, and `test_the_window_line_uses_the_per_call_floor_not_the_sum`, tests/test_prompt_size.py:133).
On the current tree the verb reports a heaviest-soul floor of 2475 tokens (soul `hestia`, 1996 tokens, plus 479 shared), and `cmd_prompt_size` (agents/cli/nerva.py:4762) builds `prompt_size.breakdown` with `skills=()` and a registry that is not booted (agents/cli/nerva.py:4779-4786). Both limits are real. The registry is created with `ToolRPCServer.__new__` and never populated, so the offline run lists no tool rows and appends a note saying the tool schemas are not included rather than reporting zero. The skills-index row is also zero in the CLI because no skills are passed. The tool and skill rows are only exercised through the library function, not through a booted hub.
Output is a text table or `--json` (with `per_call_tokens` and `per_call_soul`). The report states that its figures are estimates from the same function the runtime budget uses and points to H673 for the only exact count, the one the provider reports.
Drift re-read (2026-10-12): the only change to agents/core/prompt_size.py since the pin was f0c9c852 (H283 host identity). It adds `host_detected_component` and appends it to `breakdown` before `environment-hint`, and switches `environment_hint_component` from `hint_block` to `operator_block`, so the detected facts and the operator's words are costed as separate rows. This is additive: the floor, the shared/soul split and the rendering are untouched, and the new rows are pinned by tests/test_h283_host_identity.py:384, tests/test_h283_host_identity.py:697 and tests/test_h283_host_notify_and_hint.py:479. The agents/cli/nerva.py drift at that time touched neither the `prompt-size` parser nor `cmd_prompt_size`.

Batch 2's H326 grouped skill index changed how the skills-index row is rendered and added the `skills-loaded` row, both described above; no other claim changed.

reviews.remaining:
Not covered by `nerva prompt-size` against the frozen contract (`hermes prompt-size`: system-prompt bytes, `<available_skills>` index, memory, user profile, three prompt tiers, tool-schema JSON, per-toolset schema cost, per-skill cost).
(1) Memory and user-profile cost are not components; the report lists personas, identity, host-detected, environment-hint, tools, skills index, skills loaded and scaffold only. Memory is per session and variable, not a fixed cost, so reporting it as fixed would be exactly the kind of wrong figure this delivery avoids.
(2) Nerva has no three separate prompt tiers or user-profile block to measure (`Agent.build_prompt` has soul, skills, agent memory and scaffold), so those have no row; `<available_skills>` is a Hermes index and the delivered equivalent is the skills-index block.
(3) Cost is per tool, with no per-toolset aggregation, and there is no per-skill row, only one `skills-index` row.
(4) The offline CLI verb does not boot the registry and passes `skills=()` (agents/cli/nerva.py:4779-4786), so tool-schema and skills-index rows are empty there; the report adds a note that tool schemas are missing instead of reporting zero.
(5) Not verified against a real service: no request was sent, so the figures are estimates comparable with the internal budget, not a provider's count. The exact figure for a running install needs the tool specs and skills of a live hub.

Gap 1, the HUD mismatch between 'paired' and 'allowed', is fixed. The store writes ALLOWED = "allowed" (agents/core/channels/pairing.py:95). The SENDER PAIRING card now uses senderApproved, which accepts 'allowed' and the older 'paired' (frontend/src/gap.tsx:668). An approved sender gets a green tag and no approve button, and its revoke button sends 'unpair'. A blocked sender's revoke button also sends 'unpair'. Only a pending sender gets 'reject' (frontend/src/gap.tsx:696-708). The two-step clear-pending ConfirmAction is at frontend/src/gap.tsx:709-713. It checks the green tag, 2 approve buttons, 1 reject and 2 unpair, and that clicking revoke POSTs action 'unpair' for the allowed sender. reviews.summary:
The recovered native channel-session service rotates durable route generations under the existing stable base/session turn leases. Reset settings support idle minutes and daily local hour with timezone/DST, per-type dm/group/thread and channel overrides, explicit reset texts and bounded route-index ageing. Owner /new and /reset create a fresh transcript; /undo creates a new transcript from exchanges before the last user turn, preserving its predecessor. Existing APScheduler invokes expiry even without new inbound text and skips active leases; routing-index retirement does not delete conversation data. Per-inbound stall episodes track actual processing/model-token activity and use the existing governed owner notification transport once per due episode. Telegram topics, Slack threads/groups and other channel identity/delivery rules remain authoritative. Direct web and CLI reset/undo commands use new concrete IDs; ChatResponse and SSE end expose session_id, the HUD sends it on later turns, Sessions reopens exact older/archived topics, desktop sync and asynchronous callbacks are fenced by current topic/turn. Valid empty snapshots survive restart/resume, while missing or malformed turns refuse without changing in-memory identity. Existing Admin settings persist and validate the nine session options. Focused backend/API/settings/scheduler and frontend transition/reopen/desktop regressions pass. Native adaptation from #1233; no file checkpoint restore or runtime import. reviews.summary: Un mesaj vocal pe Telegram e transcris înainte să-l vadă agentul — echivalentul lui `stt_enabled` din Hermes. `InboundVoiceReader` întreabă poarta înainte de descărcare, mărginește octeții, îi trimite prin `BytesIO` direct la decodor (vorbirea nu atinge discul) și transformă fiecare eșec într-un motiv numit; santinelele motorului nu ajung niciodată la model ca vorbire. Transcriptul circulă ca o tură obișnuită, nu în gard: sunt chiar cuvintele expeditorului, iar protecția reală e filtrul de halucinații (H530). Jumătatea rostită: `/voice off|voice|always` e mod per conversație (`voice_mode.py`, magazie JSON `canal:chat`, implicit off, setat de chat pentru chat), `stt_echo_transcripts` e setarea `voice.stt_echo_transcripts` (o linie de serviciu „am auzit: …” înaintea răspunsului, niciodată rostită), iar `spoken_reply.py` transformă textul livrat într-o notă vocală peste motorul TTS al gazdei — doar proza (fără cod, linkuri, marcaje), tăiată la o limită de propoziție, fișierul șters după citire, nimic din text în log. Cârligul stă unde textul chiar ajunge (`send()` și `finish()` al draftului în flux), deci modul nu poate livra ca audio ce ruterul n-ar fi livrat ca text; orice eșec costă nota vocală, niciodată textul; un 400 pe `sendVoice` reîncearcă o dată ca `sendAudio`. `/voice` numește motorul care ar vorbi și spune „cloud” când e edge-tts. Reevaluarea inițială a raportat 15/15 mutanți uciși; numărul nu a fost reprodus la recitirea din 2026-09-22. Doar Telegram: pe Slack/Discord replica trece prin brokerul `channel.reply`, fără audio. reviews.summary: Fresh assessment 2026-10-13 (ff8641a7): the hub speaks systemd readiness and watchdog: READY once serving, WATCHDOG=1 from the event loop and STOPPING=1 before drain (agents/core/sd_notify.py:131, agents/core/sd_notify.py:110-113, agents/core/sd_notify.py:148, sent from NotifyingServer at agents/core/sd_notify.py:161 and agents/core/sd_notify.py:180-184), with the unit's Type=notify/WatchdogSec/Restart=on-failure (deploy/systemd/jarvis-hub.service:27-29, deploy/systemd/jarvis-hub.service:53); /healthz and /readyz exist (agents/core/routers/ops.py:42, agents/core/routers/ops.py:149); channels drain their lanes on stop (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:863-874). Re-read 2026-10-21 (batch 1c): H010 taught the hub to restart itself to apply an approved, staged restore. agents/core/hub_restart.py:1-16 is the seam: serve.py installs a stopper, and after the server drains run_server re-execs the same pid on POSIX, or exits with RESTART_EXIT_CODE under the Windows NSSM service, or spawns a successor (serve.py:466-501). On such a restart the shutdown sends RELOADING=1 instead of STOPPING=1 (agents/core/sd_notify.py:142-146), so systemd does not stop the unit under the re-exec. A keepalive thread then feeds WATCHDOG=1 and extends the timeout from the drain through the new image's boot until READY=1 (agents/core/sd_notify.py:258-262, agents/core/sd_notify.py:265-276, ended at agents/core/sd_notify.py:132-133); the restart flag is now read with env_flag (agents/core/sd_notify.py:270). tests/test_backup_h010_review.py:314-326 and tests/test_backup_h010_review.py:329-338 pin RELOADING versus STOPPING, and tests/test_backup_h010_review2.py:430 pins that the watchdog has no gap across a slow re-exec. The STOPPING=1 send is at agents/core/sd_notify.py:148 and the other sd_notify citations were re-pointed by content. This self-restart exists only for a staged restore: it does not notify sessions, add a drain marker, flush transcripts, record why the last process ended or guard against restart loops, so the remaining list is unchanged and the status stays partial. reviews.summary: Fresh assessment 2026-10-13 (ff8641a7): Email is a real, reachable channel but only the basic transport. agents/core/channels/email.py:118 polls IMAP with `search(None, "UNSEEN")` (server flag, no seen-UID store), email.py:128 takes only the first text/plain part (no HTML stripping, no attachments), and email.py:21 normalises the From address for the pairing gate (allowlist-by-pairing), with its own docstring admitting the header is forgeable without DMARC. Outbound email.py:65 builds a bare MIMEText with no In-Reply-To/References and no attachments. Governance is better than Hermes: agents/core/channels/manager.py:30 keeps email out of generic direct send so SMTP is reached only via the governed channel.reply path; tests/test_email_inbox_transport.py pins inbound threading into the inbox and the approved-reply send.
reviews.remaining:
- SPF/DKIM/DMARC (or Authentication-Results) verification of inbound senders, surfaced on the decision card
- Automated-sender suppression (no-reply, bounce, Auto-Submitted, vacation loops)
- Seen-UID tracking instead of the server UNSEEN flag
- HTML-part stripping/body extraction when no text/plain part exists
- Inbound attachment ingestion and outbound attachments
- RFC reply threading headers (In-Reply-To/References) on SMTP replies
- SMTP IPv4 fallback

reviews.summary: Telegram photos are read, not only recognised. `classify` (agents/core/channels/inbound_media.py) recognises the ten attachment kinds in `RECOGNISED_KINDS` and turns a missing file handle, a declared size above the 20 MB bot ceiling or an unreadable kind into a named reason, so the sender gets one plain line from `describe` instead of silence. `InboundImageReader` (agents/core/channels/media_reader.py) describes a photo through a proven-local VLM and hands the description to the turn as data, never as instructions. Locality follows the `screen_locator` rule: `is_local` derives only from `resolve_vlm_config().is_local`, `TelegramChannel._read_image` asks `refusal()` before any download, and `_backend_call` checks again before it posts: `interactive_local_identity` re-reads the live config and refuses a non-loopback base URL, the role consent and model-selection guards run, and the call goes through `unattended_media_request_scope` with `generate_vision_checked`, so a non-loopback VLM receives no bytes (the sender is told the owner must configure or acknowledge the local vision model, `REASON_POLICY`). `_download_file` bounds the transfer by the bytes that actually arrive, not by the sender-chosen `file_size`, and `_safe_file_path` rejects any `getFile` path that is not Telegram-shaped before it enters the bot-token URL. The description is folded to one line, capped and wrapped in the Wave 5a `fence_tool_result` fence, deliberately without the `spotlight` datamark, which would replace spaces with '▁' and blind the gateway's `detect_injection`; a photo with '<<END UNTRUSTED>>' written on it cannot close its own fence. The caption never reaches the describer: it travels separately as the sender's question. The turn goes through the normal door, so `Gateway._inbound_meta` marks it `inbound:telegram` and runs the detector over exactly what the model reads. Voice notes are read on the other path: a transcript is the sender's own words and travels unfenced as an ordinary turn (`inbound_voice`, row H071). `ChannelDescriptor` separates `recognises_media` from `reads_media` with the subset invariant checked at construction, and `READABLE_KINDS` is exactly {photo, voice}. Drift re-read (2026-10-12): media_reader.py now re-resolves the VLM config per call and adds an owner policy/consent gate (REASON_POLICY) plus a loopback identity check and native wire scope before posting, telegram.py gained ephemeral replies, owner-once/consent hooks and topic replies without touching the photo download path, and the media test now expects REASON_POLICY for a remote URL; photo/voice reading, the size bound, the path screen and the fence still hold and 132 pinned tests pass. Re-read after batch 4 (H006 H039 H221 H303 H354 H403 H414 H486) changed files this row pins
reviews.remaining: Only photos and voice notes, only on Telegram. Not delivered: reading audio files, video, video notes, animations, documents and stickers (recognised, answered with 'reading … is not wired up yet'); a disk cache under a media directory so vision tools can open a local path (bytes stay in memory for one call); location and venue pins (recognised as `location`, deliberately not echoed, not read); caching of media from observed group messages and from replied-to messages; media ingestion on WhatsApp, Discord, Teams, Google Chat and email (those adapters pass text only). Documented limitation, not solved: taint cannot be tracked through the model; what travels is the coarse fact that the turn read untrusted material, and the channel's `inbound` origin is what keeps an action derived from a photo in approval. `mark_turn_recall_tainted()` is not called here because it would be a no-op (escalate-only over an already untrusted origin). UNVERIFIED on real services: the suite is hermetic; no real Telegram message received, no local VLM actually called, `getFile` and the download exercised only against a fake client.

The router serves /.well-known/agent-card, POST /api/a2a/task and admin peer, inbox and decide routes (agents/core/routers/a2a.py:45, agents/core/routers/a2a.py:54, agents/core/routers/a2a.py:129). There is no outbound client: Nerva cannot discover, call, list, read the history of, or orchestrate a peer. There is also no JSON-RPC task lifecycle with error codes and no push-notification callbacks.
reviews.remaining:
- Outbound A2A tools (discover/call/list/history/orchestrate) mediated by the kernel, with peer responses marked as tainted input and a per-surface enable gate

Actuation goes through HomeAssistantServiceDriver (agents/core/house/actuation.py:312) and the house routes (agents/core/routers/house.py:499). HestiaBridge applies a per-entity cooldown and caps before proposing actions (agents/core/house/hestia_bridge.py:245, agents/core/house/hestia_bridge.py:263; tests/test_hestia_bridge.py:249). However, nothing outside the module and tests constructs or schedules the bridge. collect_events is only called by the reality probe (agents/core/observability/house_reality.py:481). So no filtered HA event ever starts an agent turn or becomes a message. There is also no deliver=homeassistant target for scheduled output.
reviews.remaining:
- Run a live event loop that turns filtered HA state changes (with cooldown) into agent turns or messages, tagged as tainted inbound input
- Wire HestiaBridge (observe/propose) into a running loop; today it has no runtime caller
- A deliver=homeassistant target (HA notify) for cron and automation output
- A readiness probe for the HA channel in health/status

Final review at HEAD 57ed6db. The three gaps from the 2026-10-14 assessment were that the chrome did not show the messaging gateway, had no active-sessions count and had no version badge. All three are now closed on this branch.

Backend. /status (agents/core/routers/status.py:111) now returns three more things:
- "version" (agents/core/routers/status.py:125).
- A "gateway" summary (agents/core/routers/status.py:141). It is built by _gateway_state (agents/core/routers/status.py:65-70): "running" with the sorted list of running channels, "stopped" when channels are registered but none runs, and "none" when no channel is registered.
- A "sessions" block (agents/core/routers/status.py:142). It is built by _session_counts (agents/core/routers/status.py:73-85), which counts sessions active in the last 900 s (agents/core/routers/status.py:32). The count comes from CheckpointStore.active_session_count (agents/core/checkpoint.py:407-421), which returns None when the store is missing or fails. In that case the API reports state "unknown" instead of a guessed 0.

Frontend.
- The loader reads /status with readStatusChrome (frontend/src/api/loaders.ts:119). Malformed or missing fields become unknown (frontend/src/api/status-chrome.ts:24-36).
- app.tsx stores this on the existing poll (frontend/src/app.tsx:614). The poll runs every 30 s (frontend/src/app.tsx:630) and passes the data to TopBar and Rail (frontend/src/app.tsx:676, frontend/src/app.tsx:682).
- The top bar has a GATEWAY badge (frontend/src/shell.tsx:177). Its readout comes from gatewayView (frontend/src/shell.tsx:14-20).
- The active-session count sits inside the GATEWAY badge (frontend/src/shell.tsx:149-151, frontend/src/shell.tsx:177). The badge title gives the count and the time window, and the count shows a dash when unknown.
- The hub version is shown on the brand line (frontend/src/shell.tsx:169).
- The collapsed rail has a gateway dot (frontend/src/shell.tsx:240-242).

The badge strip now drops whole badges in a fixed priority order when space runs short (frontend/src/shell.tsx:32-49). GATEWAY carries data-keep 6 and is never dropped before LLM and DATA, so the session count stays on screen as long as GATEWAY does. The count is styled so it does not wrap (frontend/src/styles.css:126). The existing honesty chrome (DATA DEMO/OFFLINE/EMPTY/LIVE, EGRESS, MIC, LiveSourceChip) is still in place.

Review history, briefly. Round 3 fixed the last skeptic finding: a separate SESSIONS badge had the lowest priority and was dropped at every laptop width from 1600 down. The count was merged into GATEWAY. The +N overflow-chip alternative was rejected as redundant, because GATEWAY is never dropped. A later unit test pins this: at the 3-badge width the visible badges are LLM, DATA and GATEWAY, and the count is still visible (frontend/src/test/status-chrome.test.tsx:161-175). The row passed two adversarial skeptics.

Honest limits:
- The poll runs every 30 s, where Hermes polls every 10 s. This is a cadence difference, not a missing capability.
- The Playwright layout spec (frontend/e2e/status-chrome-layout.spec.ts:54-108) checks that the count is drawn and is the top element at its own centre, across viewport widths. It was not run here because no Playwright browsers are installed. The implementer reports it passing, and that it fails on the previous commit.
- The pixel measurements in the implementer's summary come from a temporary probe that has been deleted. I did not re-check them.

Test runs, done twice:
- tests/test_status_router.py: 8 passed in both runs.
- vitest on frontend/src/test/status-chrome.test.tsx plus frontend/src/test/live-source-chip.test.tsx: 20 passed (2 files) in both runs. Re-read after batch 4 (H006 H039 H221 H303 H354 H403 H414 H486) changed files this row pins

Fresh assessment 2026-10-13 (9f92d937): The HUD has a server-synced appearance preference set: font (5 options), accent (4), look (obsidian/graphite), density, motion, scanline and dotgrid (frontend/src/appearance.ts:6-10), plus the HUD language added in batch 4 (frontend/src/appearance.ts:11-12), persisted through GET/PUT /api/preferences/appearance (agents/core/routers/preferences.py:27-40) and pinned by tests/test_appearance_preferences.py, frontend/src/test/appearance-sync.test.tsx and frontend/src/test/appearance-state.test.tsx. There are no operator-authored theme files, no user theme directory, no palette/colorOverride/typography/asset schema, no custom CSS, no layout variants, no font catalog beyond the fixed list and no server-rendered bootstrap CSS. Re-read 2026-10-24 (batch 4): H221 added the HUD language to the same fixed option list; there are still no operator-authored themes, custom CSS or layout variants, so the verdict is unchanged.

JobStore, the HUD and the CLI can create and edit all four job actions, with a visual schedule builder, 16 blueprints with typed forms, an atomically bounded repeat count and per-job delivery to already configured channels or to history only. There are doctor, incidents (pauses after failures), an editable notepad, status/remove and an idempotent tick in the scheduler's time zone, refused while the scheduler is running. The task, quiet-hours, budget and e-stop gates are kept, and the flush of deferred messages now checks the e-stop. The Automations entry in the main bar opens a dedicated space; the native create dialog manages focus, Tab, Escape and return to the button. The OpenAPI types include the four new routes. Review: update writes only the requested fields and cannot reset the atomic reservations; history keeps the effective text for brief/remind without delivery. Local Python scripts now have a source snapshot bound to each run's approval, persistent pending results, and either direct no_agent delivery or an isolated context treated as untrusted data. The API and CLI distinguish acceptance from completion; empty content does not call the model. Manual run now persists a bounded receipt and returns HTTP 202; scheduler/offline tick executes through the shared job firing path. Atomic coalescing and portable cross-process locks prevent duplicate execution. Configuration snapshots, pending-script reconciliation, crash-unknown state without replay, and concurrent retention are tested. HUD and CLI restore accepted request status and distinguish queued, waiting and completed execution. Approved script-only options.workdir now persists a canonical existing directory within current terminal roots for script plus no_agent:true. Real concurrent subprocess tests verify relative reads and unchanged parent cwd; denial, e-stop, deleted/escaping directories, restart and changed task arguments are covered. Model project instructions/tool workspace context remains unsupported. Model-bearing ask jobs now accept enabled_toolsets through CLI and HUD using an explicit installed basic/files/terminal catalog. reviews.summary:
An agent's persona can now be edited in the UI and is live on its next turn. That is Hermes' persona editor, over the version history Nerva already kept. Until now the history was a side record: a commit or rollback in the Prompts panel changed a JSON file while the agent kept its old persona. agents/core/soul_edit.py holds the one path an edit takes, apply_soul (:152). (1) Refusals. An agent the hub has not loaded is refused (404; agent_folder, :100, returns an enumerated folder name in the id alphabet, so no request value reaches a path). So is text over MAX_SOUL_BYTES (256 KiB of UTF-8, :40; 413), safe mode (:171; 409, because overlays are not read there, H275) and a persona the H387 guard would drop (:174; 422 with the verdict). guard_verdict (:60) runs the same scan and cap as Agent._load_soul, and GET /api/agents/{id}/soul now reports it through the same function. A line the guard only quarantines is applied, and the verdict names it. (2) Nothing live is lost. The first edit keeps the file on disk as v1 ("on disk before the first edit"). A file changed on disk since the last version, such as a hand edit, is kept as its own version ("on disk, changed outside the editor") before it is replaced (:185). An agent with no persona file has nothing to keep. (3) Written where the model reads it. The text goes to the owner's overlay (overlay_path, :115): souls/<id>/SOUL.local.md in the data home, else the repo-local SOUL.local.md, never the shipped SOUL.md. The write is atomic (_write_atomically, :126: temporary file, fsync, replace; a failure leaves no temporary file and records no new version). (4) Versioned, then live. The text is committed (:195; the same text twice is one version). The agent re-reads its persona (_load_soul, :197), and the result says whether the running agent now reads the written file. (5) Audited without the text. A SETTINGS_CHANGE row names the agent, the version and its hash. A plain commit and a history-only rollback are audited the same way (record_version, :224; agents/core/routers/admin.py:808, :860). Surfaces. PUT /api/admin/agents/{id}/soul {content, message} (agents/core/routers/agents_api.py:132, admin). POST /api/admin/prompts/{id}/rollback applies the version through the same path for a loaded agent (agents/core/routers/admin.py:849); the shared contract _identity (served from IDENTITY.local.md) and keys that are no loaded agent keep the history-only rollback. Description. A description: field in the SOUL front-matter is the agent's one-line description (description_of, :84, and description_in, :89: one line, at most 400 characters). It is listed on GET /agents and the SOUL read (agents/core/routers/agents_api.py:179, :124) and is never part of the prompt. POST /api/admin/agents/{id}/description/draft (agents/core/routers/agents_api.py:150; draft_description, :238) asks the strict-local model for one paragraph from the live persona and saves nothing. With no local model it is a 503, never a cloud call (:255-258). HUD. The Dossier has an Edit persona button that opens the live SOUL in frontend/src/soul-edit.tsx (SoulEditor, :49, mounted at frontend/src/modes.tsx:118). It offers Preview against the live text, Apply, Draft description with Use it (withDescription, :15, writes the front-matter line), and the hub's refusal in words (refusalText, :32). The Dossier also shows the description. The Prompts panel (PromptsPanel in frontend/src/gap.tsx, not pinned: high-churn) gets apply beside commit, through the same PUT, and says when a rollback is live. Tests: tests/test_soul_edit_route.py (29) covers the apply, the seed and hand-edit versions, deduplication, blocked and quarantined text, the audit row, size, ids, an unloaded folder, admin, the repo overlay, safe mode, a failed write, no store, a reload that misses the file, rollback (live, to the shipped text, refused, missing, history-only keys, audited), a plain commit, the description (listed, bounded, never prompted) and the draft (a proposal, strict-local, empty). frontend/src/test/soul-edit.test.tsx has 6. tests/test_h10_22_prompt_versioning.py now asserts that the rollback is live, in a throwaway data home. 61 mutants: 58 caught, eight of them after survivors got cases. Two survivors of the first-edit-only seed led to keeping hand edits as versions; that code's own five mutants are caught. The fsync is a crash-only property. Every configuration key is reachable and searchable from the UI, and every one but a secret or a route-only row (settings_db.ROUTE_ONLY: the skill switches, the voice command providers, the security data-handling acknowledgments) is portable and resettable. The backend it builds on: `GET /api/admin/settings` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:73) returns every category, and the per-category PUT (agents/core/routers/admin.py:194) validates with `validate_category` and answers 422 before any write, auditing the changed key names and the new value of a choice only (`_audited_values`, agents/core/routers/admin.py:124). New in H157: `GET /api/admin/settings/export` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:78, registered before the `/{category}` read so it is never taken for one) returns the declared settings as a `nerva-settings/1` document with an attachment disposition, leaving out every secret (encrypted at rest, or named like a token, secret, password, client id or API key), `mcp.servers` (it holds credentials by design) any URL that carries a password (`http://user:pw@host`, in a list too), and any free-form value the H495 secret scanner would mask (or every free-form value, when the scanner cannot run), and naming each left-out setting with its reason (export_settings, agents/core/settings_db.py:1334; is_secret_setting, agents/core/settings_db.py:1280; _looks_like_credential, agents/core/settings_db.py:1313; _url_password, agents/core/settings_db.py:1297). `POST /api/admin/settings/import` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:325) takes such a document (at most 1 MB and 1,000 keys, the body counted as it streams in, so a chunked upload is bounded too: _bounded_body, agents/core/routers/admin.py:312). The import and the reset take only an `application/json` request (415 otherwise, a type a browser must pre-check before sending) and refuse one the browser marks cross-site (403), since the admin guard trusts loopback on a default install (_refuse_cross_site_write, agents/core/routers/admin.py:298); every reply is no-store, and only a JSON `true` makes a dry run. A NaN, an Infinity or nesting too deep to store is refused (422), never stored, an `mcp.servers` entry needs a name (validate_category, agents/core/settings_db.py:1129, via _mcp_servers_problem, agents/core/settings_db.py:1201; the loader skips a nameless entry too, MCPManager.load_from_config, agents/core/mcp/client.py:926), and 2000 and 2000.0 are the same number, so no change (_same_value, agents/core/settings_db.py:1422). In the document every key must be declared and passes the same `validate_category` a single write does, so a posture flag or an out-of-range value is refused like any other; one refusal and nothing is written (422 with every reason) (plan_import, agents/core/settings_db.py:1366). Only the keys whose value differs are written, in one sqlite transaction, all or nothing, secrets encrypted as a single write encrypts them (apply_import, agents/core/settings_db.py:1456), with one audit row naming the settings (and the new value of a choice); `"dry_run": true` answers what would change, a secret's values shown as `(secret)` and a credential-shaped free value as `(hidden)`, so the preview never echoes one (describe_changes, agents/core/settings_db.py:1430). `POST /api/admin/settings/{category}/reset` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:391) puts one category back to its declared values and names the keys that moved, with an audit row; it keeps the category's secrets and its route-only rows (the skill switches, the voice command providers, the security data-handling acknowledgments) and names them (kept, reset_kept, agents/core/settings_db.py:1474; the HUD counts every kept row as a secret) and names the settings the product posture still forces (overridden, posture_overridden, agents/core/settings_db.py:1483), where the global reseed (agents/core/routers/admin.py:430) was the only reset (reset_category, agents/core/settings_db.py:1581). The v2 console SettingsPanel (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2894; widgets typed by settingsField, frontend/src/gap.tsx:2871) now has a search across every category matching a setting's category.key or label, with a match count and an honest no-match line (settingMatches, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:37); a reset per category heading (only one with declared rows) that asks first, by a second click that names how many settings go back and moves the focus to itself, drops the category's unsaved edits once it runs and names what was kept and what the posture still forces (ResetCategory, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:92); edits hidden by the search are counted beside the save; and a MOVE A CONFIGURATION section (SettingsTransfer, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:187) that downloads the export and names what the hub left out, and imports a pasted or chosen file by showing the hub's dry run (each change old → new) and applying it only on a second step, listing every reason on a refusal; a pasted `dry_run` is dropped so the apply step is never a dry run, the text is held while the hub answers, and the file picker is reachable from the keyboard. The standalone /admin app's GlobalConfigPage (agents/web/static/admin.js:447) is unchanged, and `nerva config list|get|set|check` (cmd_config in agents/cli/nerva.py; the file is high-churn and no longer pinned by this row) still edits single keys offline. tests/test_settings_transfer.py (28 cases) covers the export (every declared key either exported or named as left out, secrets, client ids, mcp.servers, a token-shaped value, a scanner that cannot run, the stored value), the import (an export imports back as no change, valid changes, every refusal a single write makes, nothing written on one refusal, one transaction, the posture flag, a secret encrypted and never echoed, the bound), the per-category reset, and the routes (admin only, the export not read as a category, preview then apply with one audit row, every reason on a refusal, no row when nothing changes, reset and 404); tests/test_h157b_settings_review.py (30, the first review) covers the JSON-only and cross-site refusals, URL passwords, a credential in a list, the hidden preview, NaN, Infinity and deep nesting, nameless MCP servers, number equality, secrets kept on a reset, the posture's settings named, the change listeners, the 1 MB bound for a sized and a chunked body and the JSON-only dry run; frontend/src/test/settings-tools.test.tsx (12) covers the search, the two-step reset, the export note, the dry-run preview and the second-step apply with the admin credential, a refusal's reasons, text that is not JSON, an import that changes nothing, a reset that drops unsaved edits and names kept secrets, edits hidden by the search, a pasted dry run never applied and the keyboard-reachable file button. 25 backend mutants, all caught (one after its case was added: a scanner that cannot run). reviews.summary:
GET /api/support/bundle (admin) builds an allow-listed diagnostic bundle (agents/core/routers/support.py:21-39). It holds meta/version and build, posture, capabilities, egress and audit counts, model ids, the names of credential variables that are set, non-default settings, and an opt-in, redacted, e-mail-masked WARNING+ log tail. The route caps that tail at 500 lines with log_lines. With download=true it serves the same no-cache JSON as an attachment named nerva-support-bundle-<UTC stamp>.json (agents/core/routers/support.py:36-38).

The bundle now has a component-health section. _health reads the orchestrator's ComponentRegistry, the same source as GET /api/health/components, and returns total, ok, the failed names, failed_unnamed and a state of ok, degraded or empty (agents/core/support_bundle.py:271-290). Only names that look like plain identifiers are printed (agents/core/support_bundle.py:66); any other key is only counted. With no registry, or when reading it fails, the section is {"error": "unavailable"} and never an invented all-ok. build_bundle includes the section (agents/core/support_bundle.py:312), and render_text prints a "components: N/M ok · failed: ..." line (agents/core/support_bundle.py:342-350). `nerva support bundle --logs N` serves the same report from the terminal (agents/cli/nerva.py:823).

The HUD SupportBundleCard now offers the log tail through a 0/50/200/500 menu (frontend/src/panels/support-voice.tsx:97, frontend/src/panels/support-voice.tsx:203-211). The menu changes the admin read to ?log_lines=N (frontend/src/panels/support-voice.tsx:108). The card shows a logs row with the record count, the truncated flag, any note or the error (frontend/src/panels/support-voice.tsx:339-353). It also shows a component-health row with ok/total and failed names in red; an empty registry is shown grey, never green (frontend/src/panels/support-voice.tsx:319-337). A "download .json" button sits beside the copy button (frontend/src/panels/support-voice.tsx:355-360). It saves the admin-fetched JSON as a Blob named from the bundle's own generated_at (frontend/src/panels/support-voice.tsx:100-104, frontend/src/panels/support-voice.tsx:156-178). It says only that the download started, and it reports an unavailable or failed download as such. The card is mounted through the panel sections (frontend/src/gap.tsx:5528), and the ConsoleOverlay gives live inspection (frontend/src/gap.tsx:5567).

Tests: tests/test_support_bundle.py:358-431 cover the health roll-up, an unavailable registry with odd names, the render_text line, and the route's attachment download with log_lines; the file passes 30 tests. frontend/src/panels/support-voice.test.tsx:178-266 cover the log opt-in path, unavailable logs, the health rendering including the empty registry, health counted as a failed section, the download file name, and an honest failure when the browser cannot download.

Minor, not part of the row's gap: after a failed reload the copy and download buttons could still save the previous bundle. Built on this branch. Hermes has a Documentation page inside its dashboard with an "open in a new tab" affordance. Nerva's written material (the user guide, FLAGS.md on what each posture flag costs, and the privacy and camera-privacy notes) was only in the repository. The Dockerfile copied it into the image, but nothing served it.

(1) The route. agents/core/routers/help_docs.py is registered on the app in agents/web.py (not pinned: a high-churn file; the pinned route tests drive web.app) and user-guarded on the router (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:27).
- GET /api/help/docs (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:103) lists the allowlist: slug, title, whether the file shipped, and each document's sections.
- GET /api/help/docs/{slug} (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:113) returns the Markdown text, capped at MAX_DOC_CHARS with a truncated flag (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:121).
- The allowlist is the fixed DOCS table (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:31): user-guide, flags, privacy, camera-privacy. A slug is only ever a key into it, never joined into a path, so an unknown slug, '../' or encoded traversal is 404.
- A file must be a regular file under the install root; a symlink is refused (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:85). A file missing from an install reads as "not available", not an error.
- Responses are no-store.

(2) The page. DocsPanel (frontend/src/panels/docs.tsx:37) is registered in the console's Start group (frontend/src/console-routes.ts:6), in PANEL_COMPONENTS (frontend/src/gap.tsx:5420) and in the desktop app's route allowlist (desktop/src-tauri/hud-routes.json:49).
- It lists the documents, disabling one not shipped, and renders the chosen one through the new shared Markdown component (frontend/src/markdown.tsx:101).
- That component emits React elements only (no innerHTML path): headings with anchors, code fences, pipe tables, lists, quotes and rules, plus bold, italic, inline code and links. A link renders only for http(s) or a same-origin path, in a new tab with rel=noopener noreferrer (safeHref, frontend/src/markdown.tsx:25). Raw HTML in a document stays literal text. There is no regex lookbehind, so older Safari can parse the bundle.

(3) Open in a new tab. Every document is a standalone deep link, /v2/console/docs?doc=<slug>[#section] (docHref, frontend/src/panels/docs.tsx:15). The panel offers it as "open in a new tab ↗" with rel=noopener noreferrer (frontend/src/panels/docs.tsx:67), and a #section is scrolled into view (frontend/src/panels/docs.tsx:49).

(4) The flag's cost where it is flipped, per the row rationale.
- Each document's sections carry the names their headings document. The hub computes them with heading_anchor (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:44), which one shared fixture pins character for character to the renderer's headingAnchor (frontend/src/markdown.tsx:94).
- The Settings panel links every setting FLAGS.md documents to its section with a "cost ↗" beside the toggle (sectionIndex, frontend/src/panels/docs.tsx:20; frontend/src/gap.tsx:2897, frontend/src/gap.tsx:2989).

The HUD now has one confirmation for every action that needs one, graded the way the approval queue grades risk, and agent text renders as Markdown wherever it is shown. Both halves of Hermes' confirm-and-render behaviour are covered. (1) One confirmation, graded by RiskTier. frontend/src/confirm.tsx declares RISK_TIER (frontend/src/confirm.tsx:19) with the names and values of agents/core/autonomy/policy.py:26 RiskTier, and tests/test_confirm_tiers.py:22 ties the two lists together. confirmStyle (frontend/src/confirm.tsx:23) gives READ_ONLY one click, REVERSIBLE two steps (the button arms, a second button confirms) and EXTERNAL and IRREVERSIBLE_OR_MONEY a phrase typed exactly (frontend/src/confirm.tsx:143); a tier it does not know takes the most. ConfirmAction (frontend/src/confirm.tsx:74) moves focus to the control that replaced the one pressed. Escape cancels, and a cancelled phrase is not remembered (frontend/src/confirm.tsx:95). Enter confirms only on a match. An action that returns a promise keeps the confirmation open, with both buttons held, until it lands; one that answers false keeps it armed to retry (fire, frontend/src/confirm.tsx:97). A page can open and close it itself (armed/onCancel, frontend/src/confirm.tsx:114, taking focus as it opens, :110) or keep a typed one always open (open: no trigger, no cancel). (2) Every hand-rolled site uses it. The kill switch's HALT ALL stays one click on purpose (READ_ONLY, frontend/src/gap.tsx:803), because an emergency stop must never wait for a second click; disengage is typed (DISENGAGE, frontend/src/gap.tsx:801, :785). Forget-me types FORGET (frontend/src/gap.tsx:3798) and the acquisition purge its phrase (frontend/src/gap.tsx:4733). Trust-ops rotation types the scope in an always-open confirmation that a refusal leaves filled and a rotation clears (frontend/src/panels/trust-ops.tsx:397). The marketplace uninstall types the folder it deletes, because the rmtree has no undo on this box; a changed folder is typed again, and a refusal keeps it armed (frontend/src/panels/marketplace-admin.tsx:313, confirmRemove :207). The webhook delete is two steps, opened by the row and held while that row's switch is pending (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:553, remove :285). The ESTOP pause is two steps (frontend/src/modes3.tsx:216). tests/test_confirm_tiers.py:26 checks that each of these files imports and uses ConfirmAction and has no window.confirm. (3) Markdown wherever agent text is shown. Chat bubbles, for agent and vision replies (frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:79, :96), and decision cards (frontend/src/shell.tsx:274) render through Bubble (frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:130). Bubble is memoised on the text, so a streamed token re-parses one bubble. It uses the shared React-only Markdown (frontend/src/markdown.tsx:101): lists, fences, tables and http(s) or same-origin links render, while raw HTML and any other link stay text. Canvas Markdown artifacts go through the same renderer (MarkdownBody, frontend/src/artifacts.tsx:78) and are bounded to MARKDOWN_LIMIT (4,000) code points when shown as well as when saved. A new breaks option (frontend/src/markdown.tsx:171) keeps a single newline as a line break for chat and artifacts, and documents keep paragraph joining. The owner's own turns are shown exactly as typed. Test-manual gap G22 (collapsed newlines, fences as prose) is closed. reviews.summary: Governed SSH terminal execution remains available only for declared, enabled targets. The runner applies hardline, audited target policy, durable approval, the terminal.exec contract and Action Kernel before the built-in SSH transport; the transport reconstructs a quoted remote argv, pins known hosts, requires key authentication, bypasses user SSH config and agent, and disables forwarding and ControlMaster (agents/core/environments/execution.py:162-231,390-405,743-923; agents/core/environments/ssh_transport.py:310-344,346-415). Owner-once approvals now add a private, one-use physical gate at ssh_transport.py:396-400: it rechecks the exact request, target decision, kernel decision and runtime before spawn. Tests prove paused policy/kernel revocation blocks dispatch and spawn (tests/test_h485_owner_once_transport.py). This adds no connection manager, real-host interoperability evidence, or other missing Hermes features. Batch collateral review (2026-10-04, base9bfa085c): The manual (legacy) kernel lane was then explicitly `decision.backend == "docker"`; it now also admits local and SSH targets only when a request check and legacy kernel check are configured (execution.py:215-220). The initial cross-backend refusal-precedence regression was corrected in 02aba704: the existing SSH-flag-off fixture again receives `ssh_transport_not_implemented` without a request callback. SSH transport, private owner-once gate and this row’s remaining remote-manager limitations are unchanged. The corrected six-module offline scope passed 413 cases; no real SSH host was contacted. Drift re-read (2026-10-12): execution.py and ssh_transport.py diffed from 02aba704/42840e3d: run() and both dispatch branches only moved, and the accepted-manual (legacy) kernel lane, formerly Docker-only, now also covers local and SSH when a request check and legacy kernel check are wired, with its own pre-spawn physical gate on SSH (ssh_transport.py:401-405) and tests/test_h011_manual_host_kernel.py added as its proof; the SSH-flag-off refusal (execution.py:390-392) and the remote-manager gaps are unchanged; 151 pinned tests pass, no real SSH host contacted.
reviews.remaining: Rândul cere mult peste execuție și restul nu e livrat: manager de conexiuni ControlMaster, erori clasificate, sugestii de gazde din ~/.ssh/config, bootstrap care refolosește-sau-pornește un serviciu remote, revalidare de liveness, tranzacție de update cu jurnal de recuperare și linii de restore per profil, fan-out "update all instances". ControlMaster e o divergență deliberată, nu o scăpare: un socket de control partajat e un canal autentificat reutilizabil lăsat pe disc, iar transportul îl dezactivează explicit. NEVERIFICAT pe hardware: nicio sesiune SSH reală nu a fost deschisă din această livrare — suita e ermetică, fără socket și fără binar ssh, deci interoperabilitatea cu un sshd real rămâne nedovedită.

reviews.summary: Default-off per-turn keep-awake with host.control gate, refcount and release. Battery/resume state via guarded snapshot/SSE, scheduled tick and background job deferral. Desktop background-throttling policy on both webviews. Current verification: 75 passed, 1 rustc skip; power-chip Vitest passed in 23-test group; no native Windows/systemd/macOS acceptance.
reviews.remaining: Windows keep-awake state can be falsely reported active: _windows_set_state ignores SetThreadExecutionState return value (zero means failure), while KeepAwake._start unconditionally sets _win_held=True (agents/core/power.py:173-177, :280-283). SetThreadExecutionState is per calling thread, but acquire/release may execute on different turn/shutdown threads; release on another thread may not clear the original assertion. Use one owning thread or a host-supported process-level mechanism, validate return and release on that owner; cover failure and cross-thread behavior. Host-bound systemd/macOS/Windows and browser background behavior has no live acceptance in this review; H182 cannot be claimed fully equivalent from mocks alone.
