reviews.summary:
Built in #1207 together with H153 (critic note 7: one spec, one panel), then fixed after an adversarial review. The v2 console has a Webhooks panel, WebhooksPanel (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:269), registered in the Interop group (frontend/src/console-routes.ts:50; the entry is asserted at frontend/src/test/webhooks-panel.test.tsx:71). Interop mode's WEBHOOKS list links to it by an accessible name (frontend/src/modes2.tsx:343). Every panel call sends the admin credential. The backend stays admin-only CRUD: list, create, switch and delete all carry Depends(admin_guard) (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:237, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:243, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:257, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:284).

Interop mode is built from its four sources alone (hydrateInterop, frontend/src/api/live.ts:126). All four (A2A peers, MCP servers, widgets, webhooks) are admin-only routes and are fetched with the admin credential, and so is the webhooks settings category: while the receiver switch is off every webhook row reads "receiver off", and a switch it could not read is said under WEBHOOKS (frontend/src/api/live.ts:119, frontend/src/modes2.tsx:344). A section whose source failed is empty and says "not connected", and an empty real list says "none" (Section, frontend/src/modes2.tsx:304); the demo seed's rows are never shown under the LIVE chip. When no source answers nothing is overwritten, so the mode stays "Not connected" and DEMO keeps its seed. The review found that fetching only the webhooks list with the credential had marked the whole mode LIVE over seeded peers, MCP servers and widgets.

The five accepted parts:
(1) Create dialog: name, agent or workflow target, target id and an HMAC-signed toggle, and, since H153, a description, an event list, a prompt template, where the result goes and deliver only, posted to POST /api/webhooks. A refusal shows the hub's own reason, and an empty target is refused before any request. The create button is held while the call is pending and while a new hook's credentials are on screen, so a second hook cannot replace a secret before it was saved.
(2) Created result, shown once (Reveal, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:227): the absolute trigger URL (triggerUrl, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:63: the page origin, the base path and the encoded id), and the token, or the signing secret for a signed hook, each with a copy button that says "copied" in a polite live region, plus the header the sender must send. Only the warning sentence is an alert, so a screen reader does not read the secret aloud. On a loopback origin it says a sender elsewhere needs an address it can reach. The secret lives only in the panel's state and is dropped on "I have saved it" (focus returns to the create form) or unmount. The list never carries it: WebhookStore masks the token to a 4-character hint (agents/core/webhooks.py:842).
(3) Detail pane: clicking a hook expands its trigger URL, auth header (with the token hint), calls, last call and creation time, the deliveries its event list skipped and the last event skipped, and an editor for its event list and prompt template (H153). The row shows target_type:target, an HMAC or token badge, an on/off badge and an event-count badge.
(4) Delete with confirmation: "delete…" arms an inline confirmation that explains the sender's credential dies with the hook and moves focus to "delete for good", which sends DELETE; "keep it" returns focus to "delete…". Each row button's accessible name includes the hook's name. A row's buttons are held while its call is pending, and every switch or delete reloads the list whatever the hub answered: a hook already deleted elsewhere is reported as gone ("ci was already deleted", "ci no longer exists") and its row disappears, with focus moved to the create form; a refused delete keeps the confirmation and says why. A per-hook on/off switch (PATCH, H153) is offered as the reversible alternative.
(5) Governance: creating, switching and deleting a hook each write a SecurityEvent (_audit_webhook, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:203, called at agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:253, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:278 and agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:290). It names the hook id, the target as a JSON string (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:197), so a target cannot pass its own text off as the row's id or flags, and the signed and enabled flags as the store reads them, never the token or signing secret. A delete of an unknown id writes no webhook audit row (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:289) and answers 404 "webhook not found" (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:292). Since #1247 the admin guard's own auth telemetry (AUTH_SUCCESS and AUTH_FAILURE rows) lands in the same audit log, so the backend tests set those rows aside before counting webhook rows (_action_events, tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:266); an unknown switch adds none (tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:322) and a repeated delete adds none (tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:331).

The receiver-disabled banner: when the receiver switch (H153, the setting webhooks.receiver_enabled) is off, the panel's receiver row says every delivery is refused until it is switched back on (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:478). The restart-gateway banner is not needed: a delivery sees the switch at most a second old (at once after a write in this process), and hook CRUD is served live; the receiver row says so. Not built, and not part of this row: a `nerva webhooks` CLI verb (critic note 7 places it with H409, as `nerva webhooks inbound|outbound`) and a mobile screen.

reviews.summary: The HUD's keyboard shortcuts live in one registry, as in Hermes. frontend/src/shortcuts.ts defines every action once (ACTIONS: id, category, label, default chord, scope): the ten mode keys, World (w), the Console (`), Ambient (a), Cinema (m) and its three stages (o, n, b, scope cinema), focus the message box (/), the command palette (mod+k) and the Keyboard Shortcuts panel (mod+/). app.tsx (World's key included: WorldAwareApp passes onWorld and shares the live overrides through useShortcutOverrides) and the cinema overlay in shell.tsx dispatch through matchAction over bindings(overrides) instead of literal key maps, and every key hint (palette, top bar, World, Console, cinema stages) is read from the registry (chordOf, displayChord). A matched action takes the key from the browser (preventDefault); Shift+letter falls back to the bare letter unless it is bound itself. frontend/src/shortcuts-panel.tsx is the panel mod+/ opens: categories Navigation, View, Composer and Session with search (searchBindings); click a chord to record a new one ("Press a key…", Esc cancels, a lone modifier keeps listening; chordFromEvent, rebind); the palette and the panel take only a chord held with Ctrl/⌘ or Alt (acceptsChord), fire in an input only then (firesInInputs), and the palette always has a Keyboard shortcuts entry, so no rebinding can lock the panel out; Space is spelled "space", and a chord with no key is refused on record and on read; Esc closes the panel without closing what lies beneath; per-binding reset and Reset all (resetBinding); an "Also bound to X" note when two actions share a chord (conflictsFor). Overrides persist per viewer in localStorage under hud.shortcuts, validated on read (readOverrides, loadOverrides, saveOverrides), and survive storage that is off. Governance: defineActions refuses any action whose id, category or label names an approval, a decision, an accept, reject, deny or consent (FORBIDDEN_TARGET), so no chord can reach a Decision Inbox action. Tests: frontend/src/test/shortcuts.test.tsx (25), app-routing.test.tsx (+14: panel, rebinding, persistence, World, composer focus, the Space and Ctrl+Space lockout, the palette entry, the typing guard, preventDefault, World behind the panel, storage off, live hints, Esc beneath, Cinema), cinema.test.tsx (+1: rebound stage keys); voice-orb and briefing-wall expect the registry's stage titles; 38 mutants, 36 killed, 2 equivalent; the review round's 19 mutants, all killed (4 by tests added after a first pass). reviews.summary:
Archived chats exist, as in Hermes. CheckpointManager.set_archived stamps or clears archived_at in a session's metadata without creating a session. get_sessions(archived=...) filters on it in SQL, read only from valid JSON, so the limit counts only the view asked for. agents/core/routers/sessions.py serves several routes. GET /sessions leaves archived chats out; ?archived=true lists only them, each row with archived_at. POST /sessions/{id}/archive and /unarchive (user_guard) are 404 for an unknown session and 400 for an invalid id. Resuming a chat through POST /sessions/resume unarchives it. agents/core/session_archive.py holds the rest. run_auto_archive archives sessions whose ended_at, else started_at, is older than memory.auto_archive_days (0 = off, at most 3650) and never touches the active one; it runs as the archive phase of the hourly, interval-gated data lifecycle sweep (SchedulerService.schedule_retention), which replaced the separate 03:40 job; pinned chats are never auto-archived. DELETE /sessions/{id}?confirm=DELETE (admin_guard) holds the session's turn lease (409 session_busy) and the memory locks. It refuses the chat in use (409), a chat another chat continues (409 has_continuations), and an id that is not a session or whose snapshot is not this session's (404). delete_session first writes an encrypted, fsynced, read-back backup (the backup cipher, key under JARVIS_KEY_DIR) of the session's rows (session, checkpoints, clock, continuation seed, history binding, foreign-import receipt), transcript snapshot and log (unreadable ones byte for byte), compaction archive, checklist and note. The backup goes to <data root>-forget-archives/sessions/<id>-<stamp>.json.enc, outside the data root, keeping the newest JARVIS_SESSION_BACKUP_KEEP=10. Only then does it delete them and clear the live conversation, with the chat's turn embeddings (VectorStore.remove_where; 503 recall_unavailable if the store cannot) and with secure_delete plus a WAL truncate. Facts already extracted into the knowledge graph, and the audit log, are not touched. A backup that does not land raises backup_failed and deletes nothing. The file work runs off the event loop. The HUD SessionsPanel (frontend/src/panels/sessions.tsx) has chats and archived tabs, archive, unarchive and a two-step "delete permanently" that names the backup. llm.project_dir only sets the folder whose convention files H594 reads (project_context.start_dir); file tools (FileScope.resolve, list_dir, search_files) and the terminal cwd still resolve relative paths from the first file root, and the setting's label says so. Tests: tests/test_h218_archived_chats.py (74), frontend/src/test/sessions-archive.test.tsx (7). At the original build a todo_none mutant (the backup's checklist dropped) survived all 39 tests; the review round pins it, with 16 targeted mutants of its fixes all killed. reviews.summary: The HUD's language control is now a list, not a two-way toggle. frontend/src/data.ts:283-286 defines LANGUAGES, the languages the HUD has full I18N tables for (English and Romanian, each with its own-language label and a text direction). The TopBar globe button is a menu button (LangMenu, frontend/src/shell.tsx:91-142) that opens a radio list over LANGUAGES with the active language checked and each row tagged with its own lang. It supports the keyboard pattern: ArrowDown/ArrowUp on the globe open it, arrows wrap, Home/End jump, Enter/Space or a click choose, Escape returns focus to the globe, and a press elsewhere or Tab closes it. The command palette carries one 'Language · <name>' row per language with the active one ticked, in place of the old 'Toggle language EN / RO' row (frontend/src/shell.tsx:413-414). There is no separate Appearance settings panel in the HUD frontend (the only 'Appearance' mention outside tests and the workspace app is the comment at frontend/src/shell.tsx:382 saying the palette is the control surface); font, accent, look, density, motion, scanline and dot grid are all chosen from the palette, so the Language rows there are this HUD's Appearance language row. The language is now a real appearance preference: 'lang' is a member of the client option table (frontend/src/appearance.ts:11-12), of the server option table whose codes mirror LANGUAGES (agents/core/appearance.py:17-18) and of the PUT body model of the preferences endpoint (agents/core/routers/preferences.py:24). It is cached locally, queued offline as an ordinary edit, and synced with the same revisioned document as the other display choices, so a second browser of the same owner picks it up; an untranslated code is coerced to 'en' by the server. App reads and sets it through that preference (frontend/src/app.tsx:105-108), sets the document lang and dir and keeps writing hud.lang for the still-served v1 shell once the first hydration has finished (frontend/src/app.tsx:233-239), and adopts a language change made by the v1 shell (jarvis:locale_changed or a hud.lang storage event) when the code is a known one (frontend/src/app.tsx:242-251). A legacy hud.lang that holds a translated, non-default code is journalled once as an explicit edit so a configured server document answering 'en' cannot revert the owner's old choice, and a plain 'en' is never uploaded (frontend/src/appearance.ts:62-77 and frontend/src/appearance.ts:85-88). Tests pin all of this: frontend/src/test/language-menu.test.tsx:25-34 ties LANGUAGES to the I18N tables, frontend/src/test/language-menu.test.tsx:44-57 and frontend/src/test/language-menu.test.tsx:59-74 pin the menu roles, checked state and keyboard flow, frontend/src/test/language-menu.test.tsx:111-123 pins switching strings and document lang with a single saved PUT, frontend/src/test/language-menu.test.tsx:160-175 and frontend/src/test/language-menu.test.tsx:177-187 pin the legacy adoption and no double upload, frontend/src/test/language-menu.test.tsx:189-200 pins following the v1 shell, and frontend/src/test/language-menu.test.tsx:202-210 pins the palette rows end to end; frontend/src/test/palette-tweaks.test.tsx:59-66 pins the palette rows and their choose-by-code action; tests/test_appearance_preferences.py:138-145 pins the server round trip and the coercion of an unknown code (its defaults document at tests/test_appearance_preferences.py:33 carries lang). Honest limits: only English and Romanian are offered, because those are the only translated tables (adding a language is a data change in LANGUAGES, the I18N tables and the server option tuple, which is kept in step by hand); the list is not searchable and there is no native-script flag or locale detection; Hermes's literal Settings page does not exist here and this is verified only by the component tests under jsdom, not in a real browser or with a screen reader. Re-read 2026-10-24 (batch 4): the globe toggle became a language list menu, the palette gained per-language rows, and the language joined the synced appearance preferences with legacy hud.lang adoption and test coverage.

reviews.summary:
Hermes' "what can it do right now" view is here: one read-only answer, for one agent as seen by one principal, built from the code a turn runs and served on three surfaces. agents/core/inspector.py holds it; build_inspector (:108) returns up to five sections (SECTIONS, :63). (1) Views. VIEWS (:56) names the five tool-profile postures: the owner and a guest on the HUD (owner, guest), the owner and a stranger on an external channel (inbound-owner, inbound; Telegram stands for every channel, under the inbound action origin a real channel turn has) and no human (internal). The look binds that principal and origin in a task of its own (:125), so nothing it binds, and nothing the runtime notes while resolving the offer, outlives it. (2) status (_status, :155): version, the backend and model the router serves, the local model's state through project_llm_status, the transcript budget llm.tool_loop_context_tokens (0 reads as 75 % of the model window), the tool loop and safe mode. (3) tools (_tools, :194): the tool runtime's own resolved offer for the agent under that principal (_resolve_offer: registry or the capability registry's view, job toolset, posture, the agent's tools: list, the shared-session rule), not the raw registry. Each row says whether the tool is gated and whether its output is fenced as untrusted, with the description cut to DESCRIPTION_CHARS (160, :65). The withheld names are listed, a resolver failure offers nothing, and loop_enabled says whether the model sees any of them (with the loop off they are what the posture would offer). (4) skills (_skills, :215): the flat command rows prompt_catalog returns under that principal and that offer (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4062), or none when llm.skills_in_prompt is off. Since H326 these rows are no longer exactly what the prompt carries: the prompt renders the category-grouped index from SkillLoader.prompt_index (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1780), which applies the same gate but also lists skills that have no command (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1795-1796); Agent.build_prompt prefers that index over the flat rows (agents/core/agent.py:860-866). (5) mcp (_mcp, :225): each server's transport, trust tier, transport-aware liveness (is_connected, so an HTTP server reads connected; a probe that raises is down) and visible tools, with no URL or command line. (6) system_prompt (_prompt, :253): the agent's system prompt and the user part Agent.build_prompt sends for an empty user message: persona, agent context, the core-memory block, the runtime, language and grounding rails and the skills block (the grouped index, plus any skills the session loaded in earlier turns; the preview renders that carry without counting a turn, ageing a load or marking anything carried, agents/core/inspector.py:264-272). tokens (:288) estimates what that fixed part costs every turn before history. The texts are masked by the log redactor (SecretRedactionFilter; nothing is shown when it cannot load, _redactor :73) and capped together at PROMPT_CAP_BYTES (64 KiB, :64) on a character boundary. The core block is read with freeze=False (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3820, documented at :3748, read by the prompt builder at :3915-3916): the frozen block when a turn froze one, else a fresh render that is not kept, so a look never fixes the day's snapshot. (7) Surfaces. GET /api/admin/inspector?agent=&view=&section= (agents/core/routers/status.py:158, admin-guarded; 404 for an unknown agent, 400 naming the views or sections, 503 before the hub is up). nerva inspect [agent] [--as VIEW] [--section tools|skills|prompt|mcp|status] [--json] (cmd_inspect, agents/cli/nerva.py:1794; render_inspector :1317) prints the same payload section by section, or as it came. The HUD's Inspector panel (frontend/src/panels/inspector.tsx, Console → Admin) reads the same route with a status line, an As switch and folding sections. Tests: tests/test_inspector.py (47) builds a partial orchestrator over the coordinator's real ToolRPC registry. It covers the guest's tools equal to ToolProfileResolver's set and not the registry, every view's posture and bindings, the agent's list, the marks and the cut, the loop off, a failing resolver, an unwired runtime, the skills, the prompt (skills block, core memory, rails, empty message, tokens), the unfrozen core block, masking, the withheld prompt, the 64 KiB cap on a split character, no leaked binding, MCP liveness, the status line and safe mode, section order, the route (payload, defaults, refusals, admin token, guard snapshot, 503) and the CLI (--json equal to the payload, rendering, --section, the loop-off line, the tree, one list of views and sections). frontend/src/panels/inspector.test.tsx has 7. 82 mutants: 79 caught, ten after survivors got cases. reviews.summary:
Nerva copies Hermes's setup.runtime_check into the owner's terminal. The hub resolves the route with the same llm_router.select_backend call a Jarvis turn makes (agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:296) and names its verdict: a local provider/model pair must be resident, and a cloud route (Gemini, Claude, or the cloud-compatible adapter set by llm.compatible_provider) counts only when the router handed back the very backend that route names (agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:145, agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:334-343), and (H380) unless its provider refuses the key that route would use; a provider that says nothing about the key reads unknown, and a 429 stays runnable. A real HybridRouter pins this for the local, cloud-flash, claude and both cloud-compatible paths (tests/test_first_run_command_center.py:536). `nerva doctor` (and `python scripts/doctor.py`) adds the advisory runtime_resolves row: one GET of /api/onboarding/command-center at the hub `nerva status` reads (scripts/doctor.py:338), run only after /readyz answered at that same address and otherwise reported as skip, never ok (scripts/doctor.py:621-625). It sends one credential, the user token when both are set and the admin token only to a hub on this machine, decided by its address (scripts/doctor.py:589-596, scripts/doctor.py:542), never prints it, and is ok only on a ready verdict that names the route, provider and model (scripts/doctor.py:672-676). A refused token, a reply cut off mid-body, a listener that does not speak HTTP, a bad URL or an odd resident list is a named warn, not a traceback (scripts/doctor.py:652-657; tests/test_doctor.py:433, tests/test_doctor.py:458). `nerva status` now labels the old any-model state 'resident' and adds a runnable: line from the same verdict (agents/cli/nerva.py:968, agents/cli/nerva.py:1143; tests/test_nerva_cli.py:282); a timeout or reset on that read shows 'unknown — hub_unreachable' and the rest of the status still prints (agents/cli/nerva.py:976-981; tests/test_nerva_cli.py:346). A reply cut off mid-body or a garbled status line on any hub read is HubUnavailable, so `nerva status` reports an unreachable hub instead of a traceback (agents/cli/client.py:187, tests/test_nerva_cli.py:200). Both tools dial a wildcard bind (0.0.0.0, ::) over loopback (agents/cli/client.py:61). An end-to-end test drives both terminal checks against the real app (tests/test_first_run_command_center.py:593). Diagnostics stay local: the redacted bundle is served over one admin GET (agents/core/routers/support.py:21), and neither module imports a network client (tests/test_support_bundle.py:75), so the share_nous upload stays refused. The projects/workspaces model was skipped by decision. Known limits the row does not require: the verdict is for the route a short Jarvis chat takes; and a cloud route is judged by the router's own selection, not by a live call. reviews.summary:
Nerva now knows which surface holds each microphone. A surface arms only if the owner allowed its kind; one device's microphone has one holder at a time; and arming, pausing, resuming and stopping carry the surface's identity and are audited. This is the adaptation's missing concept, on top of the voice primitives that already existed (wake word, push-to-talk and hands-free capture, TTS, STT, capabilities, and H222's listening indicator). The lease table is agents/core/voice/mic.py (MicArbiter, agents/core/voice/mic.py:93; one process-wide ARBITER, agents/core/voice/mic.py:232).
(1) Surfaces and devices. A surface is kind:client: host:hub (the hub's own wake-word pipeline), hud:<tab> or mobile:<device> (ARMABLE, agents/core/voice/mic.py:39). A Wyoming satellite has its own microphone and is not armed here. A lease is for one device. host is the machine the hub runs on, and a browser that the route sees on loopback shares it. The route decides that from the address a trusted proxy vouches for (_mic_device, agents/core/routers/voice.py:527), so a LAN client cannot claim to be local. Otherwise a browser gets remote:hud:<tab>, and every phone gets mobile:<device>.
(2) One holder per device. A second surface arming a held device is refused, naming the holder (MicRefused mic_busy, agents/core/voice/mic.py:49; HTTP 409). With take_over, it pauses the holder and tells it (on_change, agents/core/voice/mic.py:144). A pause frees the device (agents/core/voice/mic.py:199). A resume asks again, both for consent and for the device's holder (agents/core/voice/mic.py:212). A stop releases the lease (agents/core/voice/mic.py:221).
(3) Consent. A kind arms only if the setting voice.mic_surfaces allows it (allowed_kinds, agents/core/voice/mic.py:59). The setting is a declared tags setting whose values are validated against host, hud and mobile (agents/core/settings_db.py:257, agents/core/settings_db.py:1170). The default is hud and mobile (DEFAULT_ALLOWED, agents/core/voice/mic.py:40): surfaces someone uses on purpose. The hub's always-on listener needs host added. So VoiceChannel.start (agents/core/channels/voice.py:29) opens the host microphone only with a lease. Before this, it started at boot with no check. It stops the pipeline when taken over and starts it again when given back (_on_lease, agents/core/channels/voice.py:48). Withdrawn consent ends a lease at its next renewal.
(4) Leases lapse. A browser or phone lease lapses LEASE_SECONDS (45, agents/core/voice/mic.py:42) after its last renewal (_expire_locked, agents/core/voice/mic.py:108). The host pipeline's lease does not lapse. The table holds at most 32 leases.
(5) Audit. Every arm, take-over, pause, stop and refusal is one audit row naming the surface and the device. A renewal is not.
(6) Routes, all user-guarded. GET /api/voice/mic answers who holds each device, the paused leases and the allowed kinds (agents/core/routers/voice.py:548). POST /api/voice/mic/arm (agents/core/routers/voice.py:557) takes hud or mobile and answers 403 or 409. /pause, /resume and /stop act on a lease by name (agents/core/routers/voice.py:576, agents/core/routers/voice.py:587, agents/core/routers/voice.py:601).
(7) The HUD. The voice loop arms its lease before getUserMedia (frontend/src/voice.ts:414; armMic, frontend/src/mic-lease.ts:47) and renews it every 20 s (frontend/src/voice.ts:434). It releases the lease on every end of the loop (frontend/src/voice.ts:135). If a renewal is refused, it stops and says who took the microphone. Only a hub refusal blocks: a hub that cannot answer does not. The loop offers take over (takeOver, frontend/src/voice.ts:454; the voice pill, frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:256). The voice settings list the holders, with pause, resume and stop (MicLeases, frontend/src/mic-leases.tsx:17).
Tests: tests/test_h247_mic_lease.py has 27. They cover consent, kinds, client and device names, withdrawn consent, a conflict and a take-over, renewal, lapse, pause and resume, stop, the bound, status, the numbers, the setting and its reading, the voice channel's lease, loopback against LAN against a phone, the routes and their guard. frontend/src/test/mic-lease.test.tsx has 10: arm before the mic, a named holder and take-over, no consent, an unreachable hub, renewal and loss, a cancelled start, an unmount, a click handler, the pill and the settings list.

reviews.summary:
A settings reset now shows what it will change, never touches a secret and can be undone, and the HUD marks every setting that differs from its default. Hermes' config-reset and defaults surface is covered, on top of H157's search, secret-free export, dry-run import and per-category reset. (1) Defaults. Every declared row that is not a secret carries its declared default (agents/core/settings_db.py:746, in _mark_overlay :731, used by GET /api/admin/settings and each category read). A secret carries none. The Settings panel marks a row whose value, or staged edit, differs from its default ("changed", with the default in its tooltip); a ↺ button stages the default and the usual save writes it through the validated PUT (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2996). (2) A preview before any reset. plan_reset (agents/core/settings_db.py:1510) computes what a reset of one category, or of every category, would write: each declared setting that is neither a secret nor a route-only row (settings_db.ROUTE_ONLY: the skill switches, the voice command providers, the security data-handling acknowledgments) and whose stored value is not its default. POST /api/admin/settings/{category}/reset and POST /api/admin/settings/reseed take {"dry_run": true} and answer the changes as current → default without writing anything (agents/core/routers/admin.py:391, :430; _dry_run_asked, :379; only a JSON true, in a body of at most 4 KB). The changes use describe_changes, so a credential-shaped value shows as (hidden). Arming the reset in the HUD asks for that preview and lists it, and counts the settings kept (secrets and route-only rows, all labelled secrets) and names the settings the posture still forces (ResetPreview, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:64; ResetCategory, :92). (3) The reseed no longer deletes the store. It used to run DELETE FROM settings, wiping every setting, secrets included, with no preview and no way back. It is now the per-category reset over every category: secrets and route-only rows are kept (and named), rows nothing declares are left, it takes a JSON request from this origin only (415/403 otherwise, as H157's writes), and it is audited with the settings that moved (agents/core/routers/admin.py:430). The v1 admin page sends it as JSON (agents/web/static/admin.js:1520). The HUD gets "reset every category…" with the same preview (ResetAll, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:115). (4) Undo. reset_settings (agents/core/settings_db.py:1550) writes the defaults and records what it replaced in settings_resets (:120) in the same transaction, keeping the last 20 (RESETS_KEPT, :1516). POST /api/admin/settings/undo (agents/core/routers/admin.py:461; undo_last_reset, agents/core/settings_db.py:1607) puts back the latest reset not yet undone. A setting changed since that reset, one its declaration no longer accepts, or one no longer declared is left as it is and named in skipped. The undo is audited, and the listeners hear every value a reset or an undo writes, so the webhook receiver switch follows it. GET /api/admin/settings/resets (agents/core/routers/admin.py:91; list_resets, agents/core/settings_db.py:1594) lists the resets, newest first, naming settings but never their values. The HUD shows "last reset: <scope> · N settings · <time>" with "undo…" (UndoReset, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:135). Every reset and undo in the HUD is a two-step ConfirmAction at the REVERSIBLE tier (H168). Adapted from the row's ask: the reseed does not go through the approval queue's irreversible tier, because it is no longer irreversible. It keeps secrets, previews, and can be undone. Routing it through the queue would need a new kernel action kind for it, and none is declared (agents/core/kernel/registry.py's one settings kind is H613's settings.voice_command). Tests: tests/test_settings_defaults_undo.py has 24: defaults on rows and none for secrets; the plan (what moves, never a secret); a recorded reset and its undo; nothing moved means nothing recorded; the listeners; a setting changed since, no longer valid or no longer declared left as it is; latest first; the list keeps 20 and names no values; everything reset with secrets and undeclared rows kept; and the routes (admin-only, dry run, a hidden credential, JSON only with a 4 KB bound, the reseed's preview, audit and undo, nothing to undo 404, and /resets not taken for a category). frontend/src/test/settings-reset-undo.test.tsx has 7. reviews.summary: H270 stays PARTIAL; the triage's "already equivalent" does not survive contact with the code, and this re-read retires three claims the row had carried since before H502 (#1174 moved the hash while the text stood still) plus one the text was about to inherit. Hermes' contract has two halves and Nerva has only one of them. Outbound (what a child inherits) is genuinely stronger than Hermes and is tested: scrub_child_env (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:172-210) is default-deny with SAFE_ENV_PREFIXES (:17-33) plus the three-name JARVIS_CHILD_ALLOWED_ENV (:47-51), covered by tests/test_environment_primitives.py:62,90; STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST (agents/core/mcp/client.py:166-178) with stdio_env_baseline (:245-280) drops a credential-shaped name even when it is on the static list (:275, _SECRET_LIKE :174-176), covered by tests/test_mcp_transports.py:351 — and since H502 the baseline is the DEFAULT, not an opt-in: stdio_env_baseline_enabled() returns env_flag(STDIO_ENV_BASELINE_FLAG, True) (:179-190; flag :90 "Default ON"), docs/FLAGS.md says "on by default since H502" (its MCP defaults block, the JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE entry and the flag table row), and tests/test_mcp_transports.py:386-421 pins unset-flag → OPENAI_API_KEY withheld and =0 → full inherit (the row previously cited :395-399 as pinning the opposite; that was the pre-#1174 test, which at 45be62bd read "Flag off (default): historical behaviour — inherit everything"). The outbound allowlist's one deliberate exception is the owner's own: a name listed in JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV passes even when credential-shaped (:256-260, :272-274; tests :449-503) — owner-declared and host-wide, not an inbound gate. What #1179 changed here is disclosure, not policy: the module docstring (:17-39) now names the filesystem as a second recovery route for a same-UID child (cwd defaults to the hub's, so open(".env") reaches the file the keys came from), cwd_secret_files (:215-242) reports a readable .env/.env.local in the child's cwd, and _merged_env (:561-572) logs a WARNING "withholding is undercut" (:567) beside the INFO count, filenames only — pinned by tests :830-853 and :854-890. Nerva has no write-side policy for environment-variable names — the row's deliverable (a declared-names allowlist, depends_on "the key registry") does not exist, and the row defers it rather than excluding it. #1179 changed nothing on this row's subject: its client.py change is an outbound disclosure (cwd_secret_files :215-242 and the "withholding is undercut" WARNING in _merged_env :561-572), not a name policy or a writer. 1. THE REGISTRY (the row's core item, blocked on its stated dependency). No general env-name registry exists and no `config.write` capability kind exists in agents/core/capability_actions.py. The one writer that persists env-var names today, H595's llm.execute_code_env_passthrough setting and skill declarations, is gated by code_env._passable_name (agents/core/code_env.py:84-92, enforced at agents/core/settings_db.py:1004-1010), a denylist that still passes NODE_PATH, EDITOR, VISUAL, PAGER, BROWSER and GIT_SSH_COMMAND; owed there: refuse those names too, or replace the denylist with the declared-names registry. Of Hermes' hijack names, PATH, SHELL (agents/core/mcp/client.py:167), NODE_PATH (:171) and PATH, SHELL, PYTHONPATH (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:18, :27, :30) are named as members of the two OUTBOUND allowlists, and EDITOR is exercised at tests/test_nerva_import.py:165 (pinned dropped at tests/test_nerva_import.py:825). Design consequence: the outbound lists cannot double as the write-side registry — they deliberately admit the plumbing names Hermes forbids on write — so the registry is a separate, inbound-only list. When any env/config writer lands, that allowlist must land in the SAME PR, refusing an undeclared name before authorization — the shape of agents/core/capability_actions.py:147-151 refusing missing_inputs before the authorizer at :159-160.

2. THE MCP `env` BOUNDARY IS UNREFUSED (shippable now; the "untested" half closed with #1174). MCPServerConfig (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:145-156) sets no `model_config`, so pydantic's default extra="ignore" makes `POST /api/admin/mcp {"env": {"LD_PRELOAD": "/tmp/evil.so"}}` return 200 and silently drop the key instead of refusing it — reproduced end to end at HEAD through TestClient (200 {"ok": true}; stored MCPServer.env == {}; to_config() has no env key). 3. PER-SERVER `env` BYPASSES THE ALLOWLIST IN BOTH BRANCHES. stdio_env_baseline applies overrides unfiltered after the allowlist loop (agents/core/mcp/client.py:283-284; docstring :253 "Explicit per-server overrides always win"), and the legacy branch does `merged = os.environ.copy(); merged.update(self.env)` with no filter (:575-576). reviews.summary:
Built in #1207, then fixed after eight adversarial reviews. The first found the stdlib parser was python-dotenv's pre-1.2.3 grammar, while the lock pins 1.2.3: the doctor could print value material as key names, a named-pipe .env was no longer loaded, and a data home named in the repo .env was no longer followed. The second found that the doctor sent the admin credential to whatever answered at the hub address, that more keys than serve.py's four were read before any .env was loaded, and that a one-case line of value material could still be printed as a name. The third found that the start itself read 31 more names before the load (so ten .env knobs, the audit key and the public-profile gate among them, were shown as in effect and were not), that two read-again entries were false, and that the MCP transport ignored a user token kept in .env. The fourth found that the MCP transport and the HTTP user guard asked different questions, so a lapsed or revoked user credential locked every route but left MCP open to a local caller; that the coordinator built its Orchestrator before the load, so its audit rows went unkeyed beside the hub's keyed ones; that an IPv6 bind (JARVIS_HOST=::1) escaped both loopback checks; and that the CLI sent the admin token to any hub. The fifth found that the admin tier still trusted a loopback caller once no admin credential was active, so after the owner revoked every credential a local process with no token could mint a fresh user token over HTTP and reopen the user routes and MCP (older than H273, but it falsified this row's credential sentence); that a managed user token that had expired counted as never configured; that the CLI asked the owner to set an admin token it had withheld; and that the supervisor wrote its respawns apart from a run-log named in .env. The sixth found that the sentence about minting did not hold where no admin credential was ever configured, that the offline recovery wrote a tokens.db the hub never read when the data home was named only in a .env (and a packaged build had none to run), that the CLI's withheld message fired on refusals https would not fix, and that a named-pipe .env still split the run-log. The seventh found that the supervisor now told its child a default the hub never read (a named-pipe .env hid the runtime from the brief), that the packaged recovery revived env tokens that had been rotated away or revoked, and that the CLI still asked for a token that was set. The eighth found that the packaged recovery still missed a token in the start environment or a moved data home, and left a LAN-bound app unable to start, and that the new hint called a valid user token refused on an admin verb and proposed a rotate that revoked the owner's working admin token. Every effective configuration key now carries the layer that supplied it, the note says when a .env value is not in effect, and every surface the row names reports names and layers only.

The table. load_layered_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:365) loads the files. Precedence: the process environment (the shell, a systemd EnvironmentFile, docker -e), then the repo .env, then the data-home .env, and the first layer to set a key wins (override=False). It keeps python-dotenv's behaviour:
- Each file is read once, whether a regular file or a named pipe, the way python-dotenv reads it. 1Password mounts a .env as a FIFO.
- The load is python-dotenv's public load_dotenv on the text that was read. The names come from python-dotenv's own parser (dotenv.parser.parse_stream), which logs nothing, so a bad line is warned about once. No private python-dotenv API is used.
- PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED is checked before each layer, as python-dotenv checks it on every call, so a repo .env that sets it stops the data-home layer. Its spellings are python-dotenv's own, kept in env_config.py, the repo's one home for env-flag parsing (agents/core/env_config.py:112); a parity test pins them against python-dotenv's own switch.
- The data home is a callable resolved after the repo layer is loaded, so a JARVIS_USER_HOME set in the repo .env names it, as before. A first-run home is scaffolded before its .env is read.
- A second load in one process keeps a file's attribution only while the environment still holds the value that load set (a private digest, never the value), and works out afresh what the files shadow. The same file as both layers is read once.
- It records which layer supplied each key, by diffing the environment around each file, and the lower layers that also define it (shadowed: their value is ignored). That answers "why is my .env change not applied?".
- files() records what the load did with each file: its kind (file, fifo, absent, the same file as the repo .env, or disabled), whether it is present, and whether it was read.

provenance() (agents/core/env_provenance.py:541) is the queryable in-process table; a key that appeared after the load reads as set while running.

The hub loads first. load_hub_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:463) is the hub's own load, once per process, so a named pipe is read once:
- serve.py calls it before it builds the server and runs its guards (serve.py:337). The server's host, port, log level and shutdown timeout, the posture guards and the bind guard see a .env value, so a token in .env satisfies the bind guard.
- The lifespan calls it before its boot guards (agents/web.py:476). The data home, logging, the orchestrator with its audit log, memory and budget ledger, and the router's detect() all read after it: the audit key, the public-profile seed gate, turn embeddings, the budget, the router's URLs and cloud keys in a .env are in effect. The boot guards, the front door among them, judge the loaded environment, so the late re-check was removed.
- The coordinator (the systemd jarvis-runtime unit, compose runtime-coordinator) calls it first in run(), before its run-log path and cycle (scripts/coordinator.py:173), and again, idempotently, before it builds its Orchestrator (scripts/coordinator.py:84): it shares the hub's data root, so it keys the audit chain the hub keys. The supervisor that spawns it (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py) does not load, since its child would then read every file key as the process environment's; it reads the run-log path through hub_value (agents/core/env_provenance.py:490), the value the files give without loading them, and it hands its child only a path it found (the process, or a regular .env), which the child's load does not override, so both write that one run-log (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py:84; review-H273g m4). A path in a named-pipe .env, which the supervisor never reads, is not handed down: the child reads the pipe as the hub does, so the cycles land where the brief reads them, and only the supervisor's own events stay in the default file (_child_env, scripts/runtime_supervisor.py:122; review-H273h m1). An empty value is unset on both ends. The reality-evidence harness does too (agents/core/observability/reality_evidence.py:183).
- agents/run.py, the REPL, loads before its logging and its imports (agents/run.py:21), so a log file or scanner pattern in .env is in effect.
- PluginManager.build asks for it too (agents/core/plugin_manager.py:255), for any other entry. scripts/install_smoke.py does not load before it builds its isolated hub (a temp data root, from the process environment); its PluginManager.build loads afterwards, as for any entry.
- Log redaction is imported first, so its switch stays the boot environment's alone: a .env cannot turn it off.

Keys read before the load. note_for (agents/core/env_provenance.py:526) flags what is still read before any file can be. That is what importing agents.web freezes or resolves: the ASGI root path, the rate limit, CORS, CSP, the router's auto-deep switch, the analytics cap, the graph's Neo4j defaults, the app and data roots, and the log-redaction switch (agents/core/env_provenance.py:60). A .env value for them is recorded but not in effect, and the note says to set it in the process environment.
- What locates the hub's own files (JARVIS_APP_ROOT, JARVIS_HOME, JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR) is never taken from a file (agents/core/env_provenance.py:69). A .env value would have split the stores between two roots. It is recorded and kept out of the environment, and its own note says so (agents/core/env_provenance.py:100).
- JARVIS_USER_HOME from the repo .env names the data home and its .env. When JARVIS_HOME is not set, the stores opened while the hub was imported stay under the default root, and its note says so (agents/core/env_provenance.py:72).
- Read again after the load, so a .env value is in effect (agents/core/env_provenance.py:93): DEV_MODE; the admin and user tokens (every guard reads them per request, the MCP transport included); the OAuth client ids; the trusted proxies.

The lists are measured, not declared:

The two false read-again entries are fixed:

The question is whether a credential was ever configured (_ever_configured, agents/web.py:109): an env token, active or superseded; a rotation or a revoke with --revoke-env, which leave the store's persistent flag; an issued token, live or expired. Only a hub that never had a credential of the tier trusts a localhost caller without one (for the exception, see Known limits).

Known limits:
- On Windows, key names are compared case-sensitively although the environment is not; that case is theoretical and not handled.
- A raw uvicorn start binds where uvicorn's own flags say. JARVIS_HOST there, from a file or from the shell alike, reaches the Host-header guard and the boot guard's bind check, which judges that value rather than the address uvicorn bound.
- In a process that loads more than once (tests), a value equal to one an earlier load set keeps that load's attribution. The hub loads once.
- JARVIS_USER_HOME set only in a .env, with no JARVIS_HOME, still splits the stores: what the hub opens while it is imported stays under the default root, and the rest follows the home (autonomy.db opens under both). Its note says so on the route, in the doctor and in the HUD. Moving either half would move an existing install's history, so it is left, and set in the process environment it does not split.
- The CLI sends the admin token to a hub on another machine when that hub is reached over https: the owner named that hub, and its admin verbs need it. The doctor, which only reads, never sends the admin token off this machine. Over plain http to another machine the admin verbs (the e-stop, approvals, tools, jobs) are refused, and the CLI says why.
- A box that never had an admin credential trusts a direct localhost caller as admin, whatever happened to its user tokens: after revoke user --revoke-env, or once a user token has lapsed, a local process still mints a user token. The user-token lock binds callers from other machines; revoke all --revoke-env closes it for this one too (pinned, review-H273g m1).
- A run-log path set only in a named-pipe .env reaches the coordinator and the hub, not the supervisor, which cannot read the pipe: its own spawned, child_exited and respawned events go to the default logs/runtime.jsonl, apart from the cycles. Setting the path in the process environment keeps them together.
- A token issued with token_store issue and deleted by a revoke without --revoke-env leaves no trace in the store, and so does anything that empties it (purge_expired, which nothing in the hub calls, a deleted tokens.db, a new data root), so that hub reads as never configured for its tier at its next start and trusts a localhost caller again (a running hub that saw the credential stays locked until then). Closing it needs a persistent flag in agents/core/security/token_store.py, the owner's security lane. A rotation, a revoke with --revoke-env, or an expired token keep the hub locked.
- A managed user token alone now guards this machine too (ENV-163): an install that has only a store token needs it in the HUD ("store in this browser"), the CLI, the doctor and nerva_mcp_stdio.py.
- Under a raw uvicorn start, uvicorn's own proxy knobs (FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, UVICORN_PROXY_HEADERS) are read before the app is imported, so a .env value for them is not in effect, while announce_trusted_proxies reports the file's value.
- A trailing-dot name (localhost., 127.1.) counts as this machine, though the resolver treats it as a DNS name; a resolver that answered it with another address would receive the admin token.
- The value-material shape misses uppercase hex, digitless base32 and short mixed ids, and withholds digit-bearing names with no underscore (contrived lines).
- The data home is scaffolded (its README, a .env copied from .env.example) before the boot guards run, so a start they refuse still writes it.
- Hub mode on this machine trusts the paths the hub names: a hub in a container names paths that do not exist on the host, and every plain custom key is then withheld with a reason that is false for it.
- The scan for the hub's reads misses computed and mapped names (a URL key built from a prefix, a budget key read through a mapping); both are declared in .env.example or carry the prefix today.
- JARVIS_HOST=0::0 or ::ffff:0.0.0.0 gives a URL judged not this machine (the proxy is used and the admin token withheld, the safe direction); JARVIS_HOST=localhost:9000 gives an invalid URL, as it did before.

The table. load_layered_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:365) loads the files. Precedence: the process environment (the shell, a systemd EnvironmentFile, docker -e), then the repo .env, then the data-home .env, and the first layer to set a key wins (override=False). It keeps python-dotenv's behaviour:
- Each file is read once, whether a regular file or a named pipe, the way python-dotenv reads it. 1Password mounts a .env as a FIFO.
- The load is python-dotenv's public load_dotenv on the text that was read. The names come from python-dotenv's own parser (dotenv.parser.parse_stream), which logs nothing, so a bad line is warned about once. No private python-dotenv API is used.
- PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED is checked before each layer, as python-dotenv checks it on every call, so a repo .env that sets it stops the data-home layer. Its spellings are python-dotenv's own, kept in env_config.py, the repo's one home for env-flag parsing (agents/core/env_config.py:112); a parity test pins them against python-dotenv's own switch.
- The data home is a callable resolved after the repo layer is loaded, so a JARVIS_USER_HOME set in the repo .env names it, as before. A first-run home is scaffolded before its .env is read.
- A second load in one process keeps a file's attribution only while the environment still holds the value that load set (a private digest, never the value), and works out afresh what the files shadow. The same file as both layers is read once.
- It records which layer supplied each key, by diffing the environment around each file, and the lower layers that also define it (shadowed: their value is ignored). That answers "why is my .env change not applied?".
- files() records what the load did with each file: its kind (file, fifo, absent, the same file as the repo .env, or disabled), whether it is present, and whether it was read.

provenance() (agents/core/env_provenance.py:541) is the queryable in-process table; a key that appeared after the load reads as set while running.

The hub loads first. load_hub_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:463) is the hub's own load, once per process, so a named pipe is read once:

Recovery is scripts/token_recover.py rotate admin on the box, which loads the hub's .env files first so it writes the tokens.db the hub reads, and says which (review-H273g m2); a packaged build first removes every JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN and JARVIS_USER_TOKEN from both places the app reads them, the data home's .env (wherever the home is) and the environment the app starts from, unsets JARVIS_HOST for the restart (the boot guard refuses a LAN bind with no token), then removes security/tokens.db under its data root (JARVIS_HOME and JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR named), because that file is also what records the rotations and revokes that superseded env tokens (docs/PACKAGING.md; review-H273h m2, review-H273i m1). The check lists the token table once per store: once a tier shows configured it stays so for that store (review-H273g n1). Only a hub that never had a credential of the tier trusts a localhost caller without one (for the exception, see Known limits).
- The OAuth routes use the plugin manager's copy of the OAuth module (agents/core/routers/oauth.py:36), which re-reads the client ids after the load.

Key names come from python-dotenv itself whenever it can be imported (text_keys, agents/core/env_provenance.py:202): every binding in file order, a rebound key each time. The stdlib port (_port_keys, agents/core/env_provenance.py:143) is 1.2.3's grammar and is the fallback for a broken install. A parity test pins it on 25 edge cases, including the BOM, escaped backslashes and a key rebound without "=". A seeded differential fuzz of 4,000 random files pins it too.

derive (agents/core/env_provenance.py:327) builds the same table offline. It follows a data home named in the repo .env, or built from ${VAR}, resolving every binding in file order as load_dotenv does: the environment wins over the file's earlier values, a rebound key takes its last value, and a last binding without "=" sets nothing (agents/core/env_provenance.py:294). It parses each file once, keyed on its size, times and inode, and never opens a named pipe.

Surfaces:
- GET /api/admin/env/sources (agents/core/routers/admin.py:564) is admin-guarded and no-store, at the same boundary as GET /api/admin/env. Each key comes with its layer, a label, the layers it overrides, whether /api/admin/env masks its value, and its note. It also names what the load did with each file (path, kind, present, read); values are never included.
- `nerva doctor`'s advisory config_sources check (scripts/doctor.py:891):
  - Reading the hub. It reads the running hub's own table when /readyz is ok, asking without a credential first. Every request to the hub goes over http or https, has a timeout, refuses a redirect, and never goes through a proxy to a hub on this machine (scripts/doctor.py:568). The hub address brackets an IPv6 bind (JARVIS_HOST=::1 gives http://[::1]:8080; scripts/doctor.py:352), and an unbracketed IPv6 address, whatever its first group (0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1 too), is read the way http.client dials it (scripts/doctor.py:526). The admin credential goes only to a hub on this machine, decided by its address rather than its spelling (127.0.0.2, 127.1, localhost., ::1 and ::ffff:127.0.0.1 count; scripts/doctor.py:542). config_sources sends it only after a refusal, and runtime_resolves only when no user token is set (scripts/doctor.py:584). Otherwise the doctor predicts the table from its own shell and says which of the two it did and why.
  - Which keys. It shows every key a .env file sets, and the shell's keys that the hub's code reads or that carry Nerva's prefixes. The hub's reads are found by reading agents/ and serve.py: helper calls, a bound mapping, *_ENV constants (private ones too), a pool's from_env names and a descriptor's *_env keyword (scripts/doctor.py:759).
  - Which names are printed. A .env name is printed when the hub reads it, .env.example declares it, it is an identifier with Nerva's prefix, or it is a plain one-case name with a value, an empty placeholder included (scripts/doctor.py:1005). Any other name is counted, never printed (withheld_env_names). That includes a name shaped like a digest, a seed or an access key id, whatever follows its "=" (scripts/doctor.py:777); a value that is only = padding; a PEM line; a mixed-case name; and a name with control characters.
  - Hub mode. On this machine it reads the files the hub names to tell names from value material. For a hub on another machine it shows only the names Nerva knows, and says why.
  - Other reports. It names a .env that is not UTF-8, which the hub's load fails on (env_not_utf8), and a named pipe it does not open. For each key it prints the .env values a higher layer overrides and the note. Any failure inside the check becomes a named reason, never a crash.
- The `nerva` CLI's client (agents/cli/client.py:116) follows the same transport rules: no redirect (urllib carried both tokens to wherever one pointed), no proxy to a hub on this machine, and http or https only. Its loopback rule is the doctor's, pinned equal over one table of spellings. It sends the admin token only to a hub on this machine or over https (agents/cli/client.py:156), never in clear text to another host, whether or not a user token is set; the user token goes to the hub it names. When it withheld the admin token and the hub refuses, it names that as one possible cause beside the user token, never as the only one (review-H273g m3). The hint reads the hub's own reason for the tier it wanted: a verb that needs the admin tier asks for JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN when only the user token is set, only a token of the wanted tier that was sent is named as refused, a hub with no token of the tier configured is named as such, and the recovery offered is the additive token_recover.py issue (rotate only for a leaked token, since it revokes every token of the tier; review-H273i m2); nerva status reads the same reason on its runnable and e-stop lines (_auth_hint, agents/cli/nerva.py:1048; review-H273h m3, review-H273i m2, n4).
- The settings plane: every row says default, set, undeclared, or unreadable (an encrypted secret whose key is lost) (value_source, agents/core/settings_db.py:708). A value a selected product posture puts in effect is named beside the stored one (in_effect, overlay). An unknown stored posture is off, and the posture is read in the listing's own connection; a stored row that is not JSON (the posture included) no longer reads as off: the whole store is validated when it is first opened and before every full listing (_require_readable_store, agents/core/settings_db.py:560), and the listing raises SettingsUnreadable instead (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:739). `nerva config list` prints both (agents/cli/nerva.py:1247).
- The HUD's Admin "API keys & secrets" list shows each key's layer, the layers it overrides and its note (hydrateAdminKeys, frontend/src/api/live.ts:205; frontend/src/modes3.tsx:261).

Hermes records provenance only for vault-supplied names, and its own notes ask for this per-key table; Nerva has it. Nerva has no managed or secret-source layer in the environment: vault secrets are injected at action time, not loaded into the environment.

Known limits:
- On Windows, key names are compared case-sensitively although the environment is not; that case is theoretical and not handled.
- A raw uvicorn start binds where uvicorn's own flags say. JARVIS_HOST there, from a file or from the shell alike, reaches the Host-header guard and the boot guard's bind check, which judges that value rather than the address uvicorn bound.
- In a process that loads more than once (tests), a value equal to one an earlier load set keeps that load's attribution. The hub loads once.
- JARVIS_USER_HOME set only in a .env, with no JARVIS_HOME, still splits the stores: what the hub opens while it is imported stays under the default root, and the rest follows the home (autonomy.db opens under both). Its note says so on the route, in the doctor and in the HUD. Moving either half would move an existing install's history, so it is left, and set in the process environment it does not split.
- The CLI sends the admin token to a hub on another machine when that hub is reached over https: the owner named that hub, and its admin verbs need it. The doctor, which only reads, never sends the admin token off this machine. Over plain http to another machine the admin verbs (the e-stop, approvals, tools, jobs) are refused, and the CLI says why.
- A box that never had an admin credential trusts a direct localhost caller as admin, whatever happened to its user tokens: after revoke user --revoke-env, or once a user token has lapsed, a local process still mints a user token. The user-token lock binds callers from other machines; revoke all --revoke-env closes it for this one too (pinned, review-H273g m1).
- A run-log path set only in a named-pipe .env reaches the coordinator and the hub, not the supervisor, which cannot read the pipe: its own spawned, child_exited and respawned events go to the default logs/runtime.jsonl, apart from the cycles. Setting the path in the process environment keeps them together.
- A token issued with token_store issue and deleted by a revoke without --revoke-env leaves no trace in the store, and so does anything that empties it (purge_expired, which nothing in the hub calls, a deleted tokens.db, a new data root), so that hub reads as never configured for its tier at its next start and trusts a localhost caller again (a running hub that saw the credential stays locked until then). Closing it needs a persistent flag in agents/core/security/token_store.py, the owner's security lane. A rotation, a revoke with --revoke-env, or an expired token keep the hub locked.
- A managed user token alone now guards this machine too (ENV-163): an install that has only a store token needs it in the HUD ("store in this browser"), the CLI, the doctor and nerva_mcp_stdio.py.
- Under a raw uvicorn start, uvicorn's own proxy knobs (FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, UVICORN_PROXY_HEADERS) are read before the app is imported, so a .env value for them is not in effect, while announce_trusted_proxies reports the file's value.
- A trailing-dot name (localhost., 127.1.) counts as this machine, though the resolver treats it as a DNS name; a resolver that answered it with another address would receive the admin token.
- The value-material shape misses uppercase hex, digitless base32 and short mixed ids, and withholds digit-bearing names with no underscore (contrived lines).
- The data home is scaffolded (its README, a .env copied from .env.example) before the boot guards run, so a start they refuse still writes it.
- Hub mode on this machine trusts the paths the hub names: a hub in a container names paths that do not exist on the host, and every plain custom key is then withheld with a reason that is false for it.
- The scan for the hub's reads misses computed and mapped names (a URL key built from a prefix, a budget key read through a mapping); both are declared in .env.example or carry the prefix today.
- JARVIS_HOST=0::0 or ::ffff:0.0.0.0 gives a URL judged not this machine (the proxy is used and the admin token withheld, the safe direction); JARVIS_HOST=localhost:9000 gives an invalid URL, as it did before.

JARVIS_SAFE_MODE=1, or `python serve.py --safe-mode`, which sets it before the hub is imported (apply_safe_mode_switch, serve.py:18), is the one flag, read at call time by one module (enabled, agents/core/safe_mode.py:147). The runtime (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py, which passes it to scripts/coordinator.py) takes --safe-mode too, since it runs heartbeats, owner jobs and agents on the same data root; deploy/systemd/README.md says to set JARVIS_SAFE_MODE=1 in the env file both units read and restart both. It leaves out the owner's layers (16 since H490, H594, H613, H464c, whose `company_mode` layer leaves the company-mode sweep out, and H592, whose `personality_overlays` layer keeps every /personality style overlay out of a turn (agents/core/cognition/personality_presets.py:270); LAYERS, agents/core/safe_mode.py:68). Approving a pending skill in safe mode signs it but says it loads on the next normal boot (loaded: false; agents/core/routers/skills.py:758). Verdict raised to equivalent at HEAD by the #1251 build lane (code verdict). All three parts of the contract are built and tested locally. (A) agents/core/host_identity.py is the one host detector. It is read by the prompt (environment_hint.detected_block, agents/core/environment_hint.py:76-82), the skill gates (agents/core/skills/visibility.py:84-88), the doctor's container-storage check (host_posture container_marker, agents/core/host_posture.py:247-250), GET /api/host/probe (agents/core/routers/host_probe.py:41), the HUD host-readiness card (frontend/src/panels/host-readiness.tsx) and `python -m agents.core.host_identity`. It covers container (JARVIS_CONTAINER override, Kubernetes, marker files and PID 1 cgroup, /run/systemd/container, $container), WSL, Termux, supervisor (s6, systemd with journal and watchdog, launchd), terminal and multiplexer as closed words, and a hashed machine id, which closes the gap the earlier remaining text named. _kind_word (agents/core/host_identity.py:212) maps only container-manager words to a kind, so 'wsl', 'proot' or any other word in /run/systemd/container or $container is not a container; detect_wsl (agents/core/host_identity.py:253) reads 'wsl' there as the WSL fact, so a WSL 2 host running systemd is reported as wsl2, not as a container. reviews.summary:
The owner declares which skills, plugins and MCP servers load at boot, and a plugin toggle survives a restart. Six declared settings rows (agents/core/settings_db.py:452-457), category `loadset`, hold comma lists: skills_disabled/skills_only, plugins_disabled/plugins_only, mcp_disabled/mcp_only, editable from the settings page and `nerva config set` (which says a loadset.* key or a plugin switch applies at the next start). A disabled name does not load; a non-empty only-list loads only what it names; the disabled list wins (permits, agents/core/load_set.py:96). A list is read at call time (declared, agents/core/load_set.py:74), trimmed, de-duplicated and bounded to 256 names of at most 128 characters without control characters (parse_names, agents/core/load_set.py:43), and an unreadable store narrows nothing. For plugins the settings page's existing per-plugin `plugins.<id>` switches, which nothing used to read, count too: an explicit off is off (agents/core/load_set.py:84). SkillLoader.discover reads the lists once per pass (agents/core/skills/loader.py:710-711) and a skill named by its registry name or its folder is not registered at all, before any quarantine row (agents/core/skills/loader.py:789); a registration from an earlier pass is taken out when a later pass denies it, the per-pass snapshot is cleared in a finally, and in safe mode (the owner folder unread) no declared name is reported as unknown. PermissionGate switches off the plugins the lists name when it is built (apply_load_set, agents/core/plugin_gate.py:709), and PluginManager.build drops them from orch.plugins before binding oracle_bridge and Argus (_drop_switched_off, agents/core/plugin_manager.py:373), so the probes, the dashboard and WorldView never reach a switched-off plugin. Each gate holds its own copies of the built-in manifests (agents/core/plugin_gate.py:703), so switching one off never reaches the module table or another gate, and the readers of a plugin's enabled state ask the live gate: CloudImageRuntime is wired with orch.permission_gate (_available, agents/core/cloud_image_runtime.py:542) and the capability board reads the gate's manifests (_plugin_records, agents/core/observability/capability_registry.py:155). The plugin toggle (toggle_plugin, agents/core/routers/plugins.py:99) keeps the choice in one place, the plugin's plugins.<id> settings switch when it has one and otherwise plugins_disabled; switched on, it leaves plugins_disabled and joins a declared plugins_only (persist_plugin, agents/core/load_set.py:140). It reads the lists fail-closed (read_setting), so an unreadable store is not overwritten, and answers `persisted` (false when the store refused or could not be read, the live toggle standing). It writes a SETTINGS_CHANGE audit row naming the keys, and a re-enable that cannot be audited is switched back off and answers 503 audit_failed. The MCP load registers only the permitted saved servers (agents/web.py:2060-2067); a switched-off one is held (_MCP_HELD, agents/web.py:2037) and written back unchanged by every save, so the saved configuration never loses it, and adding a server of that name or removing it answers 409 `switched_off` naming the list (_held_refusal, agents/core/routers/mcp.py:159). The lists only narrow: nothing is installed, approved, registered or written to the approval store, and a declared name that matches nothing installed is reported as unknown (finish, agents/core/load_set.py:121). The status rows carry it: /skills (agents/core/routers/skills.py:81), /plugins (agents/core/routers/plugins.py:88) and /api/admin/mcp (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:132) return `load_set` with the declared lists, what was switched off and what is unknown (status, agents/core/load_set.py:132). Safe mode (H275) applies first; the load set narrows further. tests/test_h285_load_set.py (49 cases, plus one in tests/test_cloud_image.py) covers the parsing and its bounds, the six declared rows, the permit table, an unreadable store, a disabled skill and an only-list with their status rows and unknown names, a skill named by its folder, a named-but-absent skill installing or approving nothing (asserted on a private approval store), the skills route, MCP servers switched off and still saved, an MCP only-list, the add and remove refusals for a held server, adding and removing other servers keeping the held one, the MCP list route, the gate's disabled and only lists, the settings-page switch and that only an explicit off counts, that the lists never enable or register, the toggle kept across a restart both ways, a plugin without a settings switch, enabling under an only-list, a toggle the store refuses, and the plugins route. 33 mutants over the parser, the permit table, the persistence, the three loaders, the refusals and the status rows: all caught (two after their cases were added: an explicit off, a refused write). Test manual: ENV-169, ENV-170. Adapted from Hermes: the lists live in the settings store Nerva already persists and edits rather than a YAML file, the plugin toggle writes them, and an MCP server switched off is kept in the saved list rather than dropped. reviews.summary:
The three cron gaps that kept this row partial are now closed. The two Kanban ideas the row said to take (a claim lease with a TTL, and a crash-grace window that never replays an authorized action) were already shipped and still hold.

**Plain cron runs have a wall clock.** `jobs.run_timeout_seconds` (default 900, max 86400) is defined at agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:69-81. Matching Hermes' HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT, 0 means unbounded. `_fire_once` runs the whole ask/brief/remind action, delivery included, through `_bounded_execute` (jobs.py:1810). That method reads the setting (jobs.py:1830-1839) and wraps the run in `asyncio.timeout`. When the run's own deadline expires it raises `JobRunTimeout`; a timeout raised inside the run keeps its own message (jobs.py:1841-1852). An overrun is recorded through `_failed`, so the three-strike pause and the incident still apply. Each channel send has its own 30 s `wait_for` and marks `last_delivery_status` failed on timeout (jobs.py:2130-2145). The setting is seeded at agents/core/settings_db.py:359 and validated at 0..86400 at settings_db.py:1021-1022. Tests:
- tests/test_h288_cron_timeouts.py:140-163: an overrunning run fails with JobRunTimeout and pauses after three strikes.
- :125: a hung send is a failed delivery.
- :167: an inner timeout is not mislabelled as the run deadline.
- :101-121: 0 arms no deadline.

**Queued tasks have a finite budget by default.** `resolve_task_budget` (agents/core/autonomy/executor.py:39-55) uses a positive JARVIS_TASK_MAX_SECONDS first, then the validated `autonomy.task_max_seconds` setting (default 1800, below the 3600 s reaper TTL; settings_db.py:469, validated at 1..86400 at settings_db.py:1023-1024), then the default. It never returns None. `build_executor` passes that budget into TaskExecutor and warns when the budget is not below `autonomy.running_ttl_seconds` (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:2035-2056). `execute` applies `budget_for(kind)` with `wait_for` and returns `wall_time_budget_exceeded` on overrun (executor.py:177-200).

The Kanban worker is registered `self_bounded=True` (autonomy_coordinator.py:2062-2070; register/budget_for at executor.py:95-114), so the card's own `max_runtime_seconds` decides its outcome. A TimeoutError raised by the handler itself is re-raised (executor.py:192). Tests:
- tests/test_h288_cron_timeouts.py:202 and :215: the setting is seeded, validated and finite by default.
- tests/test_h288_cron_timeouts.py:230: the built executor ships the finite budget.
- tests/test_h288_kanban_budget.py:33-53: the Kanban kind is exempt while ordinary kinds stay bounded.
- tests/test_h288_kanban_budget.py:120-141 and :145-173: with a real dispatcher, a card capped above the budget finishes done, and a card's own 1 s cap records TimeoutError on the board run rather than an executor cancel.

**jobs.db waits for a busy writer.** The jobs store opens sqlite with `timeout=30.0` and `PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000` (jobs.py:790-793), the same values as the task queue (agents/core/autonomy/queue.py:402-404). Test: tests/test_h288_cron_timeouts.py:260-261.

**Lease, crash grace and no replay still hold.** `autonomy.running_ttl_seconds` (settings_db.py:467, default 3600) is resynced on every tick (autonomy_coordinator.py:606-610). `TaskQueue.reap_stuck_running` (queue.py:5063-5093) fails a stranded RUNNING row with `stuck_running_ttl` and never re-queues it. `AutonomyWorker._reap_stuck` (agents/core/autonomy/worker.py:1018-1032) runs it at the start of each tick, even under a halt (worker.py:1678-1687). Tested by tests/test_q6_autonomy_killswitch_scope_reaper.py:91-139. In the jobs lane, a claimed request that was interrupted becomes `unknown` with "not replayed" (agents/core/autonomy/jobs_dispatch.py:203-209), tested by tests/test_job_dispatch.py:130.

The row's rationale excludes the delivery-destination knobs, which per-job `channel`/`deliver` plus the owner chat id already cover. The ~14-knob Kanban board is a separate product lane, not part of this row.

reviews.summary:
Final review at HEAD 57ed6db (branch codex/hermes-progress-20261010). Both gaps in the ledger entry are closed on this branch.

Contract that was already in place:
- ToolRPCServer.handle (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:724) never raises. Unknown tools, bad arguments and denials come back as {ok:false, reason} dicts.
- A successful result is cleaned of secrets and invisible characters before it is returned (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:917).
- The agent runtime turns any result that is not strict JSON into a non_json_result error (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1852, agents/core/agent_runtime.py:2260).
- Oversized results go through the bounded spill/truncation envelope (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1892-1897).

Gap 1, bounded error text: closed.
- A handler exception now comes back as reason tool_error plus an "error" field (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:906-909). The same happens on the approved-execute path (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:1000-1003).
- That field is built by sanitize_error (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:349-380). It gives the exception type and message on one line, removes control and invisible characters, redacts known secret patterns with SecretScanner and the broker's own values, then cuts the line to MAX_ERROR_CHARS = 240 (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:221). It never includes a traceback.
- A saturated worker pool for plain-function handlers is answered as tool_busy (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:903-904).
- Hermes allows 2048 characters; Nerva caps at 240. That is tighter, not a gap.

Gap 2, multimodal result envelope: closed.
- A handler can return ToolContent, an ordered list of text and image parts (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:247).
- _content_envelope (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:1148-1173) validates the parts and returns {ok, tool, result, content}. Text parts are scrubbed. A malformed part is refused as invalid_result.
- Parts are bounded: at most 16 parts and 4 images, and each image at most 5,000,000 base64 characters (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:223-229). Each image's leading bytes must match a declared PNG, JPEG, GIF or WEBP type (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:240-245).
- In the runtime, _split_images (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:2213) moves the image bytes out of the JSON the model reads and leaves a short descriptor in their place. The images ride beside the tool message only when the backend can read images, and the message then says the images are data, not instructions (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1029-1035).
- The Anthropic dialect sends them as image blocks inside the tool result (agents/core/llm/tool_dialects.py:375-381).
- A real producer exists in production code: file_tools._read_image returns ToolContent (agents/core/file_tools.py:1982).
- Round 4 hardening:
  - Only an HTTP 400 or 413 marks a turn as provider_rejected (agents/core/llm/anthropic.py:38, agents/core/llm/anthropic.py:221-222). Only that signal makes the tool loop detach every image and resend once (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:911-932). A 429, 5xx, 529, auth failure or timeout keeps the images attached.
  - A job pinned to one model counts each image at a flat IMAGE_TOKEN_COST = 1,600 tokens instead of its base64 length (agents/core/llm/tokenizer.py:19, agents/core/llm/job_selection.py:81, agents/core/llm/job_selection.py:121).

Tests:
- tests/test_tool_rpc_h297_envelope.py covers:
  - the bounded, redacted error message (lines 51 and 72);
  - the error on the approved-execute path (line 92);
  - the multimodal envelope (line 170);
