reviews.summary:
file_read and file_search in agents/core/file_tools.py are off unless JARVIS_FILE_TOOLS is set and bounded to JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS (no `..`, no symlink escape, secret-looking names refused, bytes capped by max_bytes except for whole-image reads); docs/FLAGS.md:170-181 and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:490 describe this surface and the model is told to use file_search for matches and files by glob (agents/core/operating_guidance.py:277-278).

READING. A byte page starts at `offset`, a short read returns `next_offset`, and a bad offset is refused as `bad_offset` (agents/core/file_tools.py:933-937, agents/core/file_tools.py:972-981). A line window is `line_offset` (1-based first line) plus `line_limit` (default 500, at most 2000, agents/core/file_tools.py:175-176, agents/core/file_tools.py:1675-1697): it returns whole lines, never more than max_bytes, and `next_line_offset` names the next page (agents/core/file_tools.py:1774-1859); a byte offset other than 0 beside a window is refused as `bad_window` (agents/core/file_tools.py:1688-1690). New in H303: `line_numbers=true` prefixes every line with its 1-based number and a tab, `cat -n` style, right-aligned to the widest number the window can reach, and the prefix counts against max_bytes (agents/core/file_tools.py:1797, agents/core/file_tools.py:1806-1807); `line_numbers` or `max_line_chars` given alone starts a window at line 1 (agents/core/file_tools.py:1683-1686). `max_line_chars` (8..100000, agents/core/file_tools.py:183-184, agents/core/file_tools.py:1710-1714) caps a line in characters: the default is 2000 when numbered and no cap otherwise (agents/core/file_tools.py:182, agents/core/file_tools.py:1712), and a longer line is cut and ends with the marker ` …[+N chars]` (agents/core/file_tools.py:185, agents/core/file_tools.py:1760-1771). A cut line is still one line, so paging stays exact, and `lines_cut` counts them (agents/core/file_tools.py:1815-1818, agents/core/file_tools.py:1856-1858). The line reader keeps only cap*4+2 bytes of a line and consumes the rest in 64 KiB chunks, so one huge line is never held in memory (agents/core/file_tools.py:1733-1757, agents/core/file_tools.py:1808-1809). The same numbering and cap apply to the text extracted from a .pdf or .docx (agents/core/file_tools.py:2192-2194). Line numbers are opt-in: a byte page is never numbered. Pinned by tests/test_file_read_lines.py:47-58, tests/test_file_read_lines.py:71-82, tests/test_file_read_lines.py:107-120, tests/test_file_read_lines.py:156-173, tests/test_file_read_lines.py:176-198 and tests/test_file_read_lines.py:203-217; the schema and model-facing description declare it (agents/core/file_tools.py:2819-2860, tests/test_file_read_lines.py:220-230).

DOCUMENTS AND IMAGES. A .pdf (pypdf) or .docx (python-docx) comes back as extracted text; an observed input above 50,000,000 bytes is refused as `document_too_large`, a missing parser is `parser_missing` and a parse failure `extraction_failed`, and raw=true returns bytes (agents/core/file_tools.py:2166-2184, tests/test_file_read_documents.py:45-81). Only those two suffixes are extracted (agents/core/local_docs.py:28, agents/core/file_tools.py:200-201). A non-raw read at offset 0 of a .png/.jpg/.gif/.webp whose bytes carry that format's signature is returned as an image, read whole up to 3,750,000 bytes (agents/core/file_tools.py:968-971, agents/core/tool_rpc.py:230, tests/test_h297_bounded_images.py:125-146). tool_result_store pins file_read to an infinite spill threshold so reading a spill never spills again (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:100, tests/test_tool_result_store.py:64-67), and a page of a spilled result says `tainted` (agents/core/file_tools.py:895-907, agents/core/file_tools.py:965-966).

SEARCH. `file_search` (agents/core/file_tools.py:1050-1304) has three modes (`mode`, agents/core/file_tools.py:1104). `literal` is the default: case_sensitive, whole_word, each line matched on its first 8 KiB (agents/core/file_tools.py:1128-1140, tests/test_file_search.py:66-93, tests/test_file_search.py:162-169). `regex` (regex=true) runs ONE engine, Python `re`, inside a killable child interpreter started with `-I -S`, no shell and a scrubbed environment, over batches of the walk's own files (agents/core/file_tools.py:2596-2687, agents/core/file_tools.py:1177-1200); ripgrep is deliberately not used and a test pins that it is ignored even when on the PATH (tests/test_file_search.py:694-710). Lines are matched whole and split on newline only, a non-UTF-8 file is decoded with replacement characters, and the child's output is bounded by the batch, not by how many matches a line holds (tests/test_file_search.py:623-650, tests/test_file_search.py:768-777, tests/test_file_search.py:731-758). Before the child runs, `_portability_error` refuses POSIX classes like [[:alpha:]], a nested set, set operators (`--`, `&&`, `~~`, `||`) inside a class, and `\<` / `\>` as `bad_regex` (agents/core/file_tools.py:2506-2550, tests/test_file_search.py:820-838), and a static guard refuses a nested unbounded repeat such as (a+)+ as `regex_too_complex` (agents/core/file_tools.py:2462-2503, agents/core/file_tools.py:2559-2570, tests/test_file_search.py:331-351). A pattern CPython cannot finish stops at the 10 second deadline (agents/core/file_tools.py:220) with `truncated`, `stopped_by: deadline`, and only the rows of files whose search finished; the unfinished file is not counted in files_scanned (tests/test_file_search.py:486-514, tests/test_file_search.py:527-541). A build with no Python interpreter to start returns `regex_unavailable` (agents/core/file_tools.py:2653-2654, agents/core/file_tools.py:1253-1258, tests/test_file_search.py:572-580). `glob` without `pattern` finds files recursively (`mode: glob`, `files` with sizes, not read, so max_bytes does not apply), with `*` `?` `[seq]`, `{a,b}` alternation up to 32 expansions and a leading `!` to negate; a glob without `/` matches the file name and one with `/` the path below `path` (agents/core/file_tools.py:2363-2427, agents/core/file_tools.py:2455-2459, agents/core/file_tools.py:1214-1223, tests/test_file_search.py:370-386, tests/test_file_search.py:964-986, tests/test_file_search.py:1000-1016). A glob search is bounded by MAX_WALK_FILES visited files and MAX_WALK_ENTRIES examined entries (every file, directory, symlink and secret name the walk meets) plus the deadline, checked inside the walk, and it reports the cap in `stopped_by` (agents/core/file_tools.py:238-239, agents/core/file_tools.py:2244-2312, tests/test_file_search.py:799-817, tests/test_file_search.py:930-945); a 5,200-file dependency tree does not hide a file behind it (tests/test_file_search.py:853-868). Matches, matches per file, files searched, visited files, bytes and seconds are all capped and reported (agents/core/file_tools.py:214-223, agents/core/file_tools.py:1202-1213, tests/test_file_search.py:129-150). Symlinks are never followed and secret names are pruned and counted (agents/core/file_tools.py:2287-2300, tests/test_file_search.py:102-126).

NOISE DIRECTORIES. Content and glob searches do not enter node_modules, venv, .venv, __pycache__, dist, build, target, .tox, .nox and the mypy/pytest/ruff caches, nor plain directory names listed in the searched root's .gitignore, unless `include_ignored=true`; the number pruned is reported as `ignored`, and a `path` that is itself one of them is searched (agents/core/file_tools.py:246-249, agents/core/file_tools.py:2210-2241, agents/core/file_tools.py:2291-2292, tests/test_file_search.py:871-927). The `file_list` description points the model to file_search for recursive file finding (agents/core/file_tools.py:2862-2867).

reviews.remaining: Document extraction beyond .pdf and .docx is not built: no .xlsx, .pptx or other extractor exists, and DOC_EXTS and the parser table list only those two (agents/core/local_docs.py:28, agents/core/file_tools.py:200-201). The Hermes row names 'PDF/docx/…' and the gap stays open. Honest limits of what is built: (1) regex search is Python `re`, not ripgrep, so ripgrep's linear-time completion is not available: a catastrophic-backtracking pattern that CPython cannot finish, and that the static (a+)+ guard does not catch such as (a|aa)+$, stops at the 10 second deadline with stopped_by=deadline and returns only the rows of files whose search finished; regex semantics (\w \b \s, Unicode classes, no PCRE or POSIX features) are Python's, and flavour-dependent constructs are refused rather than translated. (2) With no Python interpreter to start (a frozen build) regex=true returns regex_unavailable; literal and glob search still work. (3) .gitignore handling is the cheap subset: only the searched root's own .gitignore is read, only plain directory names or paths (wildcard lines are ignored), and any '!' line disables it entirely; the fixed NOISE_DIRS list is still pruned. (4) One directory holding millions of entries is still listed in full by os.walk before the entry, file and deadline caps run, so the caps bound the walk between directories, not inside one. (5) Content search skips files larger than max_bytes (default 2,000,000) and binaries, matches a literal on only the first 8 KiB of each line, and returns bounded snippets with path and line (no context lines); the result is bounded by match counts (at most 500 rows, 20 per file), not by a configurable character budget like Hermes's max_result_size_chars. (6) Line numbers are opt-in (line_numbers=true), not the default of every read, and are not applied to byte pages or images.

K1, K2 și K3 sunt livrate: execute_code înregistrat pentru model, celule într-un interpreter rezident pe sesiune (K2, `llm.execute_code_sessions`, implicit pornit după opt-in-ul execute_code când backend-ul izolat e configurat; o dezactivare explicită e păstrată) și controale de operator peste el. Spill-ul stdout/stderr într-un fișier funcționează pe ambele căi. `_open_stream_spills` (agents/core/code_tools.py:643) deschide scriitorii în flux înainte de rulare. Pe K1, sinks trec prin `ToolRPCSandboxRuntime.run_python` (code_tools.py:606) până la `Sandbox.execute_python`. Pe K2, worker-ul trimite ieșirea celulei în cadre de cel mult 4096 de caractere (agents/core/session_kernels.py:387-388), iar `_Capture` dă fiecare cadru scriitorului (session_kernels.py:736). Gazda vede deci tot fluxul, iar memoria ei rămâne mărginită: păstrează doar capul și coada. Un flux care a încăput nu lasă fișier; rezultatul unui spill poartă calea, referința, dimensiunea și sha256. Lotul HEQ 1 (H661) a făcut din notiță apelul exact. `_spill_notice` (code_tools.py:211) scrie `file_read(path=…, offset=0, max_bytes=…)`, construit de `page_recipe` (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:145), și cere paginarea prin next_offset. `stdout_read_with` (code_tools.py:292) apare doar când turei i s-a oferit file_read și sonda `_spill_readable` (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1542) confirmă că poate deschide acel fișier; altfel notița spune că fișierul e păstrat pentru owner și nu poate fi paginat din tura asta. file_read primește directorul de spill ca ușă read-only (autonomy_coordinator.py:1497). Un spill în flux are acum un plafon: DEFAULT_MAX_STREAM_BYTES, 5 MB (tool_result_store.py:130, cifra lui Hermes). Peste el fișierul ține primii 5 MB și se termină într-un marcaj explicit (coada fluxului rămâne doar inline), iar rezultatul poartă `stdout_spill_capped`, `stdout_kept_bytes` și `stdout_file_bytes` (code_tools.py:294-296). tests/test_code_tools.py paginează înapoi tot fluxul pe ambele căi (tests/test_code_tools.py:831) și verifică plafonul (tests/test_code_tools.py:884).

web_search and web_extract at the accepted Hermes contract, with the last blocker fixed so the claim is true in the real tool loop. AgentToolRuntime cuts every tool at 30 s (agent_runtime.py:278, :1460-1472) and register_tool has no per-tool budget, so web_extract carries its own call-level budget (web_tools.py:117-118: 22 s soft, 26 s hard; read_one at :946; the soft deadline reaches WebSearchPlugin.read_page(deadline=) at websearch.py:433 and _read_pdf at :557). PDFs queue two at a time (PDF_MAX_CONCURRENT=2, per-event-loop asyncio.Semaphore, thread BoundedSemaphore backstop) but only inside that budget: a PDF that does not fit answers parser_busy with a retry hint, a read still running at 26 s answers fetch_failed with a hint, and every page finished by then is returned. Five ordinary PDFs all read; five very large ones read the first few and answer the rest parser_busy, never tool_timeout. Proven through the real AgentToolRuntime._execute_rpc with the wall scaled down (test_five_slow_pdfs_answer_every_url_before_the_loop_cuts_the_call_off, test_a_hung_page_..., test_a_pdf_that_cannot_finish_in_the_budget_..., test_a_web_extract_call_answers_inside_the_tool_loops_own_wall, which reads the loop's default from its signature). A caller with no deadline (gatherer, scripts) keeps 90 s queue wait and 30 s parse. docs/WEB_SEARCH.md no longer claims a 90 s wait inside a call. A name that does not resolve now answers url_refused exactly like a private address, so a prompt-injected caller cannot probe which internal names exist (test_a_name_that_does_not_resolve_reads_like_a_private_address; the log keeps the difference). HTTP 408/425/429/5xx and timeouts are fetch_failed (retry); every other error status is the new reason http_error with status (do not retry), checked before the media type (test_permanent_http_errors_are_not_retryable_and_transient_ones_are). Unchanged and still tested: provider ABC and registry, no keyless rescue for unattended callers, narrow provider view, 15,000-char head+tail cut, five URLs per call, full text spilled with a footer that names file_read only when reachable, untrusted_output and taint, secret_in_url, tainted_turn, site_blocked, ungated registration, no x_search. ACCEPTED NARROWINGS, to be recorded as narrowings and not as exact equivalence: (1) the backend selector is the env var JARVIS_WEB_BACKEND (plus JARVIS_WEB_PROVIDER_TIER, JARVIS_WEB_RESCUE, JARVIS_WEB_BLOCKED_DOMAINS), not a runtime web.backend setting; changing it takes an environment edit, with no HUD toggle; (2) web_search declares 50,000 bytes (web_tools.py:109, :1023) and only web_extract declares 100,000 (:1034), and web_search rows are fitted to its ceiling with the dropped count in omitted; (3) the ceiling is bytes where Hermes counts chars, and the loop may still lower it to a small model's per-result budget; (4) llm.tool_loop_enabled ships default off, so the tools reach the model only after the owner turns it on (CHT-122); (5) kernel mediation of egress is opt-in (JARVIS_ACTION_KERNEL); (6) the registry takes first-party plugins only. KNOWN LIMITS, not built: one page hung inside pypdf cannot be interrupted from Python (two such hangs hold both slots and PDF reads answer parser_busy until they end), and the memory pypdf uses to decompress a stream or extract one page is not bounded by Nerva (the 2 MB cap bounds the download only); both are in docs/WEB_SEARCH.md, and a killable subprocess with a memory rlimit would be the hard bound. NOT LIVE-PROVEN: no keyed Tavily or SearXNG query, no real PDF with pypdf installed (pypdf is in no requirements file), no plugin-registered backend dialled, no real DNS outage, no HUD ask; every leg uses fakes, a fake pypdf module and httpx.MockTransport. Mutation pass from the previous round (93 killed, 0 survived) predates this round's code and was not re-run on the new branches; the new tests cover them directly. reviews.summary:
The model can decide to say one short text aloud on one room's device, and can do it again. register_speak_tool (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:684) adds a ToolRPC `speak` tool with gated=True, trusted execution and its own gated intake (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:711, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:717). It is registered only while JARVIS_MEDIA_DIRECTOR is on (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:697), and AutonomyCoordinator wires it with the broker kernel and the governed enqueue (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:928, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:2240). It reaches the same Media Director instance the media routes use, so the owner's device registry and session board apply (agents/core/routers/media_director.py:272). SpeakTool.preflight (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:388) runs at proposal and again before the approved run. It refuses text over the spoken-reply cap and code-only text (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:394, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:396). It resolves a room to that room's one announce-capable default device, so the card title and the persisted args name the speaker (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:268, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:467). The model now writes its own long-term memory during a turn, through a tool that is atomic, guarded, recorded and undoable. `memory` (register_memory_tool, agents/core/memory_tool.py:541; registered ungated at agents/core/memory_tool.py:694 and wired from the autonomy coordinator's H314 block, whose `_living_memory` getter and `register_memory_tool(` call tests/test_h314_memory_tool.py:546-548 reads back from the coordinator's source) takes `operations`, each an add, a replace of the one fact `old_text` matches, or a remove of it, against target `memory` (the LivingMemory `core` ring of agent notes) or `user` (the `user_core` profile ring) (TARGETS, agents/core/memory_tool.py:79); a call with no operations reads both. The rings are reached only when cognition memory is on: the coordinator's `_living_memory` getter hands the tool the LivingMemory only when `cog.sub_enabled("memory_enabled")` holds (pinned by content at tests/test_h314_memory_tool.py:546-548), and a getter that yields nothing — memory off, safe mode, or a getter that fails (agents/core/memory_tool.py:557-568) — is refused `memory_disabled` (agents/core/memory_tool.py:625-627). Both rings come from one LivingMemory, so the enabled set is both or none: when memory is off the tool's offer says so through the H296 schema hook (OFF_DESCRIPTION, agents/core/memory_tool.py:587-588) and every call is refused `memory_disabled`, rather than the target enum being narrowed to an empty list. Every operation is checked on a working copy before anything is written (plan, agents/core/memory_tool.py:180): one line of at most 300 characters, the core block's own cut (MAX_FACT_CHARS, agents/core/memory_tool.py:81), with no control, format, private-use, surrogate or other invisible character (the quarantine.strip_format_chars set: variation selectors, Hangul fillers, U+034F, U+2800) (_clean_text, agents/core/memory_tool.py:136), scanned with the normalised injection scanner (_scan, agents/core/memory_tool.py:159), an old_text that matches exactly one fact, compared against the whitespace-normalised fact as the prompt shows it (_match, agents/core/memory_tool.py:168), no duplicate, and a full ring refusing an add instead of silently dropping its oldest fact; one refusal changes nothing. The rings are then written by a new compare-and-set (CoreMemory.compare_and_set, agents/core/cognition/memory.py:726) under the lock a forget clears them with, so a forget or another write that ran in between wins and nothing forgotten is written back; a second ring that fails puts the first back (_commit, agents/core/memory_tool.py:440). A compare-and-set that lost is refused `memory_changed_meanwhile`; a ring that cannot be saved is refused `memory_write_failed`. Only a clean owner turn at the operator surface writes: the resolver offers the tool to operator/owner alone, whatever llm.guest_tools says (OWNER_OPERATOR_TOOLS, agents/core/tool_profiles.py:111 and :243), the handler refuses any other posture (agents/core/memory_tool.py:577) and a turn whose origin is untrusted, an inbound message, web content or a flagged recall (agents/core/memory_tool.py:580), so an injected instruction cannot make itself permanent. Every write is committed and then recorded as an intent-log `memory.write` entry carrying the actor, the undo ref, the targets and per operation its target and action — never the text nor a hash of it, since an unsalted hash of a short fact is guessed back and the intent log survives a forget (agents/core/memory_tool.py:666). A record that cannot be made puts the rings back and records the put-back as `memory.write_reverted` (undo: `memory.undo_reverted`) with the same ref, naming exactly the rings it restored, because the intent log keeps a record whose save failed and writes it with its next one; a put-back that cannot be made (a ring moved again) is logged as an error and not recorded as one (_revert, agents/core/memory_tool.py:471; _record_put_back, agents/core/memory_tool.py:427). With no intent log nothing is written (_record, agents/core/memory_tool.py:419). The rings' previous contents are kept under the ref in a bounded undo store beside the rings (UndoStore, agents/core/memory_tool.py:255), which a forget deletes with them and which POST /api/admin/forget empties together with the live rings (clear_live_memory, agents/core/data_purge.py:546), so an undo during a forget cannot write the facts back. undo (agents/core/memory_tool.py:490) restores a write while the rings still hold what it wrote, by the same compare-and-set, recorded as `memory.undo`. The owner reads the rings and the writes undo would still restore — only those whose rings hold what they wrote (UndoStore.recent, agents/core/memory_tool.py:290) — at GET /api/memory/core (agents/core/routers/memory_kg.py:986) and undoes one at POST /api/memory/core/undo, admin-only (agents/core/routers/memory_kg.py:1013). The Console's Long-Term Memory panel shows both rings and the recent writes with an undo each, and says when an undo is refused (LongTermMemoryPanel, frontend/src/panels/long-term-memory.tsx). A write that changes a ring leaves a `memory_updated` trail row with the changed targets and the actions, never text; a call that changes nothing leaves none (_record_event, agents/core/memory_tool.py:522). The prompt's core block stays frozen per session, so a write reaches the system prompt at the next session and the tool answers with both rings as they now are. tests/test_h314_memory_tool.py (72 cases at the build, 123 collected since H423) covers the plan and every refusal (malformed, injected, invisible-character, ambiguous, duplicate or over-full operations), the compare-and-set and a ring that cannot be saved, an owner write of both rings with its record and its undo, a read, an add already saved, the five postures and untrusted origins, a failing getter, memory switched off and its offer, a broken memory module, an unknown argument, no intent log or one without a record method, a record that fails and its recorded put-back, an undo whose put-back also fails claiming none, a forget between the read and the write, a forget that empties the undo store, a second ring that fails, a full ring, undo after the ring moved, undo of a replace and a remove, undo without memory, an undo that cannot be recorded, the undo store's bound and its listing of only restorable writes, the trail row, the profile offer and the routes; frontend/src/test/long-term-memory-panel.test.tsx pins the panel. 47 mutants: 33 at the build (32 caught, four after their cases were added: a raw over-long padded fact, an audit sink without record, an empty operation list, the undo listing's limit; one equivalent, rewriting a ring the call did not change) and 14 in the review round (13 caught, one after its case was added: an undo whose put-back also fails; one equivalent, widening _moved to rings it is never given). Test manual: MEM-204, MEM-205. reviews.summary:
Built in #1207, with H340 in the same change (critic note 21: one skill_view), and fixed after seven adversarial reviews. The first (review-H318: two majors, six minors, nine nits) found an unkeyed signature counted as a vouch and approved changes that never landed. The second (review-H318b: two majors, seven minors, seven nits) found that an approved change disabled the skill it improved (a bundled skill unbundled, a signed or approved one losing its standing) and that the owner still approved without seeing the change. The third (review-H318c: one records major, eight minors, seven nits) found a write between the standing read and the renewal could ride into the vouch, a renewal failure reported as applied, a keyed signature overwritten while its key was missing, a publish that silently dropped a linked file, and cards that could be lost or left pending. The fourth (review-H318d: one major, five minors, six nits) found that text-mode SKILL.md writes made every vouched apply fail on Windows, a partial renewal left a new signature over the old text, publish still followed a link planted after its check, and cards beyond the route's page were called inert. The fifth (review-H318e: two minors, seven nits) found the old SKILL.sig read after the write with no rollback behind it, text-mode test fixtures on the Windows lane, a signature that could not be put back reported as the old text staying, a truncated write, the review superseding by the record's origin, a /v1 card approvable without its diff, and publish describing another read of SKILL.md. The sixth (review-H318f: one minor, four nits) found the whole-file write staging its temporary file inside the skill, where one a crash left would void the signature. The seventh (review-H318g: two minors, five nits) found a standing that could not be read for a moment read as unsigned, and the crash-safety claim wider than the code. All are fixed or stated below; two nits are stated by decision below. Hermes gives the agent skills_list, skill_view (a skill's SKILL.md or one of its linked files) and skill_manage (create, patch and delete). Nerva now offers all three powers under its governance: the two reads as ungated read-only ToolRPC tools, and authoring as a proposal the owner approves.

The three tools are in agents/core/skills/tools.py; register_skill_tools (agents/core/skills/tools.py:525) registers them on the orchestrator's ToolRPC server in AutonomyCoordinator, next to the todo and memory tools; tests/test_h318_skill_tools.py:400 drives all three through the live hub's own server.

The trust gate:
- SkillLoader.catalog_gate (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1551) is the prompt catalog's gate, factored out and now shared by the catalog, skills_list and skill_view.
- It says why a skill is not shown: sandboxed (quarantined included), untrusted (a signature that does not verify here), or declared for other agents. prompt_catalog applies it unchanged, and its suite passes as before.

skills_list {query?, offset?, limit?}:
- It returns name, a one-line description and the command names for every skill the gate passes for the calling agent (agents/core/skills/tools.py:604).
- A row whose text is injection-flagged is left out, as the catalog leaves it out. The query matches name or description, case-insensitively. Pages hold at most 50 rows, with total and next_offset.
- Unknown fields and malformed paging are refused by name.

skill_view {name, file?, reload?} (agents/core/skills/tools.py:644):
- It returns the SKILL.md body (frontmatter removed; the heading dialect whole) with its template variables rendered (H340), plus the list of the skill's other files, at most 3 KiB of names as the answer carries them (escapes counted) with files_more counting the rest; a file or body is served up to 64 KiB on disk, as always, and refused only when its escapes pass 128 KiB (MAX_ENCODED_BYTES), and the description is cut to 2 KiB escaped (agents/core/skills/tools.py:100-109). With file, it returns one of those files, listed or not.
- It serves the bytes the trust checks ran on at load, kept as Skill.view_files (agents/core/skills/loader.py:375): each file up to 64 KiB as bytes, at most 1 MiB of a skill, any other file only as its size (listed, refused by name). An edit on disk after the signature check is not what the model reads, and a skill's assets are not held for the process's life. Signing a skill loads it again, so the view follows the signed bytes.
- A path can only name a file of that snapshot. It must be relative, with no '..', leading '/' or backslash, and it is normalised (agents/core/skills/tools.py:515). The snapshot refuses links when it is taken.
- Only text is served (a NUL or bad UTF-8 is refused, a BOM dropped), at most 64 KiB (MAX_FILE_BYTES, counted in bytes) after the template variables render and 128 KiB once escaped. The tool declares the escaped ceiling, the file list's and the description's bounds and 4 KiB of envelope as its own result budget.
- An unknown skill and one this agent is not shown answer alike (skill_unknown).
- The answer is tainted, and carries a warning sentence saying why next to the content, in two cases (agents/core/skills/tools.py:587):
  - the body or the description is injection-flagged;
  - the skill comes from outside the product and the owner has not vouched for it.
- Skill.owner_vouched (agents/core/skills/loader.py:847) is true for a bundled skill, or for an outside one with a keyed signature or the owner's approval of these exact bytes. That is the same rule that decides whether its code may load in-process.
- An unkeyed SKILL.sig is a sha256 anyone can compute. It verifies as integrity-only, but it is no vouch, so a self-signed import stays data (review-H318 M-1, SEC-B2).
- The loop fences a tainted answer as DATA and raises the turn's taint.
- A body view that succeeds for the owner's own turn also declares the skill's required_env names to the code-environment registry for that actor and session, with a validator the registry re-runs before the names are honoured (the same loader, skill, vouch, snapshot and gate), and a tainted view revokes them; a declaration that fails never fails the view (agents/core/skills/tools.py:733, agents/core/code_env.py:161, agents/core/code_env.py:222).

skill_propose (agents/core/skills/tools.py:819):
- {name, content} proposes a new SKILL.md for an existing skill that this agent is shown. It becomes a pending SkillProposalStore proposal with origin agent:<agent>, plus one skill.patch_proposal approval card bound to it in the ledger (queue_card, agents/core/skills/proposals.py:213). The background review and /refine queue theirs the same way.
- A bundled skill is refused (skill_propose_bundled): it is product source, and an edit would unbundle it and, with its code, stop it loading. A change that would rename the skill is refused (skill_propose_rename).
- What the owner reviews comes from the ledger, never from the card. GET /api/skills/proposals (admin, agents/core/routers/skills.py:973) serves the pending proposals, a page of 20 with more counting the rest, each with its whole diff against the live SKILL.md, whether the skill drifted since, and flags for a rename or a bundled skill (describe, agents/core/skills/proposals.py:272); a proposal from before cards were bound, or whose card is gone from the queue, gets its card there, every pending proposal's, not only the page's, and the answer names every pending proposal's card (cards). The /v1 console's panel holds every skill-change card it has no diff for (one beyond the page, or one no proposal names) with Approve disabled, offering Reject (review-H318e n-4), re-reads the action list once the proposals answer, and says the change is loading, or that it could not be read, and holds Approve until it knows; a change the hub will refuse (a bundled skill, a rename) offers reject only in both consoles. The HUD's Decision Inbox shows these under SKILL CHANGES, whole, with approve and reject on the proposal's own card (frontend/src/panels/skill-changes.tsx), and the /v1 console's action panel shows the same diff under a skill-change card.
- Only the proposal's own card decides it (agents/core/skills/curator.py:217): a card anyone with a user token queued naming a proposal id changes nothing, and the decide route says so.
- Re-sending the same text, from any origin, makes no second proposal and no second card; a card that failed to queue is queued by the retry. A newer proposal from the same origin (the caller's own, even when the text re-sent was another origin's) for the same skill supersedes its older pending one (marked superseded, its card withdrawn), whether the tool, the background review or /refine proposed it (each passes its own origin, review-H318e n-2); binding a card withdraws the unbound cards naming the proposal, and a proposal superseded while its card was queued gets that card withdrawn, and a process takes at most 10 proposals a day, new skills included (skill_propose_limit).
- The owner's decision applies it at once: POST /api/actions/{id}/decide on the proposal's card runs SkillCurator.apply_decisions (agents/core/routers/actions.py:161, agents/core/skills/curator.py:154), one pass at a time, the nightly pass included, not gated by the learning loop's flag or the night window. The apply is hash-checked against drift and backed up under the skill's directory name with a unique suffix.
- The applied bytes keep the skill's standing (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1483, agents/core/skills/loader.py:1514): judged on one snapshot of the tree read before the write; after the write, the tree must be that snapshot with only SKILL.md replaced by the approved text, and the SKILL.sig that verified or the owner's approval is renewed over exactly those checked bytes, never a later read. SKILL.md is read and written as bytes, never in text mode, so the line ends on disk are the ones checked, on Windows too, and written whole: staged beside the skill's folder where it can be (a file a crash leaves inside the folder counts as a member and fails the signature closed; where beside it cannot be, another filesystem or a root the hub cannot write, the folder itself is used: review-H318g n-1), created with the old file's mode, flushed to disk and renamed over it, so a write cut short leaves the old text (review-H318e n-3, review-H318f m-1). The old SKILL.sig is read with SKILL.md, before anything is written (review-H318e m-1); a read of it that fails changes nothing and is tried again at the next decision (unreadable_signature, review-H318f n-1), and so does a standing that could not be read for a moment, which no longer reads as unsigned (review-H318g m-1); a signature that stays unreadable is warned about once per proposal. The apply is not crash-proof: a crash between the rename and the renewal leaves the skill sandboxed (untrusted, never trusted) and the next decision reports it as drifted, and on Windows a SKILL.md another process holds open cannot be replaced, so the change is retried as write_failed. Otherwise, or if the renewal fails, the old SKILL.md and the old SKILL.sig are put back byte for byte, where the old signature and approval still hold, the outcome says changed_during_apply or standing_not_renewed (rollback_failed, with the backup, if the old text could not be put back; signature_not_restored if the old text is back but its SKILL.sig could not be, which leaves the skill untrusted until it is signed again; when the old text could not be put back, its signature is not either, so what was renewed is not undone over the text that stays), and the proposal is marked stale with that reason rather than retried every pass. A standing that cannot be read (a SKILL.sig that is not UTF-8) reads as unsigned, and one proposal that fails never stops the pass. A keyed SKILL.sig whose key is not configured is not overwritten: the change waits (signing_key_missing). A shipped skill is known by its load or by where it lives (a shipped name directly under the product's skills tree), so one whose bytes drifted is still refused, by the tool, the background review and the apply. A skill nothing vouched for gains no vouch, a signature that no longer verifies is not renewed, and code changed on disk since the approval does not ride the patch. The answer reports each outcome with the state the skill is left in (shown, sandboxed, untrusted, hidden) or why it was not applied (bundled_skill, renames_skill, drifted_since_proposal, write_failed). A write that failed stays approved and is retried at the next decision, leaving no backup behind for the attempt. Publishing builds the package from one snapshot of the source, the bytes it read, and its registry row describes that snapshot's SKILL.md (review-H318e n-5): a skill whose folder is a link, a member that is a link or not a regular file, or a file that changed while read is refused (422, skill_source_refused: a link, a special file, or a file that could not be read stably), and a link planted after the check is never followed.
- {description, steps} asks for a new skill, which SkillLoader.generate_skill writes into CDX-8 quarantine (PENDING_REVIEW, never executed until the owner approves).
- Nothing writes a live SKILL.md: the live file is byte-identical after a proposal.
- Only an owner's turn that has read nothing untrusted may propose. A guest, a household member, a job, an inbound channel or a turn that read a web page (the action origin a read raises) is refused by name, and so is a turn whose origin cannot be read. Injection-flagged text is refused, as are mixed or malformed arguments.

Differences from Hermes, by decision:
- Authoring is a proposal, never a write. Since H665, deleting a skill and writing or removing supporting files are proposals too, inside a skill_propose {operations} batch that only the owner's card applies (H330 tracks that surface).
- skill_propose is offered wherever an ungated tool is, and refuses every turn that is not the owner's clean one; it is not withheld from the offer (a nit both reviews left).
- The daily limit is per process and follows local time: a restart resets it.
- Publishing a skill to the marketplace signs a staged copy, never the owner's tree, so sharing a skill is not vouching for it (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:391).
- All three tools are ungated, so an inbound guest is offered them only when the owner names them in llm.guest_tools (critic note 22). tests/_snapshots/tool_profiles.json is regenerated.

reviews.summary:
At HEAD 57ed6db, the three gaps recorded for this row are closed on this branch: the flat index, the missing cache and snapshot, and the missing dedup across turns. Two adversarial skeptics passed the row, and it was then cherry-picked onto HEAD (commit 31a8902 and the commits before it).

1) The index is grouped by category, with a name and description per skill. SkillLoader.prompt_index (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1780) builds one row per skill: its name, its description and its commands. Rows are grouped under the category the skill declares, with "general" as the default (agents/core/skills/loader.py:124-132, agents/core/skills/loader.py:1844-1873). The index uses the same catalog_gate as skills_list and drops rows flagged for prompt injection. Skills with no command are listed too.

2) The index is cached in two places. One is an in-process LRU of 16 blocks (agents/core/skills/loader.py:99-108). The other is a disk snapshot under the profile's data root (agents/core/skills/loader.py:111-115). Both are keyed by index_manifest, a hash of every skill's name, path, SKILL.md bytes, manifest and trust state (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1747-1765). The key also covers the agent, the switches, the channel, the environments, the offered tools and the bounds. A snapshot is reused only when three checks pass (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1897, agents/core/skills/loader.py:1927, agents/core/skills/loader.py:1946):
- its manifest hash matches;
- its text is clean on a re-scan;
- every row in it is one the loader would write now.
Otherwise the index is rebuilt.

3) Repeated loads are now deduplicated across turns, not only within one turn. _once answers a repeat skill_view with an already_loaded pointer that keeps the skill's file list (agents/core/skills/tools.py:779-809). The pointer says "this_turn" when the content is already in this tool loop's transcript. It says "this_session" when the session's carried block holds that digest. reload=true reads the skill again (agents/core/skills/tools.py:648-650). LoadedSkillLedger keeps the loads (agents/core/skills/tools.py:360) and carries each one for CARRY_TTL_TURNS=2 real turns (agents/core/skills/tools.py:211). The carry has these limits:
- it is bounded in sessions, loads and bytes, sized to the model's window (agents/core/skills/tools.py:205-220, agents/core/skills/tools.py:230);
- it is re-checked against the skill's current bytes and template variables;
- a guest on the shared session never gets it;
- a session's loads are forgotten when the session is archived (agents/core/session_archive.py:105).

How the index and the carry reach the prompt:
- Orchestrator._prompt_context puts skills_index and skills_loaded into a per-agent copy of the context (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4035-4104), and Agent.build_prompt renders both (agents/core/agent.py:860-871).
- handle_input and handle_input_stream each count one carry turn (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2499, agents/core/orchestrator.py:2728).
- The fix from the last review means non-stream channels now get the same context: the per-agent context is built at agents/core/orchestrator.py:5111-5112 and used at agents/core/orchestrator.py:5128 and agents/core/orchestrator.py:5141, and the shared route plan builds through _build_agent_prompt (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4983).
- The selected-image turn renders the carry without counting a turn (agents/core/llm/vision_turn.py:64, agents/core/llm/vision_turn.py:96).

The L0/L1/L2 tools from H318 stay in place: skills_list at agents/core/skills/tools.py:604 and skill_view at agents/core/skills/tools.py:644.

Honest limits:
- There is no per-category DESCRIPTION.md header. Categories come from each skill's frontmatter. This was never one of the row's recorded gaps.
- The dedup works through the carry and pointers, not Hermes' message-history suppression.
- No live provider acceptance was run.

The SKILL.md frontmatter contract Hermes parses (agent/skill_utils.parse_frontmatter and tools/skills_tool_plugin.py) now lives in one shared module, agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py, used by both the loader and the importer.

Parsing. split_frontmatter (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:47):
- drops a leading UTF-8 BOM before the fence check (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:56);
- takes the closing fence at column 0 only, as Hermes' `\n---\s*\n` does, so an indented `---` inside a block scalar is content (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:63);
- falls back to key: value lines for a block that is not valid YAML (_naive_key_values, agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:83), instead of demoting the file to the heading dialect.

The fallback is stricter than Hermes' line split:
- only column-0 keys count, so a nested `name:` cannot replace the skill's own;
- a value wrapped in matching quotes loses them;
- a fallback that finds neither a name nor a description counts as no frontmatter (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:77), so a heading-dialect file framed by fences keeps its heading parse.

contract_fields (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:359), merged into every frontmatter manifest (agents/core/skills/loader.py:961), keeps the keys Hermes recognises:
- homepage and compatibility;
- platforms, read as Hermes matches them (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:204): a list, or one string as one name. Each name maps through PLATFORM_MAP and matches the OS whose sys.platform starts with it, so darwin and win count and osx and win64 do not. An unmatched name is kept, so a gate refuses it everywhere, as Hermes hides it;
- environments and requires_apps, where a string is one item (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:224, agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:234);
- triggers and dependencies;
- tags and related_skills, where a declared metadata.hermes value wins over the top-level key (skill_view's `hermes_meta.get(k) or frontmatter.get(k)`);
- setup, prerequisites and required_credential_files;
- required_environment_variables (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:256), which matches Hermes' _get_required_environment_variables: it merges the declared list, setup.collect_secrets and the legacy prerequisites.env_vars, first entry wins, names are validated, and `optional` is read for truth;

Skill exposes platforms, environments, requires_apps, required_env (names only; no value is read) and hermes_meta, and to_dict carries them (agents/core/skills/loader.py:519, agents/core/skills/loader.py:567, agents/core/skills/loader.py:575, agents/core/skills/loader.py:579, agents/core/skills/loader.py:585).

Imported frontmatter is third-party text:
- json_safe (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:128) bounds depth, width, string length and total nodes, with a 2,048-node budget per value (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:134). A 2 KB YAML alias bomb that would expand to 64^6 nodes parses in about 0.02 s.
- Dates become ISO strings, and NaN, infinities and integers past 64 bits become null or "". A hex integer past Python's str() limit no longer raises (_scalar_text, agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:112), so the security-posture route serialises Skill.to_dict with allow_nan=False.
- discover() skips a skill whose load raises and keeps the rest, while the signing misconfiguration still stops discovery (agents/core/skills/loader.py:720-725).
- A second skill taking an occupied registry name is logged: a warning within one tree (e.g. two names sharing their first 64 characters), info for a user skill replacing a bundled one (agents/core/skills/loader.py:737).

Deliberate differences from Hermes:
- A closing fence at end of file with no trailing newline is accepted, as Nerva always did.
- The registry is last-writer-wins with that log line; Hermes' listing keeps the first.

Skills an agent writes do not take effect until a person approves them. skill_propose puts a new skill created from {description, steps} into PENDING_REVIEW quarantine through generate_skill (agents/core/skills/tools.py:872). The loader registers that skill but never runs its module (agents/core/skills/loader.py:807). skill_propose also accepts {operations} (agents/core/skills/tools.py:838-839): a batch that is dry-run checked and recorded under one approval card (agents/core/skills/tools.py:1010-1017). The decision on that card applies or drops the whole batch (agents/core/routers/actions.py:147-160).

H331 closes the three review gaps that were left.

(1) Full content before approval. SkillLoader.pending_skill_detail (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1378-1444) returns every file in a quarantined skill's folder, with SKILL.md first, then the code and the remaining files. Each file comes with its text, size and sha256. The result also includes the PENDING_REVIEW note and the code-guidance findings. Output is capped per file, in total and by file count (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1345-1347), and truncated, binary, symlinked, unreadable and extra files are flagged. _pending_skill_dir (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1349-1376) only accepts a real, non-symlinked folder that sits directly under a skills root and holds a plain PENDING_REVIEW file. It rejects crafted names. The admin route GET /api/skills/pending/{name} (agents/core/routers/skills.py:774-788) serves the result with no-store caching and returns 404 for anything not pending. The HUD's PendingSkillDetail (frontend/src/gap.tsx:1206) renders it behind a per-row "review" toggle (frontend/src/gap.tsx:1284-1285).

(2) Reject. SkillLoader.discard_generated_skill (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1446-1470) moves only a skill that is still pending into an archive outside every discovery root, using a unique timestamped name. It also removes the skill's registry entries and revokes any approval tied to its path. The admin route is POST /api/skills/{name}/discard (agents/core/routers/skills.py:791-805). In the HUD it is a two-step ConfirmAction (frontend/src/gap.tsx:1291-1293).

(3) Bulk approve and reject. POST /api/skills/review/bulk (agents/core/routers/skills.py:949-964) takes a BulkReviewBody (agents/core/routers/skills.py:812-822): approved, plus lists of skills, proposals and batches, each capped at 50, with extra fields forbidden. An empty request returns 400. _bulk_review (agents/core/routers/skills.py:843-946) handles each kind:
- Pending skills are approved, or discarded on reject.
- Proposals and batches have their own approval card decided through _decide_card (agents/core/routers/skills.py:825-840). Decided proposals are then applied with curator.apply_decisions (agents/core/routers/skills.py:897-904), and each batch is applied or closed with SkillBatchStore.decide (agents/core/routers/skills.py:939).
Each item reports its own result, and one failure does not undo the others. The HUD panel has checkboxes on pending skills, proposals (inline diff) and batches (inline preview). Its bulk calls post to this route and list every item that was not decided (frontend/src/gap.tsx:1235-1270), behind two-step approve/reject ConfirmActions (frontend/src/gap.tsx:1327-1333).

Fix from Codex review (commits 2b45f8fb, b1e44cde): the bulk route now reads the outcomes that apply_decisions returns, keyed by proposal id (agents/core/routers/skills.py:895-904). A decided proposal counts as ok only when its outcome is ok or, if there is no outcome, when its final ledger status matches the decision (agents/core/routers/skills.py:905-919). So an approved proposal that could not be applied is reported ok=false and counted as failed, with the reason: drifted_since_proposal, apply_error when the apply raised, curator_unavailable, or not_applied:<status>. Tests in tests/test_h331_pending_skill_review.py:308-384 cover a drifted proposal, a curator that raised, an empty outcome, a missing curator for both approve and reject, and a race where another pass marks the proposal stale first.

reviews.summary: Import-once stays the only way a Hermes / OpenClaw / Claude Code skill enters Nerva's skills tree (no live-scanned external_dirs tier; SkillLoader.discover() is unchanged), and a re-run of `python scripts/nerva_import.py` now notices upstream movement instead of reporting a blanket skipped/exists. Each imported skill is re-detected against the absolute source_path and sha256 recorded in its manifest.json (importer.py:955, importer.py:1000): unchanged; changed, with the old and new digests plus a bounded line diff shown by --json; moved to another folder of the same install and followed (importer.py:934); removed; renamed; unreadable; or source_untrusted when a record names a file outside the install, which is then never read (importer.py:1290). The default run is a dry run. `--apply --update` re-imports only changed skills that this source imported (importer.py:1065): the current copy is backed up under data/imports/skill_backups, PENDING_REVIEW is written before the new bytes land, SKILL.sig and the legacy approval marker are cleared, and the owner's approval is revoked. A linked control file, an unusable backup dir or a refused save fails closed, and the write is bound to the probed digest. Every import and re-import crosses skill.install through the real Action Kernel at the shipped CLI (nerva_import.py:577, bound at nerva_import.py:1044 and as the ImportRunner default at nerva_import.py:682), behind SKILL_IMPORT_CONTRACT (nerva_import.py:145). The persisted kill switch is re-read on every decision, so an engaged halt refuses an import or re-import before a byte moves. The external origin keeps a policy GRANT at QUEUE, and only GRANT or QUEUE writes (nerva_import.py:764), so every write lands quarantined. The human summary names a local edit that --update replaces (with its backup path), a failed revoke, and moved, untrusted and refused rows (nerva_import.py:938). Tests in test_nerva_import.py: 44 passed and 1 live-gated skip under python 3.11 and 3.12. They include test_cli_skill_writes_cross_the_real_kernel_and_honour_the_kill_switch, test_runner_default_authorizer_is_the_kernel_for_skills_and_queue_for_memory, test_source_moved_within_the_install_is_followed_not_reported_removed, test_apply_update_reimports_changed_skill_into_quarantine_and_revokes_approval, test_rescan_never_follows_a_record_outside_the_install and test_reimport_refuses_a_linked_control_file_and_never_writes_through_it. Two known limits sit outside the accepted requirement. (1) The CLI binds no durable audit sink, so each kernel decision is recorded only on its report row (kernel/kernel_reason) and in the in-process kernel metrics. (2) A record written before this change with a cwd-relative source_path (relative --home) is not rewritten by an unchanged re-run. From another directory it reads skipped/exists plus source_untrusted until a changed source is re-imported with --apply --update, which records the absolute path.

reviews.summary:
Every loaded skill has a CapabilityRecord in the capability registry (agents/core/observability/capability_registry.py:423-463). The record is WIRED when the skill module ran and SEAM when it did not, names the owner agent and requires/supports, carries a verification ref (agents/core/capability_verification.py:47-48) and a RollbackContract that states its own limit: disabling prevents future use but does not undo completed effects. Acquired packages get their own records. The owner reads the registry at GET /api/capabilities (agents/core/routers/analytics.py:244) and the skills at GET /skills (agents/core/routers/skills.py:39).

Usage counters. A sidecar store keeps use, view, patch and switch-on counters with a last-time stamp for each, plus origin, lifecycle state and the pin (agents/core/skills/usage.py:34-39, bump at agents/core/skills/usage.py:96-111). usage_summary turns one skill's row into the owner-facing block: use_count, view_count, patch_count, last_used_at, last_viewed_at, last_patched_at, origin, state, pinned (agents/core/skills/usage.py:158-197). It is read-only: listing a skill never creates a sidecar row, and a skill the sidecar never saw, or no usable sidecar at all, reads as zeros instead of failing the listing. Three paths feed the counters. A skill run bumps use through the skill's own hook, only after the readiness and owner-switch checks pass (agents/core/skills/loader.py:610-614, hook wiring at agents/core/skills/loader.py:800-802 and agents/core/skills/loader.py:648-656). A skill_view the model was actually served bumps view; every refusal returns before that line (agents/core/skills/tools.py:764-770, through SkillLoader.note_usage at agents/core/skills/loader.py:658-671). An applied skill batch, whether the owner's route or an approved proposal, bumps patch once for each skill it edited in place, and nothing for a created or deleted skill, a dry run, a refusal or a rolled-back swap (agents/core/skills/batch.py:658-674, called at agents/core/skills/batch.py:797). All three are best-effort, so a broken sidecar never fails the call that asked.

The owner sees the counters in three places. GET /skills puts the block on every skill (agents/core/routers/skills.py:77-78). The capability record carries the same block in detail.usage (agents/core/observability/capability_registry.py:454-460). nerva skills list appends a suffix such as 'used 3x (last 2026-10-20 08:15 UTC) . patched 1x', or 'never used' (agents/cli/nerva.py:2625-2650, applied at agents/cli/nerva.py:2692-2693); an older hub without the block lists as before. The suffix shows use and patch counts and the last-run time; the view count and the other stamps are in the JSON of GET /skills and of the record. Pinned by tests/test_skills_api.py:257-307, tests/test_capability_registry.py:204-225, tests/test_h318_skill_tools.py:622-670, tests/test_skill_batch.py:791-854 and tests/test_h329_skill_switches.py:903-919.

Reality evidence, with the accepted scope stated. Each skill record gets detail.evidence after the harness verdict and the manual override have had their say (agents/core/observability/capability_registry.py:130-152, ordering at agents/core/observability/capability_registry.py:542-543). Its status is ref_only by default (the ref names the harness case and nothing has run it since boot) and verified only after a green run in this process; it also carries harness_id, last_verified, promotion_scope in_process_only, and the route that runs the case. The owner can trigger a run: POST /api/capabilities/skills/{name}/verify, admin-guarded, runs the same single case the CI lane builds (agents/core/observability/reality_harness.py:729-747) through run_reality and the same promotion path, answers 404 for an unloaded skill, and returns the pass or fail verdict with the refreshed record (agents/core/routers/analytics.py:258-298). A green probe promotes that skill's record to VERIFIED, a red one un-verifies it. The CLI verb is nerva skills verify NAME, which prints the verdict and exits 1 on a red probe (with or without --json) (agents/cli/nerva.py:406-409, agents/cli/nerva.py:2653-2672). Pinned by tests/test_capability_registry.py:228-253 (ref-only default, verdict shown, a seam stays ref-only), tests/test_capability_registry.py:269-309 (guard, 503/404, real harness case promotes in process, stub reported honestly) and tests/test_h329_skill_switches.py:922-943.

Accepted scope: verification stays in-process only. The verdict lives until the hub's next boot, nothing is written to disk, and the durable GAP-9 ledger is deliberately not read back (agents/core/observability/reality_evidence.py:10-14); tests/test_reality_evidence.py:198-232 pins that no production module imports that ledger, so a persisted green run cannot resurrect VERIFIED after a boot. This is the row's allowed 'keep verification honestly ref-only' scope, made owner-triggerable, not a durable certification. The probe only checks that the skill is discovered and its runtime module is loaded (the same meaning as WIRED); it does not exercise the skill's commands, call a live provider or touch hardware, and no live provider or hardware certification is claimed. A Markdown-only or quarantined skill with no module fails the probe and stays SEAM.

Other honest limits: the sidecar exists only when the orchestrator's learning init succeeded (otherwise every skill reads zeros); the HUD does not show the counters or the evidence status (the owner reads them through GET /skills, GET /api/capabilities and the CLI); and the verify route is admin-only with no HUD button.

reviews.summary:
Nerva now reads each provider's quota off every cloud response and shares a 429 with every process. agents/core/llm/quota.py holds the rules. llm_async_client, the one constructor every cloud backend's HTTP client goes through (Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, xAI, the Responses dialect, VLM), now hangs two hooks (agents/core/llm/egress.py:99-100). response_hook (agents/core/llm/quota.py:338) reads the provider's own quota headers with parse_headers (agents/core/llm/quota.py:146): OpenAI-style x-ratelimit-{limit,remaining,reset}-{requests,tokens}; Anthropic's anthropic-ratelimit-{requests,tokens,input-tokens,output-tokens}-{limit,remaining,reset}; and retry-after as seconds or an HTTP date read as UTC. It understands resets given as durations ("6m0s", "20ms") or RFC 3339 times, and it stores the latest numbers per backend, key and model. On a 429 it blocks that backend, key and model (request_model, agents/core/llm/quota.py:78: Gemini's path, else the JSON body's model), or the whole key when the request names no model, until the provider's retry-after, else 30 s, never over 900 s (QuotaStore.block, agents/core/llm/quota.py:207). request_hook (agents/core/llm/quota.py:317) runs before the egress recorder on every request. It refuses a request whose model or whole key is held with ProviderRateLimited before it is sent, so a refused request never reaches the provider or the egress ledger. Another key in the pool is not held: on a refusal the Anthropic backend (_post_messages, and the stream, which retries a refused open on the next key) and the Gemini backend (generate, tool turn, stream) fail over to the next key as on a 429, and ProviderRateLimited carries retry_in, so AuthProfilePool.report_failure(key, cooldown=retry_in) keeps the held key cool for its whole hold (agents/core/llm/anthropic.py:106, agents/core/llm/gemini.py:214, agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:159). The H380 provider probe reports a held key as rate_limited, sends nothing, and caches that verdict no longer than the hold and at most 30 s (agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:191). Retry-after and reset values must be finite ('inf', 'nan' and overflowing numbers are unreadable), a negative retry-after is unreadable so the 30 s default applies, and a reset time without a zone is read as UTC. The store drops its pre-model tables once. A local host is never tracked or held, even when the same backend is held in the cloud. The state lives in one SQLite file under the data folder (QuotaStore, agents/core/llm/quota.py:173), so the hub, the CLI, the scheduler and any worker see the same numbers and the same holds. A key is known only by a 12-hex fingerprint of its hash, and every failure is swallowed, so a quota reader never breaks a request. usage (agents/core/llm/quota.py:361) gives each backend's requests and tokens left, the fraction left (clamped, none for a missing or non-positive limit), time to reset and any hold. It is served by GET /api/llm/quota (agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:439, admin, 503 quota_unavailable when unreadable or when a row cannot be serialised; each row carries its model, which /usage and the panel name), the HUD Provider Quota panel (frontend/src/panels/provider-quota.tsx, Admin group: bars, numbers, reset times, a hold tag), and /usage (agents/core/commands.py:243, admin tier, rendered by render). The router is not fed a forecast; Hermes' own guard is likewise a refusal before the request, which is what this does. tests/conftest.py gives each test its own quota store, so a mocked 429 never holds a later test (tests/conftest.py:187). tests/test_h373_provider_quota.py (78 cases) covers durations, retry-after (seconds, dates, no zone under another host timezone), OpenAI and Anthropic headers, unreadable values, key fingerprints, and the store: latest numbers, clamping, a negative limit, blocks with retry-after, the default and cap, a hold before numbers, two processes, damaged data and the default path. It also covers the hooks on a real llm_async_client (recording, no headers, a 429 hold refused before dialling and absent from the egress ledger, another key, the default hold, other errors, a local model, a local request of a held backend, a failing store), the local-host test, the hook order, rendering, the admin route and the admin /usage command. The review round added the fail-over on a refusal for both backends and their streams, the cooldown floor, per-model holds, finite and signed header values, zone-less resets, the route's serialisation, and the probe's held key (tests/test_h380_provider_probe.py). frontend/src/test/provider-quota-panel.test.tsx has 3 cases. There are 50 mutants, all killed; the review round's 18 mutants, all killed (5 by tests added after a first pass).

reviews.summary:
Choosing a model now passes one registry of guards, server-side and before the choice is stored, on every surface that picks a model, as Hermes' selection-guard registry does. agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py holds the registry: register (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:123) adds a guard, and evaluate (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:175) runs every guard once per choice, so a new guard appears on every surface at once. enforce (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:186) returns the findings once all are cleared, or raises SelectionRefused naming every finding and the flags still missing. A flag clears only a literal true. Two guards ship. The cost guard (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:130) asks confirm_expensive for a model whose output costs at least llm.cost_confirm_usd_per_mtok (agents/core/settings_db.py:208; $40 per million tokens by default, 0 never asks, in safe mode the stricter of it and $40 (0, never asking, takes the $40; H490), a negative value refused on write at agents/core/settings_db.py:1166, an unreadable one read as $40). It names the input and output prices from cost_estimator.MODELS; price_of (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:84) prices a routed slug (vendor/model) or a variant (model:beta) by its model, and an unpriced model is not asked. The data-policy guard (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:153) asks acknowledge_training for a model or route whose vendor may train on the prompts. ProviderProfile now declares data_policy, one of DATA_POLICIES (agents/core/llm/providers/__init__.py:30: local, no-training, trains-on-inputs, unknown), with a note and per-model glob rows (data_policy_for, agents/core/llm/providers/__init__.py:84), validated at construction and served in status() (agents/core/llm/providers/__init__.py:155). LM Studio and Ollama are local; Anthropic and OpenAI Responses are no-training by their API terms; Gemini is unknown with a note (an unbilled key's prompts may be used); OpenRouter is unknown, with its :free variants trains-on-inputs (agents/core/llm/providers/__init__.py:243); llm.openrouter_data_collection=allow is a trains-on-inputs route choice. A pin with no provider is checked against every profile's model rows. The acknowledgement is a consent event: record (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:229) writes a model_training_consent row to the audit log before the choice is stored, naming the surface, the setting and the model, and a choice whose consent row cannot be written is not stored (ConsentNotRecorded). A cost confirmation writes a model_cost_confirmed row naming the price, best-effort. Nothing is stored with the choice, so the next choice asks again. The surfaces: the admin settings PUT (agents/core/routers/admin.py:195; AdminPutBody takes confirm_expensive / acknowledge_training as StrictBool, agents/core/routers/admin.py:112) and the settings import (agents/core/routers/admin.py:365; its dry run lists what the guards would ask) go through _guard_selection (agents/core/routers/admin.py:170), 409 selection_guard when not cleared, 503 when the consent cannot be recorded. choices_from_settings (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:256) reads llm.claude_model, llm.gemini_model, the compatible provider/model pair (either half changed, the other read from the store) and the OpenRouter data-collection switch; an ordinary write is not asked even with an expensive model stored. A job's model pin is guarded on create and edit (agents/core/routers/jobs.py:78), only when the pin changes, and the confirmation is never stored with the job. nerva config set (agents/cli/nerva.py:1381) runs the same guards, names the flags --confirm-expensive / --acknowledge-training, and writes its rows through the hub's audit log opened from its own process (agents/cli/nerva.py:94). nerva jobs create/edit pass the flags to the hub and name them on a 409 (agents/cli/nerva.py:104). reviews.summary: A configured cloud key is checked with its provider before a turn finds out. agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py asks each cloud provider once, with the key the hub would use (configured_key, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:87: for Anthropic and Gemini, the only providers with an AuthProfilePool (POOLED), the first of the `<VAR>S` pool split on commas and whitespace as the router splits it, else `<VAR>`; every other provider reads `<VAR>` only). The command center asks with the key the route's backend holds: the pool's current key for Claude and Gemini, the compatible backend's own api_key otherwise. It sends one authenticated GET (request_for, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:105): Anthropic /v1/models with x-api-key and anthropic-version, Gemini /v1beta/models with x-goog-api-key, OpenRouter `<base>/key` (its model list is public; the key record answers 401 to a key it does not know), and `<base>/models` with a bearer for the other OpenAI-shaped providers, honouring a configured base URL. The GET goes through llm_async_client, so it is in the egress ledger as `llm:<provider>`, and H368's host-protocol mandate refuses a mismatch before it leaves; the xAI and OpenAI Responses probes use trust_env=False, as their backends do (NO_ENV_TRUST, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:67). Nothing is generated. The verdict (probe, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:223) is one of: `ok` (any 2xx, with the listed model count); `no_listing` (404/405: nothing at that URL, so the key is not proven); `auth_failed` (401, or a 400 whose body names a bad key: Gemini API_KEY_INVALID/API_KEY_EXPIRED, xAI "Incorrect API key"; the body is read inside the probe and never returned); `forbidden` (403); `rate_limited` (429, or a key held by the shared 429 guard of H373, with nothing sent); `error` (any other status, which is named, or an unexpected failure); `unreachable` (any transport error); `refused` (the host mandate); `not_configured` (no key, nothing sent); or `not_cloud` (a local provider). Only `ok` proves the key (WORKING, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:61). The key and the response body are never in a result or a log line. A result is cached per provider, key fingerprint and probed URL, so a changed key or base URL is probed afresh: for TTL_SECONDS (300 s), and a transient verdict (rate_limited, error, unreachable) for TRANSIENT_TTL_SECONDS (30 s) or, for a guard-held key, no longer than its hold (agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:53-56). Concurrent callers, forced ones included, share one in-flight request (_fresh, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:205). A forced re-check inside MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS (30 s) answers the cached verdict marked `throttled`. last (agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:263) reads the cache without a request. probe_all (agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:301) asks every cloud provider concurrently, except one whose key variable belongs to a base URL on another host (_key_for_elsewhere, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:287): an OPENAI_API_KEY beside an OPENAI_BASE_URL on a gateway is not sent to api.openai.com unless llm.compatible_provider is openai-responses. POST /api/admin/llm/providers/probe (admin; admin_llm_providers_probe, agents/core/routers/admin.py:962) checks one provider or all, with `force`; an unknown provider is a 404. The Console's Provider Check panel (Admin; frontend/src/panels/provider-check.tsx) probes nothing until asked. It shows each verdict (`key rejected` with the HTTP status beside it; `key not verified (nothing at this URL)` in amber for no_listing), the model count and a named HTTP status, offers a forced re-check per provider, and says when a re-check was throttled. The command-center model block asks the provider for a selected cloud route (_cloud_probe, agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:224; agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:339) and waits at most CLOUD_PROBE_WAIT_SECONDS (4 s), after which the verdict reads `unreachable` and the probe finishes in the background. The route is ready (`cloud_selected`) on `ok`; `rate_limited` keeps it runnable (`cloud_rate_limited`); `no_listing`, `error` and `unreachable` make it unknown (ready=None, `cloud_no_listing` / `cloud_error` / `cloud_unreachable`); `auth_failed`, `forbidden`, `refused` and `not_configured` make it not runnable (CLOUD_PROBE_REASONS, agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:204). The block carries `cloud_probe` (provider, verdict, status code, time, cached; agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:370), and its hint names the provider, what it said and the HTTP status (_model_hint, agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:391). `nerva doctor`'s runtime_resolves and `nerva status`'s runnable line read that block, so a wrong or revoked key now fails them with its reason instead of passing on "a key is set". tests/test_h380_provider_probe.py (30 cases) covers the request per provider with the key only in a header, the key resolution, one read and its model count across list shapes, nine statuses, three transport failures and an unexpected one, the protocol refusal recorded as not sent, the egress row, no request without a key or for a local provider, no key or body in results or logs, the cache per key with expiry, the throttled and then allowed forced re-check, the cache-only read, probe_all, the admin route (admin-only, one, all, force, 404) and the command center's key choice. tests/test_h380b_provider_probe_review.py (35 cases) covers the review round: OpenRouter asked about its key, not its public list; a gateway key kept away from api.openai.com and OpenAI asked when the key is its own; a 400 that names a bad key; a missing listing that proves nothing; the key read as the router reads it and the compatible backend's own key; a guard-held key rate_limited for the hold; concurrent callers sharing one request; the bounded wait; readiness per verdict and the short cache of a transient one; trust_env matching the backends; the hint; and the cache slot per URL. tests/test_first_run_command_center.py covers every `cloud_*` reason and `cloud_probe` in the model block. The panel has 3 vitest cases. The row's 38 mutants were all killed. The review round's 36 mutants: 29 caught at once, six after six cases were added to tests/test_h380b_provider_probe_review.py (a finished request is not joined again, a caller that stops waiting leaves the verdict cached, a request in flight on another event loop is not awaited, the cache-only read forgets a transient verdict, reset forgets a request in flight, the hint for an unknown provider), and one equivalent (`ready is True` and truthiness agree on True/False/None).
