reviews.remaining: **The documented per-server `env` migration path does not exist as a reachable surface.** `MCPServerConfig` has no `env` field (`routers/mcp.py:145-157`, no `model_config`), `POST /api/admin/mcp` drops the key (pydantic's default `extra="ignore"`), and neither `to_config` (`client.py:910-924`) nor `load_from_config` (`:814-849`) writes or reads one — the module docstring says as much at `client.py:41-45`. The only remedy an owner can actually reach is the **host-wide** `JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV` (`:92-98`, "Host-wide, not per-server"), which is a strictly weaker grant than the per-server one the docs describe: an owner whose forge server needs `GITHUB_TOKEN` must allow it for every stdio server on the host. Whether to ship on that or build the per-server surface first is a product decision, written up as `docs/OWNER_TASKS.md` §P28.3 with both options. **Related and also owner-level:** `XAUTHORITY` and `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` are both on `STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST` (`client.py:174`), and today one is listed-but-silently-dropped (`_SECRET_LIKE` at `:174-176` matches the `AUTH` in `XAUTHORITY`) while the other is listed-and-handed-over — they should be consistent in one direction or the other. **And the honest ceiling, stated wherever the guarantee is:** this is **defence in depth, not a security boundary**, and since #1179 the module states that ceiling by TWO routes rather than one (`client.py:17-36`). The child is same-UID with no namespace, so a server that can run a subprocess reads the withheld variables straight out of `/proc/<ppid>/environ`; and the baseline narrows the **filesystem** not at all — `cwd` defaults to the hub's own working directory, so `open(".env")` hands back exactly the keys that were withheld, which `cwd_secret_files()` now says out loud at connect (WARNING, filenames only, `client.py:585-591`) rather than leaving the owner to infer a protection from the withheld count alone. What the baseline buys is that a *careless* or *curious* server does not get them by accident, and that an owner's `JARVIS_*` settings are not ambient in a third party's process. It does not stop an adversary, and the row says so rather than implying otherwise; closing the filesystem route as well as the `/proc` one needs real process isolation (separate UID, namespace or container — `client.py:33-36`), which is not shipped. **Unaddressed from the row:** there is no refusal of an MCP entry that is a backdoor wearing an MCP costume — no command allow-listing, no signature or provenance check on the spawned binary (the docstring itself calls the screener "still-unshipped", `client.py:34`), and `POST /api/admin/mcp` still stores `req.command` verbatim after checking only transport, trust tier, tool-filter shape and bounds, and duplicate name (`routers/mcp.py:188-241`, `:184`); the only shape check is `_command_argv()`'s shell-metacharacter/NUL refusal at connect (`client.py:539-549`), which is not a screener. #1179 changed none of this — it explicitly chose disclosure over refusal. This slice hardens what the child *receives*; the row also asks who the child is allowed to *be*.

reviews.summary: archive_safe is the only module in Nerva that reads an archive. Backup verify and restore unpack through extract_tar_path (agents/core/archive_safe.py:573; agents/core/backup.py:809, agents/core/backup.py:887). Marketplace install_from_zip unpacks through extract_zip_bytes (agents/core/archive_safe.py:637; agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:816). The old backup._safe_extract and the marketplace _safe_targets+extractall pass are gone. An AST scan (tests/test_archive_safe.py:702, with probes at tests/test_archive_safe.py:688) fails when any other product module imports tarfile or zipfile outside a write-only allowlist, opens an archive for reading or calls an extract-family method. normalize_member (agents/core/archive_safe.py:122) folds backslash to '/' first. It then refuses empty, NUL, POSIX-absolute, Windows-absolute, UNC and drive-lettered names, and any '..' or empty part. Only regular files and directories are written. Symlink, hardlink, device, fifo and sparse tar members raise (agents/core/archive_safe.py:504), and so do symlink, device, fifo, socket and encrypted zip entries (agents/core/archive_safe.py:596). _Planner (agents/core/archive_safe.py:182) validates every member before the first write: name, type, in-archive conflicts and duplicates, member count and declared bytes (agents/core/archive_safe.py:257). It also checks the destination's existing content (agents/core/archive_safe.py:286): a link on the way to a member is refused, and so is a directory where a file goes (tests/test_archive_safe.py:365, tests/test_backup.py:471). The pre-scan reads the stream to its end (agents/core/archive_safe.py:522), so a bad gzip CRC, trailing data or a corrupt header part-way through is a refusal, not a shortened tree (tests/test_archive_safe.py:482, tests/test_archive_safe.py:517). Bytes are counted again while streaming (agents/core/archive_safe.py:389). The byte budget is clamped to free space plus the blocks of the single-link files the archive replaces (agents/core/archive_safe.py:314), so an in-place --force restore fits (tests/test_backup.py:443). PAX and GNU long-name header payloads are capped before tarfile reads them, 1 MiB each and 256 MiB in total (agents/core/archive_safe.py:461, agents/core/archive_safe.py:483; tests/test_backup.py:515). A link or hardlinked name at a member's path is unlinked and the file is created O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, never written through (agents/core/archive_safe.py:373; tests/test_archive_safe.py:323, tests/test_archive_safe.py:349). Backups take their caps from JARVIS_BACKUP_MAX_MEMBERS and JARVIS_BACKUP_MAX_BYTES (agents/core/backup.py:142); skill packages use SKILL_PACKAGE_LIMITS (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:42). On the producing side, create_backup writes both the encrypted and the plaintext branch through atomic_write, a sibling temp file that is fsynced and then os.replace'd (agents/core/archive_safe.py:654; agents/core/backup.py:584, agents/core/backup.py:589). Archives are GNU-format tar (agents/core/backup.py:643). The export walk skips symlinks (agents/core/archive_safe.py:715; agents/core/backup.py:562). publish_skill uses it on the staged copy it signs (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:392); the copy itself is built from the bytes of one source snapshot, which refuses a linked folder, a link or non-regular member and a file that changed while read (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:375), which has its own test (tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:219). Every other name, hardlinked ones included, is archived as its own regular member (agents/core/backup.py:603, agents/core/backup.py:627; tests/test_backup.py:388). verify and restore compare the manifest's file_count with what the archive held (agents/core/backup.py:836; tests/test_backup.py:430). install_from_zip stages inside skills_dir, runs the signature gate there, and only then renames the tree into place (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:854, agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:885). A non-zip upload is a 400 refusal (tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:194). Staging left by a killed install is swept once it is an hour old (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:773; tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:203). Restore is no longer only an operator CLI action. An admin route (agents/core/routers/backup.py:98) queues a backup.restore card at the irreversible tier (agents/core/backup.py:1580); after a human accepts it, the staged restore is applied by apply_pending_restore (agents/core/backup.py:1430) from the boot hook (serve.py:123) or the offline nerva backup restore (agents/cli/nerva.py:1776). That path still unpacks through restore_backup with force (agents/core/backup.py:1558), so every extract_tar_path check above applies (tests/test_backup_inplace_restore.py:270, tests/test_backup_inplace_restore.py:293). The module CLI restore prints 'partial restore' when a failure came after the first write (agents/core/backup.py:1777; tests/test_backup.py:484) and 'nothing restored' only when nothing from the archive was written: a pre-scan refusal (agents/core/backup.py:1781; tests/test_backup.py:259), or a refusal before extraction starts, a key that cannot decrypt the archive or a non-empty target without --force (agents/core/backup.py:1782, agents/core/backup.py:1784; tests/test_backup_cli.py:137, tests/test_backup_cli.py:154). The CLI verify and restore take a name from list or a path whose real location is an archive directly in the backups directory; a copy elsewhere, a '..' out of it or a link out of it names no backup, so the CLI cannot point the extractor at an arbitrary file (agents/core/backup.py:754, agents/core/backup.py:1769; tests/test_backup_cli.py:97). The admin restore card and the staged apply take only a name matched against the backups listing (agents/core/backup.py:1586, agents/core/backup.py:1538). tests/test_backup.py:606 pins that no other product module, script or subprocess calls restore_backup directly, and tests/test_backup_inplace_restore.py:414 pins that only serve.py and agents/cli/nerva.py call apply_pending_restore. The pre-scan also refuses a component longer than the destination's NAME_MAX or a path past PATH_MAX, which the existing-path walk cannot see under a new directory (agents/core/archive_safe.py:251; tests/test_archive_safe.py:726), and a write the destination refuses mid-restore (permissions, a full disk) is a named ArchiveRejected marked partial, never a traceback (agents/core/archive_safe.py:445; tests/test_archive_safe.py:738). A restore leaves the archive's manifest in the target; create_backup never archives a top-level backup_manifest.json from the data root (agents/core/backup.py:651), so a backup of a restored root carries one manifest and verifies, restores and serves the forget purge's verified pre-snapshot (tests/test_backup.py:640, tests/test_backup.py:679). A backup of a restored root made before this change carries that name twice; verify and restore accept exactly that one repeat, last wins as tarfile resolved it, and count the dropped copy against the manifest's file_count (agents/core/backup.py:810, agents/core/backup.py:853; tests/test_backup.py:655). The repeat is bounded: the dropped copy still counts against the member and byte caps, and a third copy or any other duplicate is refused (agents/core/archive_safe.py:220, agents/core/archive_safe.py:223; tests/test_archive_safe.py:768, tests/test_archive_safe.py:775, tests/test_archive_safe.py:790). Known limit: backups made on main from a data root holding a symlink or hardlink fail verify and restore by design. Model egress uses an explicit trust context: llm_async_client in agents/core/llm/egress.py (agents/core/llm/egress.py:107-109, :139-141) sets verify=verify_for(backend, base_url) as an SSLContext, and the Anthropic, OpenAI Responses and xAI backends all build their clients through it (anthropic.py:69, responses.py:50, xai.py:48); plugin clients use verify=tls_verify() with trust_env=False (agents/core/http_client.py:288-289). Invalid CA paths never imply verify=False. Per-target insecure overrides (JARVIS_TLS_INSECURE_TARGETS, verify_for at agents/core/tls_trust.py:252) are explicit, loudly logged with the URL, and ignored with an ERROR in hardened mode (agents/core/tls_trust.py:222-231, :261-268). Functional adaptation retained from the existing implementation: custom bundles may contain a valid short EC or pinned self-signed certificate; the 1024-byte minimum is reserved for the multi-root certifi bundle. reviews.summary: **The write half, as a generic mechanism rather than a special case.** `agents/core/tool_rpc.py` gains a registrar-owned *call classifier*: a gated tool may register a pure function over one call's args returning bounded labels. `handle()` stamps them onto the durable approval card's payload and appends the notice to the card title; `execute()` re-derives them from the args about to run and refuses with `approval_class_mismatch` unless the approved card carried the same `class` — so a card approved as a scratch note cannot be redeemed against a write to SOUL.md. `_classify` fails closed (a raising, non-Mapping, over-long or non-alphanumeric result refuses the call rather than letting it through unlabelled) and strips the reserved `tool`/`args`/`target` keys so labels cannot rewrite the card's identity. `agents/core/file_tools.py` registers `FileTools.classify_mutation` for `file_write` and `file_delete`, matches on the BASENAME in any directory inside the roots (an instruction file is wherever the harness that reads it looks — `_load_soul` alone searches three), carries a `steers_future_runs` flag into the kernel Action payload, and adds a secondary floor in `_mutate`. A sandboxed script cannot label its own write nor strip the label off one: the classifier is registrar-owned and `handle()` returns `approval_required` before the handler is ever reached. **The review found one major and it is fixed here.** The roster omitted `HEARTBEAT.md` and `HEARTBEAT.local.md` — the files in this repo that *literally* schedule future runs: `core/heartbeat.py` scans every agent directory for them, prefers the gitignored `.local` overlay exactly as `SOUL.local.md` does, and turns what it finds into cron-scheduled agent runs. Reproduced against a real `ToolRPCServer`: a write to `HEARTBEAT.local.md` produced `class=None` and the generic title "Tool 'file_write' via RPC" — a card byte-identical to a write to a scratch note, for an action that installs a cron expression driving every later run. Both names are in the class now, and the roster is pinned against `heartbeat.py`'s own source rather than restated, so a loader that learns a new name fails the test instead of silently escaping the class. The exact-set pin beside it was tightened, not loosened. **Widened by #1177 (the #1161–#1174 adversarial review) — same mechanism, larger class, re-assessed here.** The roster is now `INSTRUCTION_BASE_NAMES` (`soul.md`, `agents.md`, `claude.md`, `gemini.md`, `.cursorrules`, `heartbeat.md`) and every `.md` name's gitignored `.local` overlay is *derived* by `_local_overlay` into `INSTRUCTION_FILE_NAMES` (eleven names) instead of being spelled out by hand — which is what brought `CLAUDE.local.md` / `AGENTS.local.md` / `GEMINI.local.md` into the class; the first cut listed only the SOUL and HEARTBEAT overlays, so a `CLAUDE.local.md` write — same harness, same authority, and it wins over the committed file — asked with the title of a scratch note. `looks_instruction_name` now also matches by extension through `INSTRUCTION_FILE_SUFFIXES = (".mdc",)`, so Cursor's freely-named `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` files, the format that superseded `.cursorrules`, are in the class as well. `classify_mutation`, the `steers_future_runs` flag, `_authorize`, the `_mutate` floor and `register_file_tools` are unchanged, and `tool_rpc.py` is byte-identical. reviews.summary:
Code the agent writes is checked against a table of known-dangerous patterns, and the findings go back to the model and the owner. Nothing is ever refused. agents/core/code_guidance.py holds 26 rules (RULES, agents/core/code_guidance.py:89), each scoped to the file types it applies to. They cover unsafe deserialization (pickle/dill/joblib/marshal loads; yaml.load without SafeLoader, and yaml.unsafe_load; torch.load without weights_only=True); command and code injection (os.system/popen, shell=True, Python eval/exec, JS eval and new Function, child_process.exec and execSync, require('child_process').exec, a bare exec( in a file that imports child_process, a Go exec.Command of a shell); SQL built from an f-string or `%`; tempfile.mktemp; XSS sinks (innerHTML/outerHTML assignment, document.write, dangerouslySetInnerHTML); and crypto and TLS footguns (ECB mode, createCipher without an IV on any receiver, verify=False, unverified SSL contexts, CERT_NONE, rejectUnauthorized: false, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, InsecureSkipVerify: true, md5/sha1 over a password). They also cover XXE parser flags and a remote `<script>` without integrity=. A separate check (_workflow_findings, agents/core/code_guidance.py:189) flags `${{ github.event.* }}` inside a GitHub Actions `run:` step, on the run line or in its `|`/`>` block, whose column is the run key's own, so a `- run: |` step's env:, with: and if: keys end it and are never flagged. The guards keep the usual false positives quiet: `model.eval()` and `obj.eval()`, `def eval(`, `yaml.load(..., Loader=SafeLoader)`, `torch.load(..., weights_only=True)`, `regex.exec()`, an `===` comparison with innerHTML, `hashlib.md5(data)`, a script with integrity=, whole-line comments and non-code files. Every rule is linear: a guard reads the call's balanced arguments across lines, at most MAX_CALL_CHARS (400) of them and at most MAX_CALLS_PER_LINE (8) calls a line (_call_args, agents/core/code_guidance.py:211; _guarded, agents/core/code_guidance.py:226), or the tag it matched. scan (agents/core/code_guidance.py:265) returns `{rule, line, message}`, at most 20 findings over the first 1 MB, with lines split at `\n` only (CRLF and CR normalised), and stops after SCAN_SECONDS (0.5 s; agents/core/code_guidance.py:50); a scan cut by size or time ends with a `scan-incomplete` finding at the first line it did not finish, so a cut scan never reads as clean. `.env`, `.env.*` and the shell dotfiles are scanned as shell. The findings go to five places. On the file_write approval card, FileTools.classify_mutation (agents/core/file_tools.py:1561) adds `code_warnings` (rule@line, at most 200 characters), `code_warning_count` and a title notice (`code not fully scanned` when a limit cut it), scanning the name as spelled and the file the write lands on (a symlink, a `./` or `//` spelling; labels, agents/core/code_guidance.py:296, names each finding once and in line order); it never sets a class, so H506's approval binding is untouched, and an instruction-file notice and the warning share the title. The gated call's `approval_required` answer carries `code_warnings`/`code_warning_count` (_ANSWER_LABEL_KEYS, agents/core/tool_rpc.py:213), and the tool loop's pause reply names them as warnings, not refusals (_approval_reply, agents/core/agent_runtime.py:2044): the loop ends the turn there, so the model reads them on its next turn and the owner at once. On an ungated write's result (FileTools.write_file, agents/core/file_tools.py:1308), the model reads `code_warnings` with a `code_guidance` note that they are warnings; an approved write's result lands on the approved task's record, which no model turn reads. A refused write carries none, and a failing scan never fails a write. For a marketplace install (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:858; install and install-zip answer `code_warnings` when there are any, agents/core/routers/skills.py:495) and a generated skill (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1267), scan_tree (agents/core/code_guidance.py:340) walks the folder, skipping symlinks; only code files count toward its 200-file bound, a file past 1 MB is read as cut, the whole walk stops after TREE_SECONDS (2 s), and the file a bound stops at gets a `scan-incomplete` finding. skill_propose answers the generated skill's `code_warnings` (agents/core/skills/tools.py:891), and generate_skill resets them first (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1107), so a skipped generation never keeps another's; the background-review and [learn:] generation paths only log them (their main.py is a fixed template). The owner's switch is `security.code_guidance` (read by enabled, agents/core/code_guidance.py:161: on by default, only an explicit off turns it off and an unreadable store keeps it on; the settings row is seeded on in settings_db DEFAULTS, and safe mode forces it back on: safe_mode.FORCED_SETTINGS, agents/core/safe_mode.py:117). An aliased child_process module (`cp.exec`) is not flagged. tests/test_h507_code_guidance.py (136 cases) covers every rule firing, the guard cases, the cross-language scoping, the finding shape, the table size, the workflow rule with a blank line in a block and every non-run key, the bounds, the labels, the switch, the real ToolRPC card and approved execution, a clean and a non-code write, the shared instruction notice, a failing scan, a refused write, scan_tree (symlink, bounds, switch), generation, install with the route, and the setting row. The review round added crafted megabytes (one per quadratic rule) scanned in under a second and a card labelled promptly through the ToolRPC intake, the time and size cuts, the pause reply driven through the agent loop, skill_propose's warnings and the reset, the symlink and path spellings, a package padded with assets, the `- run: |` block, the wrapped and nested calls, the child_process and createCipher spellings, CR/form-feed/U+2028 lines, the dotfiles and the safe-mode switch. A separate check (_workflow_findings, agents/core/code_guidance.py:189) flags `${{ github.event.* }}` inside a GitHub Actions `run:` step, on the run line or in its `|`/`>` block, whose column is the run key's own, so a `- run: |` step's env:, with: and if: keys end it and are never flagged. The guards keep the usual false positives quiet: `model.eval()` and `obj.eval()`, `def eval(`, `yaml.load(..., Loader=SafeLoader)`, `torch.load(..., weights_only=True)`, `regex.exec()`, an `===` comparison with innerHTML, `hashlib.md5(data)`, a script with integrity=, whole-line comments and non-code files. Every rule is linear: a guard reads the call's balanced arguments across lines, at most MAX_CALL_CHARS (400) of them and at most MAX_CALLS_PER_LINE (8) calls a line (_call_args, agents/core/code_guidance.py:211; _guarded, agents/core/code_guidance.py:226), or the tag it matched. scan (agents/core/code_guidance.py:265) returns `{rule, line, message}`, at most 20 findings over the first 1 MB, with lines split at `\n` only (CRLF and CR normalised), and stops after SCAN_SECONDS (0.5 s; agents/core/code_guidance.py:50); a scan cut by size or time ends with a `scan-incomplete` finding at the first line it did not finish, so a cut scan never reads as clean. `.env`, `.env.*` and the shell dotfiles are scanned as shell. The findings go to five places. On the file_write approval card, FileTools.classify_mutation (agents/core/file_tools.py:1561) adds `code_warnings` (rule@line, at most 200 characters), `code_warning_count` and a title notice (`code not fully scanned` when a limit cut it), scanning the name as spelled and the file the write lands on (a symlink, a `./` or `//` spelling; labels, agents/core/code_guidance.py:296, names each finding once and in line order); it never sets a class, so H506's approval binding is untouched, and an instruction-file notice and the warning share the title. The gated call's `approval_required` answer carries `code_warnings`/`code_warning_count` (_ANSWER_LABEL_KEYS, agents/core/tool_rpc.py:213), and the tool loop's pause reply names them as warnings, not refusals (_approval_reply, agents/core/agent_runtime.py:2044): the loop ends the turn there, so the model reads them on its next turn and the owner at once. On an ungated write's result (FileTools.write_file, agents/core/file_tools.py:1308), the model reads `code_warnings` with a `code_guidance` note that they are warnings; an approved write's result lands on the approved task's record, which no model turn reads. A refused write carries none, and a failing scan never fails a write. For a marketplace install (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:858; install and install-zip answer `code_warnings` when there are any, agents/core/routers/skills.py:495) and a generated skill (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1267), scan_tree (agents/core/code_guidance.py:340) walks the folder, skipping symlinks; only code files count toward its 200-file bound, a file past 1 MB is read as cut, the whole walk stops after TREE_SECONDS (2 s), and the file a bound stops at gets a `scan-incomplete` finding. skill_propose answers the generated skill's `code_warnings` (agents/core/skills/tools.py:891), and generate_skill resets them first (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1107), so a skipped generation never keeps another's; the background-review and [learn:] generation paths only log them (their main.py is a fixed template). The owner's switch is `security.code_guidance` (read by enabled, agents/core/code_guidance.py:161: on by default, only an explicit off turns it off and an unreadable store keeps it on; the settings row is seeded on in settings_db DEFAULTS, and safe mode forces it back on: safe_mode.FORCED_SETTINGS, agents/core/safe_mode.py:117). An aliased child_process module (`cp.exec`) is not flagged. tests/test_h507_code_guidance.py (136 cases) covers every rule firing, the guard cases, the cross-language scoping, the finding shape, the table size, the workflow rule with a blank line in a block and every non-run key, the bounds, the labels, the switch, the real ToolRPC card and approved execution, a clean and a non-code write, the shared instruction notice, a failing scan, a refused write, scan_tree (symlink, bounds, switch), generation, install with the route, and the setting row. reviews.summary: Reviewed against live code; the inherited 2026-09-07 "partial" verdict stands, but for a different and much smaller reason than the audit recorded. The audit's "no Host-header validation anywhere" is stale: agents/core/host_policy.py is a 204-line module whose docstring (:4-22) names DNS rebinding explicitly, with normalize_host() at :54, parse_allowed_hosts() at :104 refusing a `*` entry at :119-120 and a leading-dot suffix wildcard at :121-122, host_accepted() at :157-181 matching loopback names, any IP literal, JARVIS_HOST, the ASGI scope's arrival address and JARVIS_ALLOWED_HOSTS, and assert_parseable_allowed_hosts() at :184 refusing boot on an unparseable list. It is wired at agents/web.py:20 (import) and agents/web.py:903-923 (`_host_guard`, returning {"error": "host not allowed", "code": 400}), registered so it runs before the rate limiter and inside the security-header and golden-signal layers (agents/web.py:877-880). Dumping app.user_middleware on the HEQ lot-1 head gives _golden_signals, _security_headers, _host_guard, _rate_limit, _no_store_for_polling, then lot 1's pure-ASGI _ForwardedProtoMiddleware, which only sets the request scheme and runs inside the guard. The boot guard is genuinely reached on the real serve path: agents/core/boot_guards.py:354, inside enforce_boot_posture, which the lifespan calls at agents/web.py:481-482 after the .env files load (agents/web.py:475-476, H273), so a list that lives only in .env is checked too; assert_front_door runs the same check over a caller's own mapping (agents/core/boot_guards.py:320). Refusal logging is rate-shaped (agents/web.py:886-888, agents/web.py:919) and logs only a coarse peer trust class (agents/web.py:891-900), never the attacker-chosen header value. Driven live on the lot-1 head with a loopback TestClient: `Host: evil.test` gets 400 on /status, /dashboard and /api/agents, where the real host gets 200 on /status and /api/agents. The row's other two asks hold, and lot 1 (H691) tightened the proxy half. Trusted-proxy entries are validated as bounded CIDRs at agents/core/proxy_trust.py:107 and :165 (note :308 only WARNS on a wide entry, it does not refuse). uvicorn's own forwarding-header allowlist (FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, UVICORN_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, --forwarded-allow-ips) now refuses boot from the boot pass, which runs after the .env files load, when an entry is a wildcard, a /0, not an address, or a peer outside JARVIS_TRUSTED_PROXIES and loopback (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:570). serve.py switches uvicorn's proxy-header layer off, X-Forwarded-Proto is believed only from a listed peer, and the rate limiter's localhost exemption now follows the localhost gate's origin (agents/web.py:862), so an unlisted same-box proxy is throttled. reviews.remaining: The Host guard exempts _PROBE_PATHS (agents/web.py:839, applied at agents/web.py:907-908), so /healthz, /readyz and /metrics answer a rebound name: live-verified, `Host: evil.test` returns 200 on /healthz and /metrics and reaches the route on /readyz, while every real API route returns 400. Because DNS rebinding makes the browser treat those responses as same-origin, an attacker page still reads the full Prometheus body (route templates, request counters, latency buckets) and the /readyz body naming the configured LLM backend and the agent/channel counts. The code names this residual itself at agents/web.py:883-885 ("a rebound page can therefore still read the golden-signal counters"). Close it by narrowing the exemption rather than removing it — the operability reason for it is sound. Suggested shape: keep /healthz and /readyz exempt but strip /readyz's detail to a bare ready/not-ready when the Host is not accepted, and require an accepted Host for /metrics unless the request is unambiguously non-browser (no Origin and no Sec-Fetch-Site, or an explicit JARVIS_METRICS_ALLOW_ANY_HOST opt-in for a monitor that scrapes by an unlisted name). Needs a test alongside test_healthz_from_any_host_is_exempt asserting that a refused Host cannot read the counter body. Separately, the row's "no WebSocket variant is needed" premise is now stale: the Kanban events and Hermes runtime upgrades refuse an unaccepted Host before accepting the socket by closing it with the generic policy code 1008, not with Hermes' machine-parseable rejection reasons and close code 4403, and no pinned test drives a rebound Host against either upgrade.

reviews.summary:
A spoken reply sounds like speech rather than read-out markdown, as Hermes requires, at every text-to-speech entry point. agents/core/voice/speech_text.py is the one normaliser (for_speech, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:161). It drops the file-mutation verifier footer (_VERIFIER_FOOTER, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:42), <think>/<thinking>/<reasoning> blocks (an unclosed one to the end, and everything before a closing tag that never opened), fenced code (``` or ~~~, an unclosed fence to the end) and HTML tags. [text](url) reads as its text, ![alt](url) as its alt, and a bare or <autolinked> URL as "link". Headings, list items, task boxes, block quotes and table rows lose their markers and end with a full stop (_line, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:133); table cells read with commas; separator rows and rules are dropped. Bold, italic, strikethrough and inline-code markers go and their words stay (_inline, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:122), with word guards so 2*3*4 and my_var_name survive. Symbols are said in the reply's language (_symbols, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:113, WORDS, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:88): & as and/și, % as percent/la sută, -> => as to/spre, degrees as degrees/grade; the language comes from the request, else a ro-RO voice, else the engine default (speech_lang, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:104). Emoji go: pictographs, flags, keycaps, skin tones, ZWJ sequences, variation selectors and tag flags (_EMOJI, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:70). Fish [emotion] tags are kept intact. Newlines are flattened to one spoken line. Text with no letter or digit left is "" (_SAYABLE, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:85), and the result is a fixed point (checked over every shared case).

Verifier footer (the clause the 2026-10-10 repair closed). Only the pinned producer's exact shape is removed from speech, and only from speech: the whole warning sentence with the warning sign (with or without U+FE0F), a positive count of at most twenty digits, and a contiguous block of at least one two-space-indented bullet with text, on its own lines, LF or CRLF. Preceding and following prose is kept. Near misses stay spoken exactly as ordinary prose: a header with no bullet, an empty bullet, a count of 0, a count of twenty-one digits, no warning sign, a lone leading space, and ordinary talk about verification. The visible chat text is untouched. One limit is stated plainly: Nerva has no producer of this advisory (it appears nowhere else under agents/); the format is the donor turn finalizer's, so the strip matters for resumed foreign sessions and for model-echoed text, and this row claims nothing about a Nerva-side file-mutation verifier.

Wiring. TTSEngine.speak normalises before any backend, Fish included, and synthesises nothing when nothing is left (speak, agents/core/voice/tts.py:216, normalised at agents/core/voice/tts.py:232; speech_for, agents/core/voice/tts.py:211). speak_stream normalises the whole reply before splitting sentences (agents/core/voice/tts.py:315), so a code, reasoning or footer block spanning sentences is dropped whole, and each sentence is then normalised again without change. Through TTSEngine.speak this covers the wake-word VoicePipeline, VoiceChannel.send and chat voice notes: speakable() is for_speech plus its cap (agents/core/channels/spoken_reply.py:69). POST /tts answers 204 with X-Nerva-Speech: nothing_to_say instead of synthesising (agents/core/routers/voice.py:76), and /tts/stream frames carry the spoken sentences. The HUD twin is speechText (frontend/src/speech-text.ts:110), pinned by the same shared cases as the hub. SpeechStreamFilter (frontend/src/speech-text.ts:155) drops a fenced block, a reasoning block or a footer whose markers arrive split across token deltas, holding back only a bounded tail that could still become one, and flushes cleanly. frontend/src/voice.ts uses it on the live sentence stream (frontend/src/voice.ts:297) and normalises each sentence (frontend/src/voice.ts:318); a 204 is silence, never an empty clip or the fallback voice (frontend/src/voice.ts:330). reviews.summary: Conducta de transcriere validează, pregătește și livrează: acceptă octeți direct (`BytesIO`, fără fișier temporar, deci vorbirea nu ajunge pe disc), îi mărginește, trece rezultatul prin filtrul de halucinații și întoarce santinele oneste în loc de text inventat. Are acum doi consumatori — ruta HTTP a browserului și canalul Telegram — peste un singur motor local partajat, nu unul per apelant. Named speech progress adds explicit selected STT command identities through the common registry, pinned across async selection and executor handoff. Native mode choice, input handling and sentinel cleanup remain covered by inbound voice and STT regressions; broader provider coverage remains open.
reviews.remaining: Un singur backend. Hermes are opt (faster-whisper local, `local_command`, Groq, OpenAI, Mistral Voxtral cu diarizare și timestamp-uri pe cuvânt, xAI, ElevenLabs Scribe, DeepInfra) plus provideri pe comandă de shell, un ABC `TranscriptionProvider`, selecție explicită strictă cu auto-detect doar la o instalare neconfigurată vreodată, un plafon pe lungimea promptului Whisper, trunchierea liniștii înainte de upload ca să scadă octeții trimiși, un picker și `POST /api/audio/transcribe`. Nimic din astea nu e livrat. Nu din lene: clauza de guvernanță a rândului spune că orice STT în cloud trece prin `plugin.egress` și trimite vorbirea înregistrată a owner-ului în afara cutiei — e aceeași clasă de dezvăluire ca TTS-ul în cloud și trebuie clasificat, nu pus ca implicit de config. Cache-ul motorului stă tot în `routers/voice.py`, care e casa greșită pentru el; canalul îl importă în loc să-l dubleze, iar mutarea lui e o schimbare separată. NEVERIFICAT pe servicii reale: niciun model Whisper încărcat cu adevărat.

reviews.summary: Whisper nu tace când nu aude nimic — inventează. Pe liniște întoarce o propoziție fluentă din datele de antrenament: generice de subtitrare („Subtitles by the Amara.org community", „Subtitrarea: ..."), formule de încheiere („Thanks for watching!", „Mulțumesc pentru vizionare!"). Pentru o casetă de dictare e o enervare; aici e un control de siguranță, exact cum spune clauza de guvernanță a rândului: un mesaj vocal devine o tură *inbound*, o tură inbound poate cere lucruri, deci un transcript halucinat e o instrucțiune pe care n-a autorizat-o nimeni, intrată într-un sistem guvernat. `hallucination.py` o oprește. Designul e dictat de asimetria erorilor: a pierde un mesaj real e inacceptabil (cineva zice „mulțumesc" și dispare fără răspuns), a lăsa unul să treacă costă o tură ignorabilă. De aici două niveluri, nu o listă: frazele distinctive (`CANNED`) cad pe text; cele pe care oamenii chiar le spun (`AMBIGUOUS`) cad doar când durata *decodată* arată că înregistrarea era prea scurtă ca să le conțină — iar un apelant care nu știe durata le păstrează. Potrivirea e pe transcriptul întreg, niciodată pe substring; regula pentru generice cere marker ȘI vocabular exclusiv de generic, fiindcă prima variantă (doar markerul) mânca „am văzut pe amara.org un film bun". Filtrul rulează în `STTEngine.transcribe` și întoarce `[silence]` — santinela care exista deja și pe care fiecare apelant o tratează ca „nu s-a spus nimic" — deci ruta de dictare din browser o primește gratuit, nu doar calea nouă de pe Telegram. CORECTARE la auditul din 07.09: verdictul „missing" era pe jumătate greșit. A doua cerință a rândului — auto-stop pe liniște (VAD), ca utilizatorul să nu apese o tastă — EXISTĂ de mult în `frontend/src/voice.ts`: `recordUtterance` eșantionează RMS la 60 ms și oprește după `SILENCE_MS`, cu plafon dur și abandon când nimeni nu vorbește. Auditul a dat un `rg -i 'vad'` peste `frontend/src/` și a raportat „nimic relevant"; linia 111 spune „VAD" în litere. Ce lipsea cu adevărat era dovada: nimic nu o testa, fiindcă harness-ul comun folosește un MediaRecorder care se oprește singur și scurtcircuitează intervalul. `voice-vad.test.tsx` folosește unul care NU se oprește niciodată singur — dacă o tură se termină acolo, doar detectorul de liniște a putut-o termina — și acoperă fereastra de liniște, plafonul, abandonul și faptul că vorbirea continuă resetează ceasul. Named speech compatibility review: the Whisper hallucination filter and decoded-duration handling remain on the native transcribe path; named commands preserve the existing exact-sentinel behavior. Hallucination and speech selection regressions pass.

A turn can read a document directly through file_read instead of relying on pre-indexed memory. file_read in agents/core/file_tools.py is off unless JARVIS_FILE_TOOLS is set and bounded to JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS (no `..`, no symlink escape, secret-looking names refused, bytes capped by max_bytes). It returns a .pdf (pypdf) or .docx (python-docx) as extracted text when the input is admitted and parseable, names a missing parser (`parser_missing`) or a parse failure (`extraction_failed`) instead of returning replacement characters, and returns the bytes with raw=true. Since H661 it pages: `offset` starts the read at a byte, a read that stops early returns `next_offset`, a page is trimmed to end on a whole UTF-8 character (unless max_bytes is smaller than one), and an offset that is not an int in 0..MAX_OFFSET is refused as `bad_offset` rather than read from 0. A document pages through its extracted text: `offset` counts bytes of the extracted UTF-8 text, and `text_size` is reported beside the file's `size` (tests/test_spill_paging.py pages a .pdf's extracted text, with the extractor stubbed, back to its last byte). Local 2026-10-09 parser-backed file_read admission refuses an observed on-disk PDF/DOCX size above 50,000,000 bytes (decimal 50 MB) as document_too_large before parser discovery or extraction. Equality is admitted; raw=true and ordinary byte pages retain their output bounds. reviews.remaining: Every accepted part is missing: (1) an ACP session entry point (session/new, load, resume, fork) that accepts an mcpServers array; this depends on H542. (2) A session-scoped MCP registry layered over the global MCPManager, so that a server registered for one session is invisible to every other session and is torn down when the session ends. (3) Off-loop registration (asyncio.to_thread) with a bounded discovery join (default 1.5 s), so a dead server cannot block session creation. (5) Governance: session-supplied servers pass through the same outbound MCP authorization gate as configured servers (H554, still partial), and their trust tier is capped at no wider than a configured server's.

reviews.summary:
Every third-party MCP tool schema is now repaired once, when the tool is registered and before any provider sees it, and each tool gets a provider-legal, prefixed name. MCPTool keeps the server's raw schema for diagnostics only and stores `normalize_mcp_input_schema(input_schema)` as `input_schema` (agents/core/mcp/client.py:351-386). `_list_tools` builds every listed tool through that constructor and replaces the previous listing instead of appending to it (agents/core/mcp/client.py:604-630).

The normalizer is in agents/core/mcp/schema_normalize.py:323-360:
- It promotes a root `definitions` block to `$defs`. A name defined differently in both blocks gets a fresh key (agents/core/mcp/schema_normalize.py:330-346). Every `#/definitions/` ref is rewritten. Only the root meta-keyword is promoted, so a property that happens to be called `definitions` stays as it is.
- It collapses a Pydantic nullable `anyOf`/`oneOf` to its single non-null branch and drops `default: null` (agents/core/mcp/schema_normalize.py:127-167).
- It infers a missing `type`, gives every object an explicit `properties` map, and prunes `required` to names that are actually declared (agents/core/mcp/schema_normalize.py:288-320).
- It flattens a root `anyOf`/`oneOf`/`allOf`/`$ref`/`enum`/`not` so the root is always a plain object (agents/core/mcp/schema_normalize.py:356-357, agents/core/mcp/schema_normalize.py:554-589).

`mcp_provider_name` builds `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. Anything outside [A-Za-z0-9_] becomes `_`, and a name over 64 characters is cut and given a digest suffix (agents/core/mcp/schema_normalize.py:601-611).

`MCPManager._provider_index` renames pairs whose names collide after sanitizing and withholds any name that is still shared (agents/core/mcp/client.py:767-803). `model_tools` offers the normalized schema under the prefixed name. It withholds a tool whose name shadows a built-in or that the server's trust tier would refuse, and marks non-read-only tools as gated (agents/core/mcp/client.py:805-834). `_resolve` dispatches a prefixed name through the index, refuses a reserved built-in name, and returns `ambiguous_tool` instead of picking whichever server matched first (agents/core/mcp/client.py:852-889). The owner's include/exclude filters still match the original tool names (agents/core/mcp/client.py:632-639).

These rows reach the model:
- MCPModelBridge reserves the built-in names and takes the `model_tools()` rows (agents/core/mcp/model_bridge.py:83-91), then registers, re-registers or revokes them on the ToolRPC allowlist in `sync` (agents/core/mcp/model_bridge.py:113-147).
- AutonomyCoordinator wires the bridge into the agent tool loop as its per-turn `tool_sync` (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1770-1775).
- Gemini still applies its own projection on top of the repaired schema (agents/core/llm/tool_dialects.py:709-730).

Tests:
- `definitions` promotion: tests/test_mcp_schema_normalize.py:78-85.
- Nullable collapse: tests/test_mcp_schema_normalize.py:101-112.
- Anthropic, OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses and xAI all ship the repaired schema under a legal name (tests/test_mcp_schema_normalize.py:264-291).
- Name shape and truncation: tests/test_mcp_schema_normalize.py:344-357.
- Disambiguation after sanitizing: tests/test_mcp_schema_normalize.py:376-382.
- A model call is dispatched end to end and its result is fenced: tests/test_mcp_schema_normalize.py:475-492.
- Production coordinator wiring: tests/test_mcp_schema_normalize.py:1075-1121.
- Root combinators are flattened on all five paths: tests/test_mcp_schema_normalize.py:1238-1247.
- Name ambiguity is no longer first-wins: tests/test_mcp_hardening.py:41-74.

Re-run 2026-10-21 against the worktree: test_mcp_schema_normalize, test_mcp_hardening, test_mcp_tool_filters and test_cloud_tool_turns gave 171 passed. CJK search. Python's sqlite3 cannot register a C FTS5 tokenizer, so agents/core/memory/cjk_fts.py does the same segmentation in Python on both sides of the index. On the stored side, every CJK run is rewritten as its unigrams and overlapping bigrams under a stock unicode61 tokenizer (agents/core/memory/cjk_fts.py:93-110). On the query side, a 1-character run matches its unigram, and a longer run must contain all of its bigrams, each quoted so FTS5 syntax in user text is never parsed (agents/core/memory/cjk_fts.py:116-135).

MemoryStore keeps a memory_fts index:
- It is backfilled, and rebuilt when the segmenter version changes (agents/core/memory/store.py:342-396).
- A CJK query goes through MATCH and the candidates are re-checked for the exact substring, instead of the old LIKE scan (agents/core/memory/store.py:595-633).

Session transcripts get a per-turn FTS5 index in agents/core/memory/session_index.py:
- sync reindexes changed snapshots and drops orphans (agents/core/memory/session_index.py:438-486).
- An incremental save hook updates the index (agents/core/memory/session_index.py:489-520).
- A removal hook drops a deleted session's rows (agents/core/memory/session_index.py:523-555).
- Deleted text is erased through FTS5 secure-delete (agents/core/memory/session_index.py:184).

session_search answers from that index over the whole history (agents/core/memory/session_search.py:303-380).

The model can read a document mid-turn through a tool call. file_read in agents/core/file_tools.py is off unless JARVIS_FILE_TOOLS is set and bounded to JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS (no `..`, no symlink escape, secret-looking names refused, bytes capped by max_bytes). It returns a .pdf (pypdf) or .docx (python-docx) as extracted text when the input is admitted and parseable, names a missing parser (`parser_missing`) or a parse failure (`extraction_failed`) instead of returning replacement characters, and returns the bytes with raw=true. Since H661 it pages: `offset` starts the read at a byte, a read that stops early returns `next_offset`, a page is trimmed to end on a whole UTF-8 character (unless max_bytes is smaller than one), and an offset that is not an int in 0..MAX_OFFSET is refused as `bad_offset` rather than read from 0. A document pages through its extracted text: `offset` counts bytes of the extracted UTF-8 text, and `text_size` is reported beside the file's `size` (tests/test_spill_paging.py pages a .pdf's extracted text, with the extractor stubbed, back to its last byte). Local 2026-10-09 parser-backed file_read admission refuses an observed on-disk PDF/DOCX size above 50,000,000 bytes (decimal 50 MB) as document_too_large before parser discovery or extraction. Equality is admitted; raw=true and ordinary byte pages retain their output bounds. Local 2026-10-09 PDF text-layer coverage uses one shared parser traversal per request and adds coverage_warning beside unchanged extracted content when more than 20% of pages or at least ten pages yield no text. It reports exact page/gap totals, the first 16 maximal one-based ranges, and preceding source excerpts capped to 160 Unicode code points, with explicit omitted-range and excerpt-truncation fields. Blank/whitespace/None page text counts; reader/page failures retain extraction_failed without partial coverage. Existing normal-loop and nested ToolRPC scanners also scan the quoted metadata; this does not declare every file result untrusted.

reviews.summary: The owner's own chat attaches @file:path, @file:path#L10-40 and @file:"a b.md" for the turn. agents/core/context_refs.py holds the rules. expand (agents/core/context_refs.py:209) finds a reference that starts a word or follows an opening bracket, quote or backtick, and not one inside a word or a path (x@file:, a/@file:, @@file:) (_REF_RE, agents/core/context_refs.py:49); a double-quoted path may hold spaces, #L7 is one line and #L2-L3 a range, and trailing punctuation or a closing quote is not part of it. The routes keep the owner's message as typed: commands, skills, LLM-backend control, the router and memory see only it. The "--- Attached Context ---" section is bound to the turn (bind_attached, agents/core/context_refs.py:251; agents/web.py:1386 on /chat, and inside the stream task at agents/web.py:1484) and appended after the message only in the model prompt (attached_block, agents/core/context_refs.py:266; Orchestrator._build_agent_turn_text, agents/core/orchestrator.py:3990), so the file text is never stored as the owner's words, replayed in a later turn's history or embedded. Hermes keeps the expanded message in the user turn; Nerva shows the attachment to the model for the attaching (tainted) turn only. Each file's text is in a fence longer than any backtick run in it, so no line of it can close the fence (_fence, agents/core/context_refs.py:194), under a header that names the file as typed and the lines actually attached, `(line 7)` or `(lines 2-3)`, as attached file content, not instructions; injection patterns and a forged Attached Context marker are flagged in that header (`flagged: …`, _flags, agents/core/context_refs.py:180), not withheld. Each path is resolved through the same FileScope as file_read (_attach_one, agents/core/context_refs.py:133), so outside the file roots, .. traversal, a symlink escape and a secret-looking path such as .env are refused. A missing file, a directory, a binary file (a NUL in its first 8 KB), a bad line range, a range past the end, an unreadable file, an over-long name, a denied stat and an unknown ~user each become a one-line warning in the same section instead of failing the message. With JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS unset, the file tools' default root <data home>/workspace is used; only an unusable JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS makes the section say nothing was attached. The limits are 8 distinct references per message, 64 KB per reference and 128 KB in all, counted in bytes. A cut reference says so, and a repeated one is attached once. A line range skips the lines before it a 64K-character chunk at a time, up to 64M characters into the file (MAX_SCAN_CHARS; past it, the warning "line N is too far into the file"), keeps at most the byte budget and never reads a line whole (_read_lines, agents/core/context_refs.py:105); invalid UTF-8 is read with replacement characters. The expansion runs on /chat and /chat/stream (agents/web.py:1375, agents/web.py:1608), off the event loop, so both the HUD and nerva chat get it; the one message that skips it is a raw checkpoint command (`/rollback` or `/checkpoints` as the whole message, checkpoint_command_name), which never becomes a model turn, so nothing is read, bound or tainted for it. It never runs for a channel message, as Hermes' gateway does not expand either. A turn that attached anything is tainted: handle_input and handle_input_stream call _taint_attached_context (agents/core/orchestrator.py:396, :2372, :2593), which raises the turn's action origin to recall:untrusted. An action planned from attached content therefore escalates GRANT to QUEUE at the kernel, while an inbound turn keeps its more specific origin. complete (agents/core/context_refs.py:272) lists in-scope completions for what follows @file:, with directories ending in / and a path with a space quoted (a name no reference could name is left out). It shows dot files only when asked and never secret paths or links out of the roots, is bounded to 50 entries, and returns nothing for a prefix over 1,024 characters. GET /api/context-refs (agents/core/routers/commands.py:63, user-guarded, read-only) serves it and the reference types, and answers 503 file_roots_unusable when the roots cannot be used. The HUD composer (frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:229, :284, frontend/src/context-refs.tsx) offers the reference types while `@` or `@fi` is typed (Tab takes `@file:`), then the in-scope paths; a list is shown only for the text it was fetched for. tests/test_h579_context_refs.py (70 cases) covers the bounds, parsing, whole files, line ranges (single, L-form, past the end), every refusal and warning, a symlink, punctuation, word starts, dedupe, the byte cut, the shared budget, the reference limit, an unreadable file, invalid UTF-8, the roots, an explicit scope and the marker; completion (prefixes, dot files, secrets, roots, a long prefix, a file or missing folder, the bound); both routes, the completion route, the turn taint on both paths, and an inbound turn. The review round added attached text never read as the owner's command (a slash command, a skill, a backend switch) and never stored or carried to a later turn, through the real routes; a file that cannot close its fence; injection and a forged marker flagged; a range in one huge line bounded in memory and a range of many short lines linear; a range too far into a file; quoted paths and their completion; references after brackets and quotes and not inside words; the distinct-reference limit; the header's path and lines; paths the system refuses to look at; and the roots. frontend/src/test/context-refs.test.tsx has 6 cases. The row's 53 mutants predate this code; the review round's 34: 28 caught at once, five after five cases were added, and one equivalent (a kept read stops at the budget either way, since readline(0) answers ""). reviews.summary: Both intake halves of the accepted adaptation exist: the HUD composer and the terminal. useComposerImages (frontend/src/composer-images.tsx) takes image paste and drag-drop (frontend/src/composer-images.tsx:113-114) plus a file chooser, and accepts at most eight PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP images of up to 4 MiB each (frontend/src/composer-images.tsx:4-5); the shared InputBar wires paste and drop in (frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:247). Each draft is first reviewed against the server (prepare / selected-prepare with image digests, destination binding, data-policy and remote/training/cost acknowledgements), and App.submit sends an image draft to runVision (frontend/src/app.tsx:538, frontend/src/app.tsx:504). runVision picks one of three routes (frontend/src/vision-turn.ts:8): POST /api/vlm/composer/describe-prepared (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:499), POST /api/vlm/composer/chat-prepared for a selected main route (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:584) or POST /api/vlm/composer/selected-chat for a selected Ollama route (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:1092); the router is registered at agents/web.py:1743. All three routes check data-URI signatures and bound raster decoding (validate_raster, agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:61) and refuse a malformed body with its first reason instead of FastAPI's echoing 422 (_BoundedValidationRoute, agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:28). describe-prepared and chat-prepared also refuse a non-local destination without the owner's acknowledgement (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:718) and call VLMBackend.generate_vision_checked (agents/core/llm/vlm.py:460); selected-chat is local Ollama only, refusing any remote acknowledgement (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:985-987) and streaming /api/chat itself (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:1051); the H277 native adapters (OpenRouter, DeepInfra, Nous, Claude, Gemini, Responses, xAI), empty-reply recovery and reply normalization sit behind that guard. The terminal: `nerva chat --image PATH` (repeatable, up to eight) and `--clipboard-image` (agents/cli/nerva.py:641-644) turn the chat verb into a vision turn (dispatch at agents/cli/nerva.py:3981, _vision_turn at agents/cli/nerva.py:4352) that refuses --agent/--session/--reasoning and never posts to /chat. Files are typed by signature (_image_mime, agents/cli/nerva.py:4095; _read_image, agents/cli/nerva.py:4105); the clipboard is read by wl-paste, xclip, pngpaste/osascript or PowerShell (_clipboard_command, agents/cli/nerva.py:4180; _clipboard_image, agents/cli/nerva.py:4290) under a bounded, deadline-killed reader (_run_reader, agents/cli/nerva.py:4205), and an off-machine destination needs --remote-vision naming it (agents/cli/nerva.py:4441). Governance gap found on this re-read: the previous verdict rested on isolation (the vision answer a client-only transcript entry, ordinary turns posting only {message, agent} to /chat/stream). Since #1233/#1246 that holds only for describe-prepared and the terminal. The chat-prepared and selected-chat routes commit the image-derived question/answer pair into the durable conversation (orch.complete_selected_image_turn at agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:619-623 and agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:1065), and later text turns in that session post to /chat/stream with the session_id (frontend/src/app.tsx:431-432) and read that history. That history is now governed (H586 fix, 2026-10-12, c9f67240, 0631eeb9, 9a485766, 44b53b51, 0bc59ec5 and 307b33eb): every later chat turn runs _guard_media_history (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2459-2477) at both turn entries (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2557 and agents/core/orchestrator.py:2781), which reads the session history and, when any turn carries media, raises the turn's action origin through mark_turn_recall_tainted, so a side-effecting action derived from that history is queued for approval (ASK) instead of auto-granted, and an unreadable history marks the turn too; one-shot completions (process/process_detailed: the autonomy _llm executor, nightly reflection, the summarize route) run the same guard inside an action-origin binding scoped to the call (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2324-2326), so the mark never leaks to the caller; image turns are embedded with taint metadata (taint_source external:image, agents/core/memory/manager.py:342-345), so recalling the image reading in any later turn taints that turn through the existing RAG guard, and a session_search hit on a turn carrying media is flagged image_derived and taints the turn too (agents/core/memory/session_search.py:241-242 and agents/core/memory/session_search.py:410-414; the FTS5 index path keeps each turn's media flag, agents/core/memory/session_search.py:362-363, so an indexed hit is flagged the same way), and, since the model's call runs search_sessions in a worker thread whose own mark cannot reach the turn, the production mechanism is the registered tool handler declaring tainted on its result (agents/core/memory/session_search.py:451-453), which the agent tool loop reads as declared_taint and turns into the turn's mark; and a session holding a media turn is never promoted to durable memory, like a foreign import: _session_has_media (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2479-2484) stops the per-turn learning review (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4158 and agents/core/orchestrator.py:4315), the LivingMemory feed (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4396) /refine, which answers image_history_not_promotable (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4274-4275), and nightly reflection, whose KG/core-lesson consolidation skips a window holding a committed image turn (agents/core/autonomy/reflection.py:169-170); /undo, on the web (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2022-2024) and on channels (agents/core/channels/session_lifecycle.py:251-253), copies the kept turns with their media provenance, so an undo cannot launder the image reading into trusted history. tests/test_h586_image_history_taint.py pins the QUEUE verdict through the real kernel authorize (with a stubbed history and with a real MemoryManager after a committed image turn), the untouched text-only origin, the fail-safe mark, both entries' call order, a one-shot completion over image history running tainted without leaking the mark, the tainted embedding read back through rag_guard, and the refusals of review, LivingMemory and /refine, a web /undo keeping the provenance (guard, promotion gate and tainted re-embedding) and nightly reflection skipping the image window and a session_search hit on an image reading tainting the turn, directly and through ToolRPCServer.handle (13 cases, red before the change). Stated limits: the guard reads the held history, which keeps the newest 100 turns, so a media turn that has aged out of it no longer marks later turns (its embedding stays tainted), and with the opt-in memory.compression_summarizer the per-session summary cache can carry image-derived text past that window. reviews.summary:
Nerva reads a project's convention files into the turn, as Hermes reads its context files and subdirectory hints. agents/core/project_context.py walks from the nearest git root (never above the file root) down to the working directory (llm.project_dir when it is a folder inside the roots, H218; else the first JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS root; since #1233 a bound kanban workspace's cwd instead, read inside that workspace's scope), and reads AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules and .cursor/rules/*.mdc in each directory in that order (CONVENTION_NAMES, agents/core/project_context.py:59; candidates, agents/core/project_context.py:168). A directory that the model's file_read, file_list or file_search touches is noted for the session (note_tool_path, agents/core/project_context.py:408, bounded to 8 directories and 256 sessions, agents/core/project_context.py:70-71); its chain is read on every later turn, and the tool's own result carries the files the turn had not seen yet, marked tainted so the loop fences it (attach, agents/core/project_context.py:427; _with_project_context, agents/core/file_tools.py:780, called by the three read tools at agents/core/file_tools.py:992, agents/core/file_tools.py:1048 and agents/core/file_tools.py:1304). A script's file call (execute_code, no tool turn) brings none. A local terminal_run runs only after approval, by the worker from the queue: the queuing turn's session is recorded at intake (note_task, agents/core/project_context.py:439) — on ToolRPCServer.handle's generic gated path (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:894) and, since #1233 gave terminal_run its own trusted intake, in _terminal_intake (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1199, the call at agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1264; registered with gated_intake and gated_review at agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1291-1292) — and when the approved command ran locally, note_terminal (agents/core/project_context.py:451; keyed by the task id, not by a turn) notes its cwd for that session, so its next turn reads the chain (_rpc_terminal_run, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1196). Normally the command runs outside any turn and its result goes to the task row, not to the model; with Smart review or a live owner-once/consent reply, the registrar's gated_review (review_terminal_task, agents/core/autonomy/terminal_review.py:22-24) awaits the worker's own run of that task and hands the queue-verified result back to the model in the same turn — the directory is noted either way. A project SOUL.md, HEARTBEAT.md or IDENTITY.md is never read, not even through a symlink (HUB_FILES, agents/core/project_context.py:63; _admit, agents/core/project_context.py:183). Every file is resolved through FileScope (outside the roots, symlink escape and secret paths refused), must be a regular file (a FIFO is never opened), and is bounded to 20 KB, with 40 KB and 12 files a turn and 8 rules a directory (agents/core/project_context.py:65-68), shared by parallel tool calls under the turn's lock; a cut says how much was shown, a file past the budget is named, and files past a count cap are counted (load_file, agents/core/project_context.py:220; collect, agents/core/project_context.py:239; render, agents/core/project_context.py:274). Each file's text and name are scanned with detect_injection_normalized, plus Unicode TAG characters (decoded and scanned) and the fence's markers (_detect, agents/core/project_context.py:122). A flagged file becomes a [BLOCKED ...] line naming the rules (injection_flag_names) with none of its text, and a flagged name is withheld; other names have non-printable characters escaped and undecodable bytes replaced. The caveated block, which holds the files in the untrusted-data fence, sits after the core-memory block in _build_agent_turn_text (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4010-4016); _begin_project_context (agents/core/orchestrator.py:406-434) builds it off the event loop at turn start in both turn paths (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2574 and agents/core/orchestrator.py:2806) and marks the turn recall-tainted when any file was given, so an action planned from it escalates GRANT to QUEUE. A noted directory's files are in every later turn of the session, so those turns are tainted too: web_search, web_extract and memory writes refuse until the setting is off or the hub restarts. A guest's turn is given none of them. It is off with llm.project_context_files (agents/core/project_context.py:74) and in safe mode (layer project_context, agents/core/safe_mode.py:82, named on the HUD banner; enabled, agents/core/project_context.py:312). tests/test_h594_project_context.py: 66 cases. The original build's 51 mutants were all killed; the review round's fixes each come with a case that fails without them.

reviews.summary:
Each turn can now be saved in full and exported as training data. Saving is opt-in through NERVA_SAVE_TRAJECTORIES. Agent.generate_response opens a per-turn recorder (agents/core/agent.py:968). On the plain path it records the prompt with steering folded in (agents/core/agent.py:1090). The tool loop records the guided system prompt and the tool definitions it offered to the provider (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:766-767). After an H672 compaction fold it records the refreshed offer and the rebuilt system prompt again (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:866 and :861).

TrajectoryRecorder.note_tools keeps the union of every tool offered during the turn, capped at MAX_TOOLS (agents/core/trajectory.py:168-188). to_record writes one redacted, clipped record per turn that holds the system prompt, the tools, each step with its tool calls and results, the reply and the exit reason (agents/core/trajectory.py:229-259).

Trajectory files are owner-only. _append_private creates the directory as 0700 and opens the file with O_CREAT|O_NOFOLLOW|O_BINARY and mode 0600 before it writes any byte. It also narrows a file or directory that an earlier version left wider (agents/core/trajectory.py:368-391). A backend failure can come back through the tool loop as a plain ToolTurn whose exit is model_response. Such a turn is now recorded as degraded with completed=false, using the strict llm.base.is_backend_failure_reply signal. A real answer that opens with "[" stays completed (agents/core/agent.py:976-996; agents/core/llm/base.py:221).

There are two export shapes:
- to_sharegpt renders the Hermes ShareGPT shape: a system turn carrying a <tools> block, <tool_call> and <tool_response> JSON, a think block on every gpt turn, and the parallel results of one step joined into a single tool turn (agents/core/trajectory.py:479-503).
- to_messages renders OpenAI SFT rows with a tools column (agents/core/trajectory.py:506-529).

Both are served by the admin route GET /sessions/{id}/trajectories (agents/core/routers/sessions.py:222-249) and by `nerva sessions export ID --sharegpt` (agents/cli/nerva.py:3422-3445). So the export is no longer only the standalone training/prepare_data.py script, which writes one user/assistant pair per trace (training/prepare_data.py:21).

Tools self-register through ToolRPCServer.register_tool (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:477). Adding a tool is now covered by a public developer doc with a skill-vs-tool rule, the two places to change, and a checklist (docs/developer/adding-a-tool.md:12, :54, :140). How a turn executes, including the loop's invariants, is documented in docs/developer/agent-loop.md:11-160, and ARCHITECTURE.md points to both (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:975-978).

The CLI wrapper hooks are a recorded design difference, not a missing feature. docs/decisions/2026-10-21-no-cli-extension-hooks.md says nerva is a one-shot verb CLI over the HTTP API with no TUI to hook into. It maps each customisation Hermes users reach for to an existing governed place in Nerva, and states when to revisit the decision.

reviews.summary:
The three native external intakes reserve an authenticated caller scope before enqueue or execution: owner action intake, webhook ID and verified A2A peer. agents/core/idempotency.py:147 uses SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE with a unique (scope,key), a length-framed method/path/body fingerprint and bounded public references, never bodies or credentials. The visible-ASCII key grammar, durable file-store property, restart/racing-worker behavior, conflict/in-progress/replay handling, attempt fencing, bounded expiry and webhook heartbeat remain implemented. Actions reserve before q.request (agents/core/routers/actions.py:76); A2A reserves after peer verification and webhooks after token/signature and enabled checks. Ninety focused regressions passed. These are native single-owner/webhook/peer scopes, not a claim that Hermes RoomLink exists. Reservations expire after 24 hours and stale pending attempts after 600 seconds; outcome-write exhaustion can allow a later retry to run again. This is bounded retry deduplication, not an unconditional exactly-once distributed transaction. The existing target-specific failed-turn recognition limitation is unchanged.

reviews.summary:
Final review at HEAD 57ed6db. The gap in the ledger entry was "no ordered multi-skill operations batch with all-or-nothing rollback, nor a teaching payload on the failing op". That gap is closed on this branch.

What is in the code now:
- normalize() takes one ordered operations array. Each operation names its own skill and uses one of create, patch, write_file, remove_file or delete (agents/core/skills/batch.py:50, agents/core/skills/batch.py:167-222).
- A create that comes after another operation on the same skill is refused with skill_batch_create_not_first (agents/core/skills/batch.py:208-213).
- A delete in a batch of more than one operation is refused with skill_batch_delete_not_alone (agents/core/skills/batch.py:214-218).
- run_batch applies every operation to staging copies first and touches nothing live until every operation and final check passes (agents/core/skills/batch.py:693-742). It then swaps the live folders one at a time. If the swap or the signature/approval renewal fails, it reverses every folder already swapped and reports skill_batch_apply_failed with rolled_back (agents/core/skills/batch.py:756-782). Replaced folders are archived (agents/core/skills/batch.py:783-793).
- A failing operation returns a teaching payload: failed_op, hints and file_preview (agents/core/skills/batch.py:90-100). A patch whose old_string does not match also gets the closest line and a preview of the file at that point (agents/core/skills/batch.py:460-475).
- Owner path: POST /api/skills/batch, admin only, with dry_run (agents/core/routers/skills.py:1027).
- Model path: skill_propose {operations} does a dry run and records the batch with one approval card for the whole set (agents/core/skills/tools.py:941-1022, agents/core/skills/batch.py:860-876).
- Only the bound card's own status in the queue applies the batch, and it applies against the skill fingerprints that were checked (agents/core/skills/batch.py:889-917, agents/core/routers/actions.py:147-160). The approval judge never scores a batch card (agents/core/autonomy/approval_judge.py:644-646). This meets the governance requirement of one approval, not N.

Review history, in brief:
- Two adversarial skeptics passed the row.
- Round 4 fixed a binary-diff hole. _diffs now decodes the old and new bytes separately (agents/core/skills/batch.py:529, agents/core/skills/batch.py:555-560). Text that replaces a binary file is shown whole with every line marked as added (agents/core/skills/batch.py:534-538). Non-UTF-8 added bytes are flagged added_unreadable (agents/core/skills/batch.py:544-546), and skill_propose refuses those with skill_batch_unreviewable (agents/core/skills/tools.py:993-1000).
- The skeptic's last finding was a removed binary file shown as "binary file replaced by text". It was fixed with the red-first test tests/test_skill_batch.py:590, so it now reads "(binary)".
- The frontend now builds the diff only when the owner opens the fold (frontend/src/panels/skill-batches.tsx:73, frontend/src/panels/skill-batches.tsx:81, frontend/src/panels/skill-batches.tsx:85).

Honest limits:
- The model path cannot propose a change that adds non-text bytes. The owner route can.
- Rollback during the swap is best effort. If a folder cannot be renamed back, it is reported as not_rolled_back and its old copy is kept in staging for the owner, not hidden.
