reviews.summary:
The shared identity band exists. agents/_identity/IDENTITY.md is one behaviour contract: the reply-sizing rule (match length to the weight of the ask), earned depth, the named prohibitions (no filler, no restating the request, no re-summarizing, no narrating visible tool calls), the anti-sycophancy line ('agree because it is right, not because the owner said it') and 'say when you do not know'. Its reply rules govern the agent's own replies to the owner: text drafted in someone else's voice (an email, a post, a message written as the owner) keeps that voice, greetings and sign-offs included, and a persona's warmth or curiosity lives inside the answer (review-H670 m-5); its honesty rules hold for everything an agent writes, drafted text included (review-H670b m-1). Its leading maintainer note (stripped before the model sees it, _strip_maintainer_note, agents/core/agent.py:453) says never to add 'be targeted and efficient in your exploration', and why. The repo-root SOUL.md mirrors the text, so agents working on the repo read the contract the product ships; a test keeps the two equal. identity_path (agents/core/agent.py:438) resolves it as soul_path_for does a persona: the data home's souls/IDENTITY.local.md, then a gitignored agents/_identity/IDENTITY.local.md, then the shipped file. read_identity (agents/core/agent.py:481) runs it through the same H387 helpers as a SOUL (the injection scan on the uncapped body, then the cap), announces a flagged or truncated contract (its blocked and quarantined stubs name the contract, not a persona), caps it at its own 4,000 characters (IDENTITY_MAX_CHARS, never above the persona's cap, so the two bands stay within the persona cap plus 4,000), and reads it once per settled file signature for the whole process. An override that cannot be read (not UTF-8, a directory, no permission) is reported at ERROR and the shipped contract used instead, cached against the shipped file's signature so an edit of it is seen; a contract that cannot be located or read at all leaves the agent without it; none of these stops an agent from being built. Agent.system_prompt (agents/core/agent.py:572) is the contract first, then the machine context when there is any (hint_block, agents/core/environment_hint.py:85: what Nerva detected about the host from H283 host_identity under its own heading, then the operator's JARVIS_ENVIRONMENT_HINT under its own heading; each is empty when nothing was detected or set), then the agent's persona (any part may be empty; an agent without a SOUL still gets the contract). Every place a system prompt is built uses it: Agent.process (agents/core/agent.py:1123) and the synthesis path in agent.py, and the orchestrator's two sites (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2931, agents/core/orchestrator.py:4988) through _system_prompt_of (agents/core/orchestrator.py:530). At a compaction boundary refresh_soul (agents/core/agent.py:741) re-reads the contract as it re-reads the persona (_refresh_identity, agents/core/agent.py:610): a few stats when unchanged; when the file that resolves is absent, vanishes before the read or cannot be read, the contract in force is kept, reported at the boundary as failed-open and warned once per episode (an override absent for an instant resolves to the shipped file for that boundary, as a persona's does); and a moved contract reported as rebuilt, so an edit reaches running agents without a restart. The contract in force at start is committed to the prompt VC (SoulVersionStore) as _identity (_record_identity_version, agents/core/orchestrator.py:512), a no-op when unchanged or empty, so its history is recorded and diffable through /api/admin/prompts/_identity/... beside the personas; what is served is the file (a rollback in the VC does not change it), and an edit picked up at a boundary is recorded at the next start. The prompt-size report counts it as a shared component every call pays (identity_component, agents/core/prompt_size.py:136), followed by the host-detected (agents/core/prompt_size.py:149) and environment-hint (agents/core/prompt_size.py:158) components, and the packaged build ships it through its agents/*/*.md glob (overrides, *.local.md, never ship). IDENTITY.md and its .local overlay are in the H506 instruction-file class (INSTRUCTION_BASE_NAMES, agents/core/file_tools.py:368), so a file write to them asks as an instruction file; a test derives the class from every name the contract's and a persona's loaders can resolve. The data home's README lists souls/IDENTITY.local.md. Persona SOULs and Persona.prompt_block (agents/core/cognition/persona.py:142) stay the character layer on top. tests/test_identity_contract.py (18 cases) covers every rule's presence, the banned line's absence and the kept warning, the mirror, the scan verdict, every active agent's system prompt starting with the contract (and, with the host pinned to 'nothing detected' by an autouse fixture and no operator hint, exactly contract then persona), an agent without a persona, the orchestrator's helper and all four sites, both overrides and their order, the scan and the cap on an override, an edit reaching a running agent at the boundary, the one-stat unchanged path, a failed re-read keeping the last-good contract, the version record (once, and a failing store never stopping a start) and one read shared across agents; tests/test_h670b_identity_review.py (21 cases) covers the first review: the instruction-file class, a contract absent or vanishing at a boundary, a non-UTF-8 or unreadable override, the contract's own cap, no empty version, the start-time record, the contract's scope, a mid-file comment, the prompt-size component, the ERROR on a flagged contract, the stubs' wording and CHT-117; tests/test_h670c_identity_review.py (14 cases) covers the second review: honesty unscoped, a shipped contract that stops being UTF-8, a vanish before the real read, the hub's start recording the contract, one warning per episode and a second one, a reader that raises, the fallback following a shipped edit, a directory override, a permission error at load and at a boundary, the fallback rules once when both bands are blocked, and the docs. The first review (one major: the contract was outside the instruction-file class; seven minors: a missing contract emptied at a boundary, a non-UTF-8 override stopped every agent, the two bands exceeded the cap, the VC's rollback and A/B claim, the contract's unscoped rules against drafting personas and trait directives, six untested survivors, CHT-117 naming a retired agent; six nits) is answered; its six real survivors are pinned. The feature's 17 mutants were caught but one equivalent; the first review round's 15 were caught, one only against a stand-in (the vanish case, now driven through the real read). The second review (no major; three minors: the scope lifted the honesty rules from drafted text, a shipped contract that stopped being UTF-8 emptied the contract at a boundary, three real survivors; eight nits) is answered; its 31 mutants' three real survivors are pinned, and this round's 10 were all caught, two after their cases were added (a reader that raises, a second warning episode). Known limits: the prompt-size report measures the shipped contract, not an override in force (as it measures shipped personas); PromptRefresh.text is still the persona alone; the contract's scan verdict is reported only in the log (a persona's also reaches GET /api/agents/{id}/soul); the data home's README is written once, so an existing install does not get its new row. Parent AST comparison and re-read source/citations confirm unchanged mechanisms; the cited backend test modules pass in the frozen full run. Existing frontend evidence remains tied to unchanged source. No new capability or mutation claim is added. Shared identity text, loader, prompt composition and cited identity behavior are unchanged; no status promotion.

Each ToolRPC call rechecks its selected registered name/gated metadata after the independent job scope and registration checks, synchronously before preflight, gated approval intake or handler admission. Revocation during the tool_started await is therefore refused locally even without a context fold. Resolver failure or a missing selected tool denies with the existing tool_not_allowed reason. The check uses inherited principal/origin/job context and does not rebuild provider schemas, change the stable gate/taint views or write H661 turn-offer notes. A production-wiring regression checks the unchanged offer sentinel inside the handler child; a gated regression records no preflight, intake, pending approval or handler effects. Existing stale source pins are deliberately not globally restamped. The historical fold/persona assessment below keeps its original scope. Both refreshes from Hermes's row exist (`agents/core/session_refresh.py`, the parked mechanism commit 89b53e85 cherry-picked unchanged; its module docstring has since gained a note on where each half is wired) and are wired at Nerva's two compaction boundaries, each failing in its own direction. **Nerva is turn-based, so most of the row was already true between turns and is pinned as such**: `Orchestrator._prompt_context` reads the skills catalog per turn, the plugin block is rendered per turn, and `AgentToolRuntime._run_loop` resolves ToolRPC → capability registry → tool profile at the top of every run (`test_between_turns_the_offer_was_already_live`). Two things were not live. **(1) The system prompt.** `Agent._load_soul` ran once in `__init__` and `orchestrator.py` sent `agent.soul["content"]` for the life of the process, so a persona edited or quarantined mid-session needed a restart. `Agent._read_soul` is the one builder (same file resolution, same H387 scan, same cap) behind both `_load_soul` and `Agent.refresh_soul`, and `_refresh_souls_at_boundary` (orchestrator.py, a module function so the bare-stub tests of that path keep working) calls it for every agent from `_history_for_prompt`'s `publish()` — after the clock CAS, never before it, and pinned as such: a refused `commit_clock` migrates nothing, an accepted one is followed by the refresh in that order. In front of the builder sits an `os.stat` probe (`_soul_signature`: resolved path, inode, size, mtime, ctime and the body cap), because once a session is over budget the conversation-level commit happens on **every** turn — `ContextCompressor.compact()` recomputes from the raw turns each call — and the walk is process-wide: an unchanged persona costs one stat, and only a file whose kernel signature moved reaches the builder (measured over the 18 shipped SOULs, 76 KB: 59.0 ms → 0.55 ms per boundary, 18 → 0 reads and scans). A file written within the last two seconds has no trusted signature (git's racy rule: a same-size edit in the same timestamp tick would be invisible to a stat) and is read and compared by bytes until it ages. Past the probe the keep path is byte equality of the builder's whole output — body *and* front-matter, so a tier or trait edit with the same body is adopted and the HUD's `soul["meta"]` follows — never a dirty flag; a builder that throws keeps the last-good bytes (fails OPEN); a file absent for the instant of an editor's save-by-rename keeps them with a plain warning, and an agent that had no persona and still has none is unchanged, not failed. A scan verdict is not a failure — a persona that is now mostly injection is dropped exactly as a restart would drop it — and it is announced exactly as a restart announces it: `_announce_soul_verdict` is the one place both moments log, so a quarantine at the boundary is the H387 ERROR line, not an INFO line. **(2) The tool set inside one turn.** A loop of up to `llm.tool_loop_max_iterations` model turns kept the list it resolved at the top. `_run_loop` treats a committed fold (`_compact_context` grew `compacted`) as the boundary and re-resolves through `_resolve_offer` (the same three steps, minus the turn-start side effects) via `session_refresh.refresh_tools`, which fails CLOSED: a resolver that raises withdraws every tool, an empty resolution is a revocation, and either ends the loop with `_TOOLS_WITHDRAWN_REPLY` after a `tool_loop_withdrawn` event rather than asking a provider a turn on a stale or empty list. The offer and the executor move together (`_specs_for` rebuilds the specs, the gate map the executor checks `offered` against, and the untrusted set) — pinned by a tool withdrawn through the *profile* while still registered in ToolRPC, the one shape that can tell the executor's `tool_not_allowed` from the RPC's own (keeping the stale gate map runs the handler, and that test goes red). Between folds the registry is not consulted at all, so the set stays stable between two folds; Nerva's fold happens inside one user turn, so Hermes's "mid-turn tool sets stay stable" reads here as *between folds*. reviews.remaining: **The boundaries are opt-in, so on a shipped default nothing migrates**: the conversation-level commit exists only with `memory.context_compression` on (default off) and the in-turn fold only with `llm.tool_loop_enabled` on (default off) — a default install still needs a restart for a persona edit, exactly as before. **Execution-admission scope:** production coordinator-wired agent-loop calls now recheck live profile authorization before preflight/intake, including between folds. This does not cancel an already-running tool or rewrite queued approvals; direct/script RPC and approved task execution retain their existing contracts. A standalone runtime wired only with `tool_profile` must explicitly supply the separate `execution_profile` hook to gain this check. The model's offered schemas and gate/taint views still refresh only at their existing boundaries. **The persona migration is process-wide**: `orchestrator.agents` is every agent and `agent.soul` is the one dict every session's system prompt reads, so the session that commits migrates the persona for all sessions (the boundary log line says so); refreshing only the routed agents would need the route at `_history_for_prompt`, which it does not have. **On the staged shared-route path the turn's budget is computed against the persona in force before the commit** (`_shared_route_plan` → `build()` measures `agent.soul` while planning; the refresh runs in `accept()` → `publish()`), so a persona that grew is sent that turn with a budget computed for the old size — bounded by `_soul_max_chars`, self-correcting next turn; the H363 cached prefix and the H673 usage anchor under-count for one turn after a rebuild the same way. The probe trusts the kernel's signature; what the builder reads outside the file (the scan patterns) is code and needs a restart. The prompt half covers the SOUL only: Nerva's plugin and skills sections live in the user prompt and were already per-turn, so there is no plugin section in the system prompt to fail open — the fail-open is exercised on the SOUL builder. The in-turn boundary does not rebuild `messages[0]`: a persona change reaches the *next* turn, not the loop in flight. "A newly configured MCP server appears without a restart" now holds at the turn boundary for every tool the MCP manager currently lists: the production coordinator wires `MCPModelBridge.sync` as the runtime's `tool_sync` (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1766-1775), and `_run_turn` awaits it before resolving the offer at the top of every turn (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:720-722), bounded to 5 s and keeping the registered offer if it fails (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1507-1516); the sync registers, re-registers or revokes the bridge's tools on the ToolRPC allowlist (agents/core/mcp/model_bridge.py:113-147). The in-turn fold does not run that sync, so an MCP tool added or removed mid-loop reaches the offer on the next turn, not at the fold; whether the MCP manager itself connects a newly configured server without a restart was not verified by this row. The lineage row stays at `nerva.context-compaction.v1`; the boundary note is a log line plus the runtime event, not a field on the row. `refresh_tools` compares names, so a tool whose schema changed under the same name is adopted only because the fresh list is taken whenever the set moved, never on its own. The stale comment at `agents/core/file_tools.py` saying `_load_soul` runs no injection scan predates H387 and is left for a hygiene commit (it would drift five unrelated rows). Nine ledger rows cite `agent.py`, `agent_runtime.py` or `orchestrator.py` and were drifted by this branch (and by #1188 on main: its registry path in `orchestrator.py`, and the pairing kwarg, refusal branch and lifespan hand-over in `telegram.py` and `web.py`, which H146, H449, H364 and H671 also cite and were read against — the pairing store is not their subject); each was re-read against the diff on its cited paths before its hashes moved. Six keep their text and take fresh stamps — H146, H298, H363, H364, H449, H679: the in-turn re-resolution runs through `_profiled`, which still applies the job toolset on both sides of the profile, and the result-spill, cache, reasoning and job-pin mechanism those rows cite is untouched. reviews.summary:
A compaction summary no longer holds the owner's turn past a short bound, and a silent summarizer is cut. Hermes keeps two clocks: how long the summary may make the user wait, and how long the summarizer may go quiet. Nerva awaited the strict-local summarizer inline with neither. Its only limit was the httpx read timeout (120 s for Ollama), a total-duration wait on a non-streaming call, and nothing told the owner. (1) Bounded hold. ContextCompressor takes a gate (agents/core/context_compressor.py:327, used at :605). The orchestrator builds it per turn (_summary_gate, agents/core/orchestrator.py:4686, passed at :4514) around SummaryHold (agents/core/compaction_hold.py:149). SummaryHold.wait (:159) waits at most memory.compression_max_turn_hold_seconds for the LLM summary (settings_db.py:315; default 10 s, 0 = never wait, clamped 0..120 by hold_seconds, compaction_hold.py:64). One summary per session is written at a time: a turn that finds one still in flight neither waits on it again nor starts a second. Past the hold the turn goes on without the summary, and compress marks the result summary_deferred (context_compressor.py:630). compact (:422) then sends the turns verbatim, their old images dropped, when they still fit the window under the owner's memory.compression_max_tokens; otherwise it sends the deterministic digest. The summary keeps being written. When it lands it seeds this session's iterative-merge prior (_ctx_summary_cache), but only if no newer turn has replaced the prior this turn started from, and never through the compaction-clock CAS: publish commits only what the prompt was built from, and never writes the digest over the pending summary (orchestrator.py:4919). A turn cancelled while it waits (Stop, a client gone) still leaves its summary for the next turn. A summary that fails later seeds nothing and is logged by name. aclose stops what is still being written within the task budget (orchestrator.py:5664; SummaryHold.aclose, compaction_hold.py:198). (2) The owner is told. record_turn_notice (agents/core/turn_notices.py:35; a per-turn sink collected like turn_approvals, one notice per code) carries DEFERRED_NOTICE (compaction_hold.py:39) out as notices on /chat (ChatResponse.notices, agents/web.py:1193, TurnNotice :1118) and on every /chat/stream end event, the failed one included (:1490, :1497). The HUD shows each notice as a system line under the reply (frontend/src/turn-notices.ts, app.tsx:469). The hub log says the summary was deferred and, later, that it landed. (3) Inactivity deadline. The summarizer now streams (stream_summary, compaction_hold.py:89, called at agents/core/llm/auxiliary_text.py:186). It is cut after memory.compression_summary_idle_seconds with nothing received (settings_db.py:316; default 60 s, up to 600, no "off": idle_seconds, compaction_hold.py:72). Any chunk counts as life: a visible token, and a reasoning chunk that shows no text, through the new on_activity callback on the Ollama and LM Studio streams (agents/core/llm/base.py:797, :1022). A slow stream that keeps talking is never cut. A cut stream is cancelled and given CLOSE_GRACE (1 s) to close its HTTP response. A backend with no stream is awaited whole. A degraded reply ("⚠️ …", "[backend error …]") or an empty one is now a failure, and so the digest is used. Before, the non-streaming generate could hand an error text over as the summary. Tests: tests/test_h674_compaction_hold.py (52) covers both settings, the idle deadline (silent, slow-but-talking, token-only, thinking, degraded, no stream), the hold (in time, at the bound, single flight, zero, cancelled wait, late failure, failure within the hold, aclose), the compressor's deferral (digest, verbatim when it fits, owner's budget, covered with a prior), and the orchestrator: the turn going on at the hold, the late summary seeding the next turn, a newer prior never overwritten, no clock commit for the deferred summary, the idle setting reaching the summarizer, aclose. It also covers the notice on /chat and every stream end event, the collector unbound after /chat, and on_activity on both local streams. frontend src/test/turn-notices.test.ts covers the HUD. 72 mutants: 70 caught after nine survivors got cases. Two were equivalent. m23 (busy ignoring done()) is equivalent because the done callback always pops the flight first. The other was a redundant typeof check in the HUD helper, which was removed. The phase-2, H20.3 and compaction-policy suites pass unchanged. The AUD-7 and H677 end-event and reply pins gain the notices key. reviews.summary: Re-read on main at 55d625f4. Telegram has the partial-then-edit mechanism: TelegramDraft (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:125) sends the first token as a message, then edits it in place through _edit_message (telegram.py:599) at most once per STREAM_EDIT_INTERVAL (telegram.py:61, 1.2 s) and only when the visible text changed; finish() (telegram.py:198) settles the final text in the streamed message, sends overflow as new messages, retries markup Telegram rejects as plain text and falls back to a fresh send when the final edit fails. The adapter declares supports_edit=True (telegram.py:241) and exposes begin_stream (telegram.py:615). The real caller is Orchestrator._begin_channel_draft (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2143), invoked for every non-observed channel turn (orchestrator.py:1696): it opens a draft only when the adapter has begin_stream, its descriptor says supports_edit, the owner setting channels.streaming_replies is on (orchestrator.py:2151) and the delivery router would send to this source; the turn then runs through handle_input_stream with an on_token callback that forwards each token to draft.push (orchestrator.py:2062-2065) and draft.finish (orchestrator.py:1721) replaces the whole-reply send. The conservative default is declarative rather than a stub: ChannelDescriptor.supports_edit defaults to False (agents/core/channels/descriptor.py:36), so an adapter that declares nothing gets the whole reply. Slack and Discord (and now ntfy) are deliberately excluded from streaming (orchestrator.py:2148) because their replies go through the governed channel.reply approval queue (_queue_workspace_reply, orchestrator.py:1730-1731); test_edit_support_alone_cannot_publish_unapproved_tokens pins that an editable transport alone cannot publish tokens before that approval. Final review at HEAD 57ed6db, branch codex/hermes-progress-20261010. The row is now equivalent to Hermes config-literal-dots for the CLI, which is the only place Nerva addresses a setting by a dotted name. The earlier assessment left three gaps: a json value could only be replaced whole, there was no unset, and no test pinned a dotted key name. All three are closed on this branch.

What the code does now:
- Name grammar. agents/core/settings_path.py:57-105 parses a setting name into segments. A backslash-escaped dot (`\.`) or a double-quoted segment counts as one key and is never split (settings_path.py:66-99).
- Greedy matching. Runs of plain segments are matched greedily against the keys that already exist at that level, longest first (settings_path.py:118-138). When more than one reading exists, the name is refused as ambiguous and the error spells out the quoted form of each reading (settings_path.py:133-137).
- Category and key. resolve_setting takes the first segment as the category and matches the key greedily, so a declared key may itself contain dots (settings_path.py:141-156).
- Reading, writing and removing inside a value. get_in, set_in and unset_in walk a json value with the same greedy step (settings_path.py:159-257). A list index must be ASCII digits (settings_path.py:36 and :171).
- Phantom-sibling refusal. set_in refuses to create a plain key `ui` beside an existing dotted key `ui.theme`, which Hermes calls _phantom_sibling (settings_path.py:193-202, called at :225). Quoting or escaping the segment says the new key is wanted on purpose.
- CLI wiring. agents/cli/nerva.py:1187-1206 resolves names for config get, set and unset; the unset verb is declared at agents/cli/nerva.py:261-264. `config get` also matches stored rows that nothing declares (nerva.py:1195-1199, passed stored=True at :1261). `set` and `unset` accept declared settings only (nerva.py:1280-1284).
- Writes below a key. A path below a key goes through set_in or unset_in (nerva.py:1293-1305). The whole new value then passes the same validation, retention, model-selection guards and route-only refusals as any other write (nerva.py:1286-1317, the retention approval, selection guards and store write in _write_setting, nerva.py:1361-1400, which `config edit` shares).
- Unset of a whole setting puts back its declared value (nerva.py:1302-1303).
- An appearance write moves the device-sync revision (_stamped, nerva.py:1353-1358).
- Docs. docs/INSTALL.md:134-135 shows the path, escape and quote spellings and `config unset`.

Tests in tests/test_h688_config_paths.py:
- greedy, escaped and quoted resolution of a dotted declared key (:50)
- get, set and unset of a dotted key inside a value, behaving the same across all three (:68)
- phantom-intermediate refusal (:82)
- ambiguous and missing paths failing loudly (:94)
- CLI round trip inside a json setting, including the phantom refusal and unset (:136)
- whole-setting unset (:168)
- a declared key whose name contains a dot, addressed plainly, escaped and quoted (:188)
- an undeclared stored row is readable but not writable (:230)
- non-ASCII digits are refused as list indexes (:261)
- the appearance revision moves on a CLI write (:278)

That review raised three findings: `config get` had lost undeclared rows, non-ASCII digits were accepted as list indexes, and the docs example wrote a key nothing reads. r2 (commit bf34ed1) fixed all three with regression tests that failed before the fix. The row then passed two adversarial skeptics and was cherry-picked onto HEAD.

Every hub on an install now obeys one kill switch, and no other code path bypasses it. This closes the gap where a hub running under $JARVIS_PROFILE ignored the default hub's ESTOP.

**The switch.** `paths.install_root()` (agents/core/paths.py:177-191) returns the install's unprofiled root and ignores $JARVIS_PROFILE. `profiles_root()` (agents/core/paths.py:195-198) names the `<install root>-profiles` directory. `data_root()` builds each profile's root under it (agents/core/paths.py:201-207). The sentinel is `install_root()/ESTOP` (agents/core/estop.py:55-57), so `engage()` (agents/core/estop.py:120) writes the same file from any scope. `check_paused()` (agents/core/estop.py:181) is the gate used by the heartbeat (agents/core/heartbeat.py:489), the autonomy tick (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:576) and the jobs runner (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1755). It still fails safe: an OSError reports engaged (agents/core/estop.py:97-117).

**Legacy sentinels are one switch, not a hidden second one.**
- `_legacy_sentinels()` (agents/core/estop.py:60) lists `<install root>-profiles/*/ESTOP`.
- `_fold_legacy()` (agents/core/estop.py:75-94) moves the first one onto the canonical sentinel with `os.replace`, which keeps its body, and deletes the rest. A sentinel it cannot move stays where it is and still counts as engaged.
- `is_engaged()` (agents/core/estop.py:97) and `get_state()` (agents/core/estop.py:155) both see legacy sentinels.
- `disengage()` (agents/core/estop.py:137-152) removes the canonical sentinel and every legacy one.

**Forget and backup leave the shared switch alone.**
- ESTOP is on `data_purge.KEEP_FILES` (agents/core/data_purge.py:86).
- `create_backup` leaves the root's ESTOP out of the archive (agents/core/backup.py:568-572; import at agents/core/backup.py:92).

**Tests** (tests/test_estop.py):
- The `estop_home` fixture patches only `install_root` (:26).
- Profile tests: :131, :142, :147 and :159.
- A legacy sentinel is folded into the canonical one (:183), is visible from the default hub and lifted by a resume there (:200), and a resume lifts several legacy sentinels at once (:217).
- A forget keeps ESTOP (:230), and a backup never carries it (:247).
- An unpatched integration test (:272) runs a real profiled `HeartbeatScheduler` and the ops estop state/resume routes.

**Red first and review fixes.** With the new tests on the old code, 5 failed and 13 passed. The adversarial review led to three fixes: forget and backup keep ESTOP, legacy sentinels fold into the one switch, and the integration test was added. Both skeptics passed.

reviews.summary:
Nerva already has the shape of a small bundle plus a large on-demand catalog. 12 first-party skills ship under skills/ (for example skills/brief/SKILL.md). They are rendered into the prompt's skills block: since H326 the category-grouped index from SkillLoader.prompt_index (agents/core/agent.py:862-864, agents/core/skills/loader.py:1780), cached in an in-process LRU and a manifest-validated disk snapshot, with the flat 'Available skills' rows only as the fallback (agents/core/agent.py:865-867); skills_index_component measures either form (agents/core/prompt_size.py:166). Hermes skills are not bundled; they are imported one at a time on request. POST /skills/import (agents/core/routers/skills.py:451) is user-guarded and DEV_MODE-gated, and frontend/src/panels/skills-import.tsx drives it. It calls SkillImporter.import_from_hermes (agents/core/skills/importer.py:206). That import checks an exact, digest-verified pin allowlist and fails before any network call (tests/test_hermes_import.py). The pin still predates the upstream reorganisation. agents/core/skills/hermes_pin_v1.json:4 and agents/core/skills/importer.py:50 are v2026.8.27 with 78 entries (tests/test_hermes_import.py:232). So the catalog still lists github-auth, github-code-review, github-issue-to-pr, github-issues, github-pr-workflow, github-repo-management, plan, session-librarian and blogwatcher. It has neither the consolidated github skill nor grill-me or the other new optional skills. _safe_pin_path requires every pinned path to start with skills/ (agents/core/skills/importer.py:113), so upstream's optional-skills/ tree cannot be pinned at all. Each pin entry digests only one SKILL.md, so reference files cannot be imported.

Batch-03 collateral review (2026-10-10): the changed evidence paths were compared with their previously current preimages. H329 adds strict global/channel owner switches and exact human-approved re-enable; H299/H397 add result-aware default-advisory stalls. This review preserves the existing contract verdict and remaining limits; unrelated stale pins remain unchanged. Current verification and limits are recorded in docs/plans/2026-10-10-hermes-closure-03.md.
